Hollow Snow Vault - Ice Ribs.description: Light reveals pressure cracks along the ribs. Careful support or a different route can avoid breaking the roof.

Hollow Snow Vault - Drowned Casing.description: A partly submerged instrument case lies within the elemental’s cold boundary. Reading, extraction and demolition have different costs and evidence outcomes.

Hollow Snow Vault - Vent Shelf.description: Dry air channels lead to a raised shelf. Bellows Mites gather here; blocking their only outlet increases pressure rather than simply removing a hazard.

Reedglass Anchorage.name: Reedglass Anchorage
Reedglass Anchorage.basicInfo:
A low mooring, boat store and sheltered deck stand above the northeastern lake margin. This is Mirrorwater’s practical entry point for surveyors, carriers and visitors on an agreed route. Small working boats travel real water within an island; crossing the next sky gap still needs transport.

ROUTES: Tetherroot Chain: the attended southern carrier crossing; Mirrorwater Basin: a marked water channel; Heatherwatch Shelf: the southeastern cooperative crossing. A sky gap requires the stated actual crossing; nearby map pins do not imply connected ground.
Reedglass Anchorage.hiddenInfo:
The anchorage is a usable refuge with no mandatory combat. A missing sampling skiff may be trapped in reeds rather than stolen. Returning it settles that job; the boat does not become expedition loot. Reports from the marsh should distinguish confirmed channels from beautiful reflections of empty sky.

Reedglass Anchorage - Arrival Deck.description: The platform receives the cooperative route from Tetherroot and departures toward Heatherwatch. Cargo and passengers are counted under actual terms.

Reedglass Anchorage - Boat Store.description:
Small skiffs, poles and patch materials can be hired or commissioned. A boat works on water, not over the open sky.

Mio Sasahara maintains the boats and quotes actual local trips. She is confident on water and uncomfortable over wide open sky; do not treat that fear as incompetence at her work.

Reedglass Anchorage - Sample Shelter.description: Dry surfaces permit sorting, labeling and agreeing a report. A valid negative result can be useful if the actual question was tested.

Reedglass Anchorage - Reed Margin.description: A marked channel enters Mirrorwater Basin. Water depth and recent movement can be checked before pushing off.

Mirrorwater Basin.name: Mirrorwater Basin
Mirrorwater Basin.basicInfo:
A broad lake plateau holds sheltered bays, flooded groves and scattered grassy shelves. Reflections conceal the difference between an open channel and a cloud gap beyond the rim. The basin supports ecology surveys, salvage and controlled creature work.

ROUTES: Reedglass Anchorage: a marked water channel; Glassreed Labyrinth: a navigable shallow-water route; Spillway Steps: a shore-and-limestone route. A sky gap requires the stated actual crossing; nearby map pins do not imply connected ground.
Mirrorwater Basin.hiddenInfo:
Mantlefin Drifters feed under the broad water surface and occasionally rise through reeds. Adult mouths are underneath their central keel, not on a humanoid face. Glassreed Sifters disturb the shallows. An observed migration can explain damaged survey lines without requiring a lake monster boss.

Mirrorwater Basin - Sounding Bay.description: A protected bay permits depth checks and a defensible launch. The nearest return landing remains visible.

Mirrorwater Basin - Flooded Grove.description: Roots and submerged branches create narrow channels. Disturbed sediment and cut reeds indicate real movement below the surface.

Mirrorwater Basin - Drifter Reach.description: Wide water gives Mantlefin Drifters room to turn. Ripples and pale fin edges can be observed before entering their path.

Mirrorwater Basin - Rim Watch.description:
A grassy rise overlooks the lake’s spill edge. A visible sky reflection is a warning to confirm the actual shoreline, not a new portal.

Orivelle’s observed circuit reaches this rim on its third day. Observers recognize it by the old notch in its left wing.

Glassreed Labyrinth.name: Glassreed Labyrinth
Glassreed Labyrinth.basicInfo:
Dense translucent reeds and narrow water lanes create an extensive wetland maze. Sound carries oddly through hollow stems, and the same channel can look different from the water. Material gathering here rewards marking a route and identifying mature growth.

ROUTES: Mirrorwater Basin: a navigable shallow-water route; Drowned Orrery: a charted lake approach; Undertow Hollows: a southern shore approach and cave entry. A sky gap requires the stated actual crossing; nearby map pins do not imply connected ground.
Glassreed Labyrinth.hiddenInfo:
Glassreed Sifters clip stems into feeding cages, while Lantern Leech swarms follow exposed light at dusk. Cut only mature loose stems under an actual permit. An expedition that records the colony’s movement may obtain the required material without provoking the entire wetland.

Glassreed Labyrinth - Channel Mouth.description: Solid banks permit markers and a retreat bearing before entering the reeds.

Glassreed Labyrinth - Hollow Lanes.description: Several channels meet around a stable stump. Physical route markers persist; a failed roll need not generate an impossible new map.

Glassreed Labyrinth - Sifter Cages.description: Six-legged Glassreed Sifters weave cut stems around their bodies. The cage flexes as they turn; exposed joints and interrupted feeding currents offer counterplay.

Glassreed Labyrinth - Clearwater Pocket.description: A small open pool provides a brief view above the reed tops. Sampling and regrouping are possible without making the pool a guaranteed safe campsite.

Spillway Steps.name: Spillway Steps
Spillway Steps.basicInfo:
Terraces of pale limestone carry shallow water down to multiple hanging falls. Mineral growth and unusual flow make this a useful survey and procurement site. Open rock gives good visibility but little concealment from creatures moving between pools.

ROUTES: Mirrorwater Basin: a shore-and-limestone route; Lanternmire Islets: a short wetland crossing between real landings. A sky gap requires the stated actual crossing; nearby map pins do not imply connected ground.
Spillway Steps.hiddenInfo:
Spillback Crabs use hinged backplates to redirect a narrow jet. Cracked channels show where repeated blasts have undermined footing. Adjusting a blocked flow can move a feeding group without a kill. Stable shed plates are useful for pump housings; living shell is not free scrap.

Spillway Steps - Upper Shelf.description: Water depth and flow can be compared before descending. A dry section permits tools and sample containers to be secured.

Spillway Steps - Crab Pools.description: Spillback Crabs brace on six walking legs while raising paired jet shields. They commit visibly before firing and struggle to turn on dry broken rock.

Spillway Steps - Mineral Steps.description: Colored deposits show different flow histories. A careful small sample preserves more information than smashing the entire terrace.

Spillway Steps - Hanging Falls.description: Water leaves the island in open air. The fall can be measured from a safe anchor; it is not a hidden route to another region.

Lanternmire Islets.name: Lanternmire Islets
Lanternmire Islets.basicInfo:
Small wet islands gather around dark pools and luminous plants. Solid hummocks, rooted mats and open channels form a compact island group treated as one field location. Light is attractive here, but not every glow is a threat or a guide.

ROUTES: Spillway Steps: a short wetland crossing between real landings. A sky gap requires the stated actual crossing; nearby map pins do not imply connected ground.
Lanternmire Islets.hiddenInfo:
Mire Lanterns lure insects with organs above their four-legged bodies; Lantern Leeches swarm around bright disturbance. Old marker lights can be restored without clearing every pool. Natural glows do not reveal an automatic secret door, and a creature’s lure is not compulsory mind control.

Lanternmire Islets - Firm Hummock.description: A low dry rise supports a temporary field station and a visible return marker.

Lanternmire Islets - False Lights.description: Separate moving creature lights from fixed flowers by position and rhythm. Observation gives a practical alternative to following every glow.

Lanternmire Islets - Root Mats.description: Some mats bear only the local wildlife’s weight. Poles, a lighter route or actual magic can test them; fae ancestry does not make every person weightless.

Lanternmire Islets - Old Marker Posts.description: Rotting posts identify the former sampling line. Repairing one can produce a useful route record without activating a magical fast-travel network.

Drowned Orrery.name: Drowned Orrery
Drowned Orrery.basicInfo:
A roofless observation ring lies half submerged in a lake hollow, its smaller instruments scattered through flooded chambers. The ruin measured reflected light and current cycles. Diving, draining or working from the exposed ring changes which parts can be studied.

ROUTES: Glassreed Labyrinth: a charted lake approach. A sky gap requires the stated actual crossing; nearby map pins do not imply connected ground.
Drowned Orrery.hiddenInfo:
The apparent moving star inside the mechanism is a Lensback Eel using the ring to focus its lure. It does not operate the whole ruin or possess its creators’ knowledge. Accurate records can distinguish the live reflection from the old machinery. Removal may be unnecessary if it no longer threatens the survey.

Undertow Hollows.name: Undertow Hollows
Undertow Hollows.basicInfo:
Linked caverns beneath a southern wetland island carry alternating air and water channels. A broad entry pool gives way to narrow siphons and dry shelves. This is a demanding midgame cave survey, with a real return route and practical reasons to limit how far a team commits.

ROUTES: Glassreed Labyrinth: a southern shore approach and cave entry. A sky gap requires the stated actual crossing; nearby map pins do not imply connected ground.
Undertow Hollows.hiddenInfo:
A Water Elemental follows a blocked circulation loop while Mantlefin young feed in quieter pools. The blockage, not an omnipotent cursed heart, drives the pulses. Opening a safe bypass or documenting an unsafe condition are valid responses. The party should not be forced through a lethal siphon to complete an ordinary sample job.

Undertow Hollows - Dry Traverse.description: A broken high shelf bypasses part of the flow at the cost of difficult footing. Its limits are visible before commitment.

Heatherwatch Shelf.name: Heatherwatch Shelf
Heatherwatch Shelf.basicInfo:
A weather shelter and hardened landing occupy the western approach to the violet plateaus. Stores, a rescue cache and survey markers support prepared expeditions. The surrounding heath is visible from cover, making this a practical place to judge conditions before crossing into rougher country.

ROUTES: Rimeglass Refuge: the eastern cooperative crossing; Reedglass Anchorage: the southeastern cooperative crossing; Mauvewind Steppe: an open marked approach; Singing Stone Spines: a pale-ridge path. A sky gap requires the stated actual crossing; nearby map pins do not imply connected ground.
Heatherwatch Shelf.hiddenInfo:
A contracted keeper may be present, generated when needed; there is no mandatory named frontier commander. Rescue stores remain communal property. The refuge is not a level gate: a cautious visitor can turn back or hire transport even when nearby wilderness is beyond their ability.

Akito Kazamori is the established local guide. He can be extravagant in stories and exact about immediate danger. His Orivelle accounts need evidence; they are not a guaranteed summoning method.

Mauvewind Steppe.name: Mauvewind Steppe
Mauvewind Steppe.basicInfo:
Broad flowering plateaus carry low heather, shallow gullies and scattered rocky spines. Herd paths and predator runs cross the open ground. Surveying growth, recovering shed material and escorting a load are practical jobs here, with broad visibility and limited cover.

ROUTES: Heatherwatch Shelf: an open marked approach; Prismbloom Basin: a sloping mineral shore route; Crownfall Chasm: a southern heath route. A sky gap requires the stated actual crossing; nearby map pins do not imply connected ground.
Mauvewind Steppe.hiddenInfo:
Bramblehorns graze among Glassmane Courser herds. The herbivores defend space and young; the coursers are sharp-edged predators despite their long-legged grazing silhouette. Cropped shrubs, hoof patterns and eye placement can distinguish them. A convoy may change route instead of fighting the whole herd.

Mauvewind Steppe - Herd Flats.description: Bramblehorn groups maintain real distances. A warning display can be respected; every grazing animal is not a hostile target.

Mauvewind Steppe - Courser Shelf.description: Glassmane Coursers wait on pale ridges where their segmented mane resembles grass. A flank watcher can detect the deliberate stillness before a rush.

Singing Stone Spines.name: Singing Stone Spines
Singing Stone Spines.basicInfo:
Tall pale stone blades form narrow passages and natural resonating chambers. Wind produces changing notes rather than a constant song. The formations matter to acoustic research and precision enchantment, while their broken passages reward route planning.

ROUTES: Heatherwatch Shelf: a pale-ridge path; The Inverted Crown: a prepared crossing followed by a high ridge. A sky gap requires the stated actual crossing; nearby map pins do not imply connected ground.
Singing Stone Spines.hiddenInfo:
Hushbell Carapaces and Chimeback Striders occupy different sound niches. Certain missing notes identify a carapace rather than a damaged rock. A field team can compare tones, isolate a blocked passage or gather a permitted loose shard without smashing the formations into a weapon supply.

Singing Stone Spines - Resonance Lanes.description: Wind speed and visible geometry explain most changes. The lanes do not magically know a visitor’s secrets or demand a spoken password.

Singing Stone Spines - Strider Court.description: Chimeback Striders brace tripod legs around a ringing backplate. They telegraph a pulse by lifting the plate; broken sightlines and interrupted resonance offer counterplay.

Singing Stone Spines - Quiet Pocket.description: A local patch of silence may reveal a Hushbell Carapace. Observation or a detour can preserve the acoustic survey.

Prismbloom Basin.name: Prismbloom Basin
Prismbloom Basin.basicInfo:
Mineral pools collect beneath violet flowering banks, leaving iridescent crust and clear growth. Local light makes shallow surfaces look deeper and close ledges seem farther apart. This is a valuable fieldwork site for material quality, optical effects and habitat study.

ROUTES: Mauvewind Steppe: a sloping mineral shore route. A sky gap requires the stated actual crossing; nearby map pins do not imply connected ground.
Prismbloom Basin.hiddenInfo:
Prismfold Fans turn their jointed translucent bodies toward the sun, while Petalglass Snails graze the margins. The fans’ refraction can mislead a rush but is not reality manipulation. Polarized shade and changing the viewing angle expose the real body. Loose cast-off plates are a valid procurement target.

Prismbloom Basin - Fan Beds.description: Prismfold Fans hold several paired membranes above a low segmented body. Their moving shadow and repeated hinge angles reveal where they actually are.

Prismbloom Basin - Bloom Banks.description: Flower roots stabilize the slope. Taking every plant destroys the bank and violates any limited collection agreement.

Prismbloom Basin - Clear Pool.description: A clear pool offers an undisturbed comparison. It provides evidence, not a universal heal or Mana restoration.

Crownfall Chasm.name: Crownfall Chasm
Crownfall Chasm.basicInfo:
A deep fault cuts one of the southern violet islands, exposing mineral bands, ledge paths and wind tunnels. Broken observation gear remains on an accessible shelf. Rescues, instrument retrieval and structural surveys can be attempted without treating the entire abyss as a dungeon entrance.

ROUTES: Mauvewind Steppe: a southern heath route; Stillstar Sanctum: a carrier-assisted ledge crossing. A sky gap requires the stated actual crossing; nearby map pins do not imply connected ground.
Crownfall Chasm.hiddenInfo:
Veilhook Ray flocks ride the chasm lift. Their ventral hooks catch cliff growth and unsecured gear; a snatched bag can remain on a reachable ledge rather than disappear forever. A measured route and visible tether plan can avoid a fight in open air. Falls use actual resolution and available recovery.

Crownfall Chasm - Lower Shelf.description: A solid shelf permits a bounded recovery task and a real ascent back out. Do not invent a second realm beneath the chasm.

Stillstar Sanctum.name: Stillstar Sanctum
Stillstar Sanctum.basicInfo:
A low ruined survey sanctuary lies among pale ridges. Enclosed calibration rooms, a roofless court and a buried work chamber occupy one compact ruin. Visitors can document its optical instruments and seek a permitted component while preserving the remaining record.

ROUTES: Crownfall Chasm: a carrier-assisted ledge crossing. A sky gap requires the stated actual crossing; nearby map pins do not imply connected ground.
Stillstar Sanctum.hiddenInfo:
The last custodians sealed a noisy resonator because it damaged nearby habitat. A Palimpsest Warden still reacts to repeated flashes inside the work chamber. The choice is between stabilization, careful removal and documenting why the part should remain; destruction yields no intact precision component. The custodians’ full history is not known from a glance.

The Inverted Crown.name: The Inverted Crown
The Inverted Crown.basicInfo:
The innermost pale peak curves around a sheltered bowl, its exposed underside resembling an inverted crown. High shelves, wind tunnels and a narrow final ridge form one demanding midgame expedition site. It is known from distant silhouettes before its inner route is actually surveyed.

ROUTES: Singing Stone Spines: a prepared crossing followed by a high ridge. A sky gap requires the stated actual crossing; nearby map pins do not imply connected ground.
The Inverted Crown.hiddenInfo:
A mature Choirglass Colossus shelters in the crown bowl, sometimes driving other animals outward with resonance. Generate one persistent individual when actually encountered, at level 48–55, with real abilities, a readable body and a resolved disposition. This is a dangerous local organism, not a world-ending deity or a level-100 boss. A successful defense, relocation of the expedition route, negotiated access if genuinely sapient, or defeated animal can change the local risk. Do not repopulate it after a recorded resolution.

The Inverted Crown - Underside Gallery.description: A covered passage reveals the suspended rock structure without making every void beneath an island walkable.

The Inverted Crown - Choir Bowl.description: The colossus braces inside a broad bowl with three visible resonance vanes. Ground cover, damaged tuning structures and gaps between pulses provide actual tactical choices.

The Inverted Crown - Return Ridge.description: A narrow but real route leads back toward the saddle. Retreat remains an attempt with counterplay; a successful exit does not require killing the creature.

Adventurer's Guild - Glowhaven Branch.name: Adventurer's Guild - Glowhaven Branch
Adventurer's Guild - Glowhaven Branch.basicInfo: A welcoming timber-and-stone guild hall serves adventurers and clients in Glowhaven City. Honey-colored beams, teal-and-ochre tiles and warm geometric stained glass frame a substantial reception counter, rank-tabbed request boards and communal tables. Komugi Hanabishi handles the front desk. Side rooms support appraisals, briefings and records, with a controlled practice yard at the rear. Sword carriers, shield users and spellcasters all have reason to visit.
Adventurer's Guild - Glowhaven Branch.hiddenInfo:
This is the international Adventurer's Guild's court-permitted Glowhaven branch. Use Komugi Hanabishi at reception rather than inventing a replacement clerk. Other actual roles may be filled when needed, but she is not every assessor, healer or specialist. The hall is normally safe and does not spawn combat because it serves adventurers.

Use the actual exam and badge triggers. Registration starts an application; Bronze is granted only after judgment and a resolved practical test are certified. Rank badges are personal credentials and confer no stats, political immunity or portal access. Higher badges qualify for lower-tier jobs. Promotion eligibility is a review invitation, not a compulsory duel or instant badge exchange.

The stated reward is paid in full; do not narrate or deduct a further guild commission. A completed guild contract grants one Guild Service Credit; unrelated quests do not. Reusing a completed contract does not create another payment. Accepting a foreign job never issues court portal keys.

The branch currently uses five credited jobs for a Silver review, ten further credits for Gold and twenty further credits for Platinum. Appropriate judgment, actual work at the required responsibility and an accepted assessment still matter. These are branch review thresholds, not character-level gates. Strong newcomers can request a prompt fair assessment; strength is not an offense. The recognized ranks are Bronze, Silver, Gold and Platinum.

Guild work: use the actual request board for a small set of badge-appropriate offers. Short contracts and the Salvage, Road and Separate Pay adventures have separate actual terms. Browsing does not accept work; the guild board trigger handles eligible postings. Higher-rank notices can remain locked. Portal keys require the court.

CATALOGUE SUPPLY CONTEXT: Appropriate ordinary or specialist stock can include Surveyor's North Compass; Folding Map Board; Mechanist's Repair Roll; Field Healing Tonic; Trail Vigor Draught; Waterproof Courier Tube. These are exact itemTypes identities, not already granted items or guaranteed unlimited stock. Present a few relevant goods when browsing or a supply request actually happens, with real payment and ownership. Visiting does not buy anything. Rare teaching scrolls may enter a genuine specialist collection or discovery; do not place every scroll in every shop.

Sepulchral Portal House.name: Sepulchral Portal House
Sepulchral Portal House.basicInfo: A dry tiled threshold stands outside the abandoned glasshouses. Its pale return arch shows the familiar roots of the Evertree. A worn inspection table and sheltered benches make it a practical place to prepare or turn back.
Sepulchral Portal House.hiddenInfo: Preserve the actual Nature/Soul distinction: living plant framework, spiritual binding and conscious occupant are separate. Use the authored creature types as real generated actors before resolving attacks. No instant unregistered damage. Retreat and the portal house remain usable. Cleared encounters stay cleared; do not respawn an endless army on every arrival. Exploration is optional and has a visible level 35–50 risk band. This is a refuge, not an automatic ambush. A clear committed return goes directly to Evertree Base - Portal Room without needing a key.

Sepulchral Portal House - Return Arch.description: An intact pale arch opens toward the recognizable Evertree roots. Dry benches and an old inspection table make this threshold a usable staging refuge.

Sepulchral Portal House - Vestibule.description: Cracked green tiles lead past a gardener's coat hooks and a plan of the sanctuary carved in stone. The main conservatory is visible through the outer doors.

Sepulchral Conservatory.name: Sepulchral Conservatory
Sepulchral Conservatory.basicInfo: Cracked green glass roofs shelter pale timber bodies, white-leaved memorial trees and slow irrigation channels. Two tending wings circle an inner bronze-latticed greenhouse. Some wooden figures carry names; others repeat only a gardener's old instructions.
Sepulchral Conservatory.hiddenInfo: Preserve the actual Nature/Soul distinction: living plant framework, spiritual binding and conscious occupant are separate. Use the authored creature types as real generated actors before resolving attacks. No instant unregistered damage. Retreat and the portal house remain usable. Cleared encounters stay cleared; do not respawn an endless army on every arrival. Exploration is optional and has a visible level 35–50 risk band. Introduce small groups of two or three appropriate Gravewood Golems or Rootbound Pallbearers around the Rootwalk/Tending Gallery, and a Censer-Willow with one Ossuary Trellis deeper in the memorial wing. Announce visible movement, cover and ways to withdraw before attacks. These are encounter compositions, not a claim that a typed spawn effect exists. The rootwake valve in the Tending Gallery and mourning valve in the Ossuary Greenhouse must actually be released, repaired or overcome before the inner lattice opens. A nonmage can work with tools, evidence or qualified help. Threnvoss is the sole named caretaker in the Grafting Heart; no substitute boss or automatic opening hit. Two finite Grafted Sentinels can defend the heart if real generated actors exist. The Keeper Archive establishes which vessels hold conscious spirits. Defeat or a genuinely carried-out release can quiet the sanctuary.

Sepulchral Conservatory - Entry Rotunda.description: A roof of cracked green glass shelters a dry circular platform above slow irrigation water. Two overgrown tending wings lead toward a bronze-latticed inner greenhouse.

Sepulchral Conservatory - Rootwalk.description: Pale root bridges cross irrigation channels beside silent racks of unfinished wooden bodies. Broad piers offer cover from the guardians beyond.

Sepulchral Conservatory - Tending Galler.description: Pruning tools, repaired joints and strips of binding cloth cover long workbenches. Timber guardians patrol around an exposed rootwake valve.

Sepulchral Conservatory - Memorial Orcha.description: White-leaved trees carry small bronze nameplates. Some hollow trunks answer a voice; others repeat only an old work instruction.

The ground, visible approach and nearby cover make it possible to observe before committing to the next stretch. A grove of enormous pale trees encloses a patch of sky that never becomes fully clear.

Hinoki Hollow Onsen.name: Hinoki Hollow Onsen
Hinoki Hollow Onsen.basicInfo: Warm mineral water rises beneath a low cypress bathhouse at the wooded edge of Benitsuru. A covered washing court, small quiet pools and a garden rest veranda offer a break from the capital. A basic bath and clean towel cost 6 marks. A short maintained lane leads toward South Gate Caravan Yard.
Hinoki Hollow Onsen.hiddenInfo: Atsuha Yunokawa runs this actual bathhouse. Establish ordinary fees and privacy before use. A bath is ordinary rest, not an automatic cure or duplicated resource grant. A guest may talk, wash or leave; do not infer intimacy from paying for a bath.

Hinoki Hollow Onsen - Reception Porch.description: The reception porch is a usable part of Hinoki Hollow Onsen, with work surfaces or clear standing space fitted to the people who use it. Voices and activity from the adjoining space carry across its entrance. Warm mineral water rises beneath a low cypress bathhouse at the wooded edge of Benitsuru.

Hinoki Hollow Onsen - Washing Court.description: The washing court is a usable part of Hinoki Hollow Onsen, with work surfaces or clear standing space fitted to the people who use it. Voices and activity from the adjoining space carry across its entrance. Warm mineral water rises beneath a low cypress bathhouse at the wooded edge of Benitsuru.

Hinoki Hollow Onsen - Stone Pools.description: Stone Pools is a distinct stopping point at Hinoki Hollow Onsen. The ground, visible approach and nearby cover make it possible to observe before committing to the next stretch. Warm mineral water rises beneath a low cypress bathhouse at the wooded edge of Benitsuru.

Hinoki Hollow Onsen - Rest Veranda.description: The rest veranda is a usable part of Hinoki Hollow Onsen, with work surfaces or clear standing space fitted to the people who use it. Voices and activity from the adjoining space carry across its entrance. Warm mineral water rises beneath a low cypress bathhouse at the wooded edge of Benitsuru.

The Gilded Albatross.name: The Gilded Albatross
The Gilded Albatross.basicInfo: An ornate but hard-used sailing ship rides at a charted anchorage. Its butterfly-winged captain takes salvage work and agreed voyages, while crew members mend gear, cook and argue over their shares. Passage, employment and joining an expedition are separate arrangements.
The Gilded Albatross.hiddenInfo: Local opportunities and ecology: Sailcloth Moth, Mooring Mimic. Aboard is a working household. Pests or salvage complications occur through real causes and can be addressed without spawning a fight every visit. Crew are not automatically recruited. Use the actual scene, relevant NPC types and the party’s real experience. These are possible situations, not an instruction to generate all of them at arrival. Authored people and the three named creatures retain their own power. Travel encounters remain separate from exploration within the location.

The Gilded Albatross - Boarding Landing.description: A boat comes alongside a rope ladder and guarded boarding rail. Visitors announce their business before climbing aboard.

The Gilded Albatross - Main Deck.description: Coiled ropes leave clear working lanes between the masts. Sailors repair canvas, secure loads and exchange news without stopping the ship’s work.

The Gilded Albatross - Quarterdeck.description: A broad rail overlooks the sails and sea. Reina Kazehara discusses routes and terms here when she is not needed elsewhere.

The Gilded Albatross - Galley.description: A swinging kettle hangs beside a compact stove and well-lashed stores. Nanae Kogure feeds the crew and guards her best seasoning.

The Gilded Albatross - Salvage Hold.description: Tagged crates, drying equipment and a small inspection table occupy the hold. Stored finds remain under their actual owner’s custody.

The Gilded Albatross - Crew Passage.description: Cabin doors and hammocks line a narrow, airy passage. Visiting passengers receive an agreed berth; other cabins remain private.

Splinterwake Wreck.name: Splinterwake Wreck
Splinterwake Wreck.basicInfo: A broken merchant hull lies among sharp eastern rocks. Low water exposes cargo spaces, but the approaches bear gouges far below the tide line. Large disturbances sometimes move through the surrounding water; an ordinary salvage trip need not challenge their source.
Splinterwake Wreck.hiddenInfo: Local opportunities and ecology: Barnacle Brute, Undertow Eel, Mooring Mimic. Use finite groups of one to three fitting creatures, with room to observe or retreat. The level-55 authored kraken is a separate optional deepwater danger; never replace it with a fresh generated duplicate. Check actual Ghorvath placement and state before involving it. Use the actual scene, relevant NPC types and the party’s real experience. These are possible situations, not an instruction to generate all of them at arrival. Authored people and the three named creatures retain their own power. Travel encounters remain separate from exploration within the location.

Splinterwake Wreck - Outer Anchorage.description: Sound water lies beyond the submerged spars. Boats can wait, observe the swell and choose whether to approach.

Splinterwake Wreck - Broken Deck.description: Tilted planks and snapped ribs rise above the water. Lashings, safe footing and the changing tide matter more than speed.

Splinterwake Wreck - Flooded Hold.description: Cold water covers loose cargo and low beams. Air, light and an actual way back are necessary for diving.

Splinterwake Wreck - Deepwater Edge.description: The reef drops suddenly into dark water. Broad suckered marks on timber and unnatural swells warn of a great predator’s passing.

Moonarch Isle.name: Moonarch Isle
Moonarch Isle.basicInfo: A weathered stone arch and low foundations stand above a small rocky landing. Salt-resistant plants grow between old paving stones. Surveyors can study the remains without assuming the arch is an active portal.
Moonarch Isle.hiddenInfo: Local opportunities and ecology: Inkpot Cuttlefish, Shoalglass Ray, Undertow Eel. The arch is a ruin, not an automatic portal. Low water, stable footing and recorded marks make useful investigation. Sheltered landing encounters can be modest; the flooded undercroft needs preparation. Use the actual scene, relevant NPC types and the party’s real experience. These are possible situations, not an instruction to generate all of them at arrival. Authored people and the three named creatures retain their own power. Travel encounters remain separate from exploration within the location.

Moonarch Isle - Pebble Landing.description: A sheltered shelf offers room to beach a small boat in fair conditions.

Moonarch Isle - Broken Arch.description: One stone span still stands above cracked paving. Its surviving carvings reward patient copying rather than force.

Moonarch Isle - Tide Crypt.description: A shallow undercroft opens from the lower foundations. Water stains mark when its passages become unsafe.

Moonarch Isle - Offshore Drop.description: Beyond the sheltered landing, the bottom drops into dark water. Heavy swell and broad marks on driftwood warn of deepwater animals.

Stillback Isle.name: Stillback Isle
Stillback Isle.basicInfo: A vast shell rests so quietly among the low rocks that it resembles part of the island. Mauruun grazes, sleeps and watches the water with immense patience. Fishers give the creature room and know better than to mistake stillness for helplessness.
Stillback Isle.hiddenInfo: Local opportunities and ecology: Tideglass Shrimp, Inkpot Cuttlefish, Hookbeak Gull. Mauruun is the unique resident, not a generated hostile turtle. Quiet arrival does not provoke it. Any finite small wildlife problem must leave its passive baseline intact. Use the actual scene, relevant NPC types and the party’s real experience. These are possible situations, not an instruction to generate all of them at arrival. Authored people and the three named creatures retain their own power. Travel encounters remain separate from exploration within the location.

Stillback Isle - Quiet Landing.description: A small sheltered beach lies away from the creature’s head. Boats can land without stepping onto its resting ground.

Stillback Isle - Shell Garden.description: Weathered plates hold weed, harmless shell life and patches of old fishing line. The creature’s breathing shifts the ground beneath anyone who climbs aboard.

Stillback Isle - Nesting Shelf.description: Warm sand and low rocks form a protected resting shelf. Mauruun reacts strongly to harassment, injury or disturbance here.

Greenrush Estuary.name: Greenrush Estuary
Greenrush Estuary.basicInfo: Reed channels and pale sandbars divide the river’s meeting with the sea. Working skiffs follow changing water marks between the marsh and the coast. Fish traps, nesting birds and stranded debris offer ordinary work as well as reasons to explore.
Greenrush Estuary.hiddenInfo: Local opportunities and ecology: Tideglass Shrimp, Reedlace Sprite, Tangletooth Otter, Brinecap Slime. Shallow-land jobs favor levels 2–8, a single active hostile initially, clear warning and practical alternatives. Deeper optional work can reach 12–18 after actual preparation. Do not turn passive wildlife into attacking packs. Use the actual scene, relevant NPC types and the party’s real experience. These are possible situations, not an instruction to generate all of them at arrival. Authored people and the three named creatures retain their own power. Travel encounters remain separate from exploration within the location.

Greenrush Estuary - Skiff Landing.description: Daisaku Minobe’s timber supports hold small boats above the mud. Repairs and passage are arranged before a hull is taken.

Greenrush Estuary - Reedwalk.description: Raised footing follows a shallow channel where birds nest and fish flash beneath reeds.

Greenrush Estuary - Sandbar Crossing.description: The exposed bar offers a short route at low tide. Wet stakes and drift lines show how quickly its character changes.

Greenrush Estuary - Field Shelter.description: Sample jars, drying nets and a weather board crowd a modest covered workbench.

Thistlebank Alchemy Cottage.name: Thistlebank Alchemy Cottage
Thistlebank Alchemy Cottage.basicInfo: A low rural cottage smells of bruised herbs and warm copper. Yorina Tsugawa sells preparations by arrangement and complains loudly when customers mistake a difficult recipe for a miracle. A small garden and workroom support a real household as well as her experiments.
Thistlebank Alchemy Cottage.hiddenInfo: Local opportunities and ecology: Sailcloth Moth, Burdock Lurker. The garden and workroom support small experiments, trade and household life. Do not add another dangerous unstable-potion conspiracy merely because an alchemist is present. Use the actual scene, relevant NPC types and the party’s real experience. These are possible situations, not an instruction to generate all of them at arrival. Authored people and the three named creatures retain their own power. Travel encounters remain separate from exploration within the location.

Thistlebank Alchemy Cottage - Cottage Do.description: Plant trays and clean boots compete for space beneath a patched awning.

Thistlebank Alchemy Cottage - Copper Wor.description: A sturdy bench carries labeled jars, a condenser and a basin for safely cooling mixtures.

Thistlebank Alchemy Cottage - Herb Plot.description: Raised beds grow ordinary useful plants alongside a few temperamental magical specimens.

Wrenhill Windmill.name: Wrenhill Windmill
Wrenhill Windmill.basicInfo: The windmill turns above scattered grain plots on Brookmeadow’s western approach. Customers wait with sacks while Shūhei Kusanagi counts loads and Fuyuka Kusanagi listens for mechanical trouble. Flour dust, local gossip and sibling arguments move through the yard together.
Wrenhill Windmill.hiddenInfo: Local opportunities and ecology: Flour Beetle, Sailcloth Moth. A bounded store or machinery problem can occur during actual inspection; stop the machinery before handling a jam. Routine business and the siblings’ own work continue. Use the actual scene, relevant NPC types and the party’s real experience. These are possible situations, not an instruction to generate all of them at arrival. Authored people and the three named creatures retain their own power. Travel encounters remain separate from exploration within the location.

Wrenhill Windmill - Mill Yard.description: Wagons wait clear of the turning machinery and weighing platform.

Wrenhill Windmill - Grinding Floor.description: Wooden gearing drives covered stones beneath a dust-worn beam. Work stops before anyone handles a jam.

Wrenhill Windmill - Sail Gallery.description: An exposed gallery gives access to the sails and a wide view across the downs.

Old Southwatch.name: Old Southwatch
Old Southwatch.basicInfo: An old lookout stands on a forested southern rise. Hirotaka Fushimi keeps its lower room habitable, mends what he can and considers unsolicited tracking advice an insult. Its view remains useful even though it no longer commands a garrison.
Old Southwatch.hiddenInfo: Local opportunities and ecology: Burdock Lurker, Chalkback Ram. The keeper and the ruin have ordinary uses. Any finite wildlife issue belongs to the surrounding path, not an obligatory ambush in his home. Use the actual scene, relevant NPC types and the party’s real experience. These are possible situations, not an instruction to generate all of them at arrival. Authored people and the three named creatures retain their own power. Travel encounters remain separate from exploration within the location.

Old Southwatch - Forest Steps.description: Roots cross the old stone approach; daylight makes the loose sections easy to notice.

Old Southwatch - Keeper’s Room.description: A stove, bedroll and carefully maintained tools occupy the lower room.

Old Southwatch - Lookout Walk.description: The upper walk overlooks the forest edge and open plain. Damaged masonry limits where it is safe to stand.

Bluecoil Rest.name: Bluecoil Rest
Bluecoil Rest.basicInfo: A great blue serpent sleeps across a remote reef, its body half hidden by clear water. Slow breathing lifts spray against the rocks, while shed scales catch beneath the tide line. Boats can observe from outside its reach; disturbing its resting ground risks waking a formidable animal.
Bluecoil Rest.hiddenInfo: Local opportunities and ecology: Kelpclaw Crab, Tideglass Shrimp. Nerathyl is the unique fixed sleeping serpent. Begin with its established current condition; never reset it after actual events. Show its formidable level-45 danger before a close approach. No free surprise strike or automatic awakening from observation at the distant mooring. Use the actual scene, relevant NPC types and the party’s real experience. These are possible situations, not an instruction to generate all of them at arrival. Authored people and the three named creatures retain their own power. Travel encounters remain separate from exploration within the location.

Bluecoil Rest - Distant Mooring.description: A bare outlying rock gives observers a place to secure a boat well away from the sleeping body.

Bluecoil Rest - Scale Shore.description: A narrow wash gathers naturally shed scales and drift. Fresh drag marks warn when the serpent has recently moved.

Bluecoil Rest - Serpent Ledge.description: The immense animal’s head and coils occupy the inner rocks. The ledge is its resting place rather than an ordinary landing.

Beaconrest Lighthouse.name: Beaconrest Lighthouse
Beaconrest Lighthouse.basicInfo: A red-capped offshore lighthouse guides boats through Whitecrest’s outer channels. Kōzō Hinoura keeps its light and stores in order with help from Saki Hinoura. Visiting crews bring supplies, repairs and more gossip than either keeper admits enjoying.

Beaconrest Lighthouse - Supply Jetty.description: A low jetty receives deliveries when the channel is usable.

Beaconrest Lighthouse - Keeper’s Kitchen.description: Tea, charts and a drying rack share a warm little room beside the stores.

Beaconrest Lighthouse - Lantern Room.description: Polished lenses surround a maintained light assembly. Its working parts are handled with the keepers’ permission.

Beaconrest Lighthouse - Signal Balcony.description: Colored shutters and flags face the harbor approaches.

Starlark Abbey.name: Starlark Abbey
Starlark Abbey.basicInfo: White stone and a small bell tower rise above the southern river. The abbey is devoted to Avelune, Lady of Returning Light, and combines worship with a working hospice, gardens and guest rooms. Visitors need not share the faith to receive ordinary welcome or care.

Starlark Abbey - Pilgrim Court.description: Travelers wait beside a water basin and a shaded bench while attendants arrange beds or introductions.
paths: Starlark Abbey - Chapel of Returning Light

Starlark Abbey - Chapel of Returning Lig.description: Lamps burn beneath a pale star-and-lantern image. Prayer and ceremony have their own rhythms beyond the day’s work.

Starlark Abbey - Hospice.description: Clean linen, screens and herb-scented water surround a small number of beds. Patients are people with privacy, not an audience for every visitor.
paths: Starlark Abbey - Chapel of Returning Light

Starlark Abbey - Kitchen Garden.description: Useful herbs and vegetables grow along narrow paths watched over by Eiji Kuramochi.

Starlark Abbey - Guest Wing.description: Plain rooms and a shared table shelter pilgrims, workers and people recovering from a difficult journey.

Gullwatch Reefs.name: Gullwatch Reefs
Gullwatch Reefs.basicInfo: Low eastern reefs support nesting seabirds and pools bright with small marine life. Fishers know the usable channels and places to collect modest materials. Slippery stone and an incoming tide can turn an easy outing into a practical rescue.
Gullwatch Reefs.hiddenInfo: Local opportunities and ecology: Hookbeak Gull, Kelpclaw Crab, Shoalglass Ray, Salt-Crest Wyvern. The sheltered pools support levels 3–8 and noncombat collection. Exposed high nests are a separate deliberately approached level 24–30 hazard. Mark that difference through tracks, circling and local advice before danger. Use the actual scene, relevant NPC types and the party’s real experience. These are possible situations, not an instruction to generate all of them at arrival. Authored people and the three named creatures retain their own power. Travel encounters remain separate from exploration within the location.

Gullwatch Reefs - Boat Shelf.description: A shallow rocky shelf offers a temporary landing in fair water.

Gullwatch Reefs - Tide Pools.description: Clear pools hold small creatures and useful shell fragments. Disturbing a nest can bring more trouble than the collection is worth.

Gullwatch Reefs - Gull Ledges.description: High shelves overlook the channels and nesting grounds.

Longgrass Crossroads.name: Longgrass Crossroads
Longgrass Crossroads.basicInfo: Three dirt roads meet between the northern approaches, river bridge and Brookmeadow’s western downs. A worn shelter gives travelers room to rest without blocking carts. News, lost animals and the occasional dishonest bargain pass through with the traffic.

Longgrass Crossroads - Way Shelter.description: A plain roof shelters a bench, water jar and a small space for travelers’ notices.

Longgrass Crossroads - Cart Verge.description: Wagons can pull off the road here to change a wheel or compare routes.

Longgrass Crossroads - Riverward Track.description: The southern branch follows open ground toward the bridge and village approach.

Seaward Overlook.name: Seaward Overlook
Seaward Overlook.basicInfo: A quiet grassy cliff looks out across the coast. Wind moves through the trees above a sheltered sitting place, while the exposed edge rewards care. Couples, walkers and solitary visitors can enjoy the view without finding a resident host.

Seaward Overlook - Sheltered Grass.description: A low bank blocks some of the wind and leaves room to sit together.

Seaward Overlook - Sea Ledge.description: The open ledge gives a broad view of water and distant sails; its edge remains unguarded.

Phoenix Wing Academy.name: Phoenix Wing Academy
Phoenix Wing Academy.basicInfo:
Phoenix Wing Academy trains mages for public defense, security readiness, and the practical work of keeping people safe when danger is real. Its red uniforms and phoenix heraldry accompany demanding drills, a fierce dueling culture, monster fieldcraft, and preparation for protecting others under pressure. Lessons connect combat execution with judgment: identify the threat, control the scene, coordinate with others, and know when to stop. Students receive broad magical education comparable to the other academies; no element, temperament, or moral alignment determines admission.
Akane Todo represents Phoenix Wing Academy as its Archon in the Conclave of Archons. Headmaster Kōhei Sanada manages its academic system and daily operations. Its public assignments can include authorized protection, threat assessment, dungeon reconnaissance, and supervised monster tracking or subdual. Student status grants no independent power to arrest, sentence, seize property, or act as a professional soldier. The City Guard handles ordinary policing, the Magistrate's Hall handles judgments, and the Elite Strikeforce retains its separate exceptional duties.
Every student must complete an expedition beyond the Glowhaven region under authorization from the Great Sage or the Great Sage's court. Readiness is tested in the field as well as the arena. The institution's demanding reputation contains ambitious duelists, reluctant fighters, practical researchers, cooks, and people who disagree about what responsible defense requires.
Phoenix Wing Academy.hiddenInfo: Akane Todo wants the academy's judgment and protective work respected alongside its fighting strength. Kōhei Sanada resists performances of toughness that endanger injured students, while Ritsu Kurogane demands precision and Ranka Kagari pursues her own experiments and profit. None speaks for every colleague. The academy's unresolved situations include unsafe incentives in training and discrepancies in a potion trial; surface them only through the relevant actual people and evidence. Institutional pride can complicate criticism without making all staff corrupt or secretly benevolent.

Hydra Head Academy.name: Hydra Head Academy
Hydra Head Academy.basicInfo:
Hydra Head Academy prepares mages to work across people, institutions, and places: diplomacy, trade, logistics, community assistance, mediation, and the coordination that makes civic projects function. Violet clothing and hydra heraldry identify an academy where an impressive result is often one that several parties can actually carry out. Teaching joins magical competence with negotiation, preparation, supplies, routes, and the consequences of conflicting interests. Its broad curriculum and combat instruction remain comparable to the other academies.
Reika Saionji represents the academy as its Archon in the Conclave of Archons. Headmaster Kiyoko Fujinami runs daily academic operations in close partnership with Reika Saionji. Advice, commissions, research collaborations, and authorized civic assistance connect the school to the city. Supporting a dispute does not confer judicial authority; facilitating trade does not establish ownership of another person's goods. Courts and civic offices retain their actual responsibilities.
Every student must complete a Great Sage- or court-authorized expedition outside the Glowhaven region. A field assignment may turn on cooperation, transport, community needs, a survey, or a dangerous situation requiring trained magic. Diplomatic emphasis does not make the academy defenseless or its people uniformly agreeable. Mercenary, shy, confrontational, gentle, extravagant, and intensely private people can all belong here.
Hydra Head Academy.hiddenInfo: Reika Saionji's intimidating public image hides a reserved, kindly researcher and businesswoman. Kiyoko Fujinami understands the person behind that reputation, but a visitor does not learn it simply by reading the academy's name. Faculty have distinct ambitions: Kaoruko Hanazono balances botanical supply with her fragrance business, Reon Fujisaki enjoys glamour, and Kana Fujimoto struggles to keep an ordinary lesson orderly. Fragrance discrepancies and an illusionary attendance dispute can expose competing priorities through actual play. A polished institution can contain disruptive students without a hidden institutional conspiracy.

Gryffin Tail Academy.name: Gryffin Tail Academy
Gryffin Tail Academy.basicInfo:
Gryffin Tail Academy advances magical knowledge through analytical study, field investigation, and the infrastructure needed to make findings useful. Cyan uniforms and gryffin heraldry accompany demanding academic standards, exact practical assessments, and the most advanced research facilities among Glowhaven's four academies. Its education still includes broad magical and combat training; an athlete, reluctant reader, socialite, or struggling practitioner is not misplaced simply because the institution values rigorous work.
Gryffin Tail Academy is the only academy with a formal specialization in magitech research: mechanical engineering integrated with magic, enchantments, or magical components. An enchanted necklace is not automatically magitech, and other academies and artisans remain able to make, buy, study, and repair enchanted goods. Its expeditions can survey dungeons, measure unusual environments, examine specimens and sites, and bring back evidence for further study. Every student must complete an expedition beyond the Glowhaven region authorized by the Great Sage or the Great Sage's court.
Gen'ichirō Mizuhara represents the academy as its Archon in the Conclave of Archons; Norio Shibata manages its records and day-to-day academic administration as Headmaster. Research prestige can make a recommendation valuable and an unfair assessment damaging. Published standards, private ambition, practical results, and the treatment of inconvenient evidence can pull in different directions. A strict instructor's preferred incantation is not a universal law of spellcasting.
Gryffin Tail Academy.hiddenInfo: Gen'ichirō Mizuhara is maneuvering to make his academy's certification the recognized gate to advanced spellwork. He uses supposedly neutral standards to favor people he considers worthy; this prejudice is his agenda, not a truth about any species or every colleague. Norio Shibata prefers correct records to political confrontation and can fix a clerical error while avoiding an unfair policy. Sōichirō Takamine's concern about inconsistent assessment offers a specific avenue for investigation. Records, witnesses, and rulings matter; noticing one unfair act does not automatically expose the Archon's whole plan.

Dragon Hoard Academy.name: Dragon Hoard Academy
Dragon Hoard Academy.basicInfo:
Dragon Hoard Academy specializes in expeditionary exploration and work with relics: finding and surveying unfamiliar sites, assessing discoveries, and preparing for the difficult handling and return of objects whose significance or danger may not be immediately apparent. Yellow-and-gold clothing and dragon heraldry accompany a formidable, exacting institutional tradition. Its strictness descends chiefly from its founder's character and generations of teaching practice; it is not a personality shared by every student or a single-word creed.
Tōru Shizunami represents the academy as its Archon in the Conclave of Archons. Headmaster Miyu Asahina keeps its academic programs and daily operations working. Genzō Iwakura's fieldcraft, Madoka Narukami's demanding practical instruction, Noriaki Takatsuki's exact preparation, and the existing Discovery Labs, Observatory, Exhibition Hall, and Training Court support a school that expects discoveries to survive the journey home. Exploration and relic work complement its broad magical education and combat training rather than replacing them.
Every student must complete an expedition outside the Glowhaven region under authorization from the Great Sage or the Great Sage's court. Relic-oriented missions may involve survey, identification, careful documentation, stabilization, or an explicitly permitted recovery. Discovery grants no automatic title to an object, private site, or another community's heritage. Permissions, safety, custody, and actual claims matter; no universal salvage law is presumed. Curious students, stern professionals, gamblers, repairers, reluctant participants, and a famously talented Archon who dislikes unnecessary work retain their own priorities.
Dragon Hoard Academy.hiddenInfo: Tōru Shizunami's remarkable magical insight coexists with his private misery over work he never wanted. Miyu Asahina admires him but wants reliable systems rather than endless personal rescue. Madoka Narukami, Genzō Iwakura, and Noriaki Takatsuki take their work intensely seriously; their contrasts with their Archon can be funny without making them incompetent. Mai Kajiwara's disputed shield repair, an unofficial betting board, and a planned field exercise offer separate pressures. None is compulsory on arrival, and the student's board is not an academy-approved financial institution.

Conclave of Archons.name: Conclave of Archons
Conclave of Archons.basicInfo:
The Conclave of Archons brings together the four exceptionally capable mages who publicly represent Glowhaven's academies: Akane Todo of Phoenix Wing Academy, Gen'ichirō Mizuhara of Gryffin Tail Academy, Tōru Shizunami of Dragon Hoard Academy, and Reika Saionji of Hydra Head Academy. Each holds their academy's seat. The Conclave gives the institutions an arena for negotiation, coordinated responses, research interests, and rivalry. The headmasters continue managing their respective schools.

The Conclave is distinct from the larger Council that elects the Great Sage. It carries influence without making its four members the only eligible candidates. Public representation and exceptional capability do not mean the Archons administer every street, shop, or classroom themselves. Routine inquiries go to the appropriate local office; an Archon appears when their actual responsibilities or interests warrant it.
Conclave of Archons.hiddenInfo: Succession makes cooperation more difficult: each academy has interests in who follows Ilyra Stillglass, and each Archon approaches influence differently. Do not manufacture a shared secret plan, a formal election date, or an automatic candidate for every school. Gen'ichirō Mizuhara's certification ambitions, Akane Todo's concern for public protection, Tōru Shizunami's reluctance, and Reika Saionji's research priorities can conflict in a concrete meeting. No member automatically knows another's private motives, and Ilyra Stillglass's academy of origin remains unknown.

The Council.name: The Council
The Council.basicInfo:
The Council is Glowhaven City's larger governing body and the institution that elects the Great Sage. It is separate from the four-member Conclave of Archons. A candidate may be an Archon, a council member, or someone from outside either group whose ability earns sufficient support. A term lasts up to one hundred years or ends at the incumbent's death; reelection is possible.

The Council has elected Ilyra Stillglass three times over her 254-year rule because it has continued to regard her as the best choice. Academy influence, noble households, infrastructure, and civic interests make its deliberations important to ordinary life. Petitions and proposals reach decisions through actual representatives, evidence, and negotiation. Wealth, sponsorship, or a school title can open a conversation without granting ownership of the Great Sage's office. The Council's authority does not turn every official into an omniscient enforcer.
The Council.hiddenInfo: The academies are maneuvering over the succession while Ilyra Stillglass remains in office. Different participants can value continuity, capability, patronage, or their own advantage; disagreement is not proof that every member is corrupt. Her attendants know the assistance her failing sight requires, while outsiders have uneven information. Preserve that distinction and her unknown academy origin. Do not invent a definitive membership roster, an existing majority, or a death announcement to accelerate a scene. A political outcome requires actual commitments and decisions, not a single flattering speech.

The Elite Strikeforce.name: The Elite Strikeforce
The Elite Strikeforce.basicInfo:
The Elite Strikeforce serves the Great Sage as Glowhaven City's elite military and confidential security force. It handles major threats and sensitive operations beyond ordinary street policing. Its personnel can also carry the Great Sage's authority on diplomatic journeys to neighboring nations, where judgment and discretion can matter as much as destructive power.

The force operates separately from the City Guard. An ordinary theft report, classroom dispute, or rude visitor does not normally demand its intervention. Serious evidence of a major threat can bring specialized personnel, actual orders, and coordinated action. Its public reputation rests on exceptional capability and proximity to the Great Sage, while identities, assignments, and operational details need not be public knowledge. Its four principal masked operatives are Ayame Kazehara, Gōtarō Iwamine, Shion Kurobane and Seiran Yukitsugu. Their white uniforms and ivory masks are recognizable duty equipment; their individual methods differ.
The Elite Strikeforce.hiddenInfo: Use confidential orders and limited information to create specific decisions rather than an all-seeing service. Members learn what their actual role and briefing provide. A request can be denied, narrowed, verified, or referred to the City Guard. Do not invent a secret commander, named agent, private prison, or blanket power to overrule every institution. Their presence needs an established operation or a credible response to events. Diplomatic work can involve protecting a negotiation or carrying terms without automatically threatening a foreign country.

City Guard.name: City Guard
City Guard.basicInfo:
The City Guard patrols Glowhaven's streets and gates, investigates ordinary crimes, protects the public, and makes arrests within civic authority. Reports go through its headquarters and local officers; the Magistrate's Hall handles hearings and judgments. Tetsuya Ōmi is an established contact at headquarters, while officers at the gates have their own posts and immediate knowledge.

Guards are trained adults who use observation, practical magic, equipment, and coordinated tactics. They ask for support when a danger exceeds their strength and distinguish a witness's allegation from an established finding. Theft, assault, repeated violence, and murder can bring investigation, pursuit, actual capture, and a recorded custody order. Wraith Island provides the exterior approach to the separate Wraith Island Prison realm. Prisoners, authorized workers, visitors, and intruders have different permissions. The Elite Strikeforce has separate military and exceptional-security duties.
City Guard.hiddenInfo: Reports are incomplete until checked. Officers know different pieces of a case, and witnesses can be mistaken, frightened, self-serving, or prejudiced. Tetsuya Ōmi cannot know a private event without a source. Evidence, proportional response, and actual resistance affect what follows. Guards can make mistakes or lose fights without the institution forgetting a documented crime. Release, sentence review, property deposits, authorized prison work, and escape follow the recorded case; an accusation, joke, proximity to a jail, or a knockout does not create or erase a conviction.

The Silken Brood.name: The Silken Brood
The Silken Brood.basicInfo: The arachne matron and the creatures defending the inner workings of the Silken Chasm. Their motives and reactions differ; a passage can sometimes be bypassed without exterminating every creature.
The Silken Brood.hiddenInfo: Vhalessra is responsible for the weaving that snagged the field-test route. She wants control of a stable passage. This does not grant her soul-draining powers or knowledge of every visitor.

Glowhaven.name: Glowhaven
Glowhaven.basicInfo:
Glowhaven is the civic community and autonomous polity centered on the Evertree: the city, surrounding villages, farms, waterways and coast. Its mostly human population includes long-settled nonhuman residents and foreign newcomers. The Great Sage governs through the court, the larger council, public offices and ordinary working institutions. The four academies are prominent parts of public life, not the whole population. Residents include growers, fishers, shopkeepers, craftspeople, tenants, porters, householders, students and people who simply want a dependable livelihood.
A civic affiliation identifies belonging and everyday obligations; it does not mean employment by the state, personal loyalty to the Great Sage or membership in every local guild. A person can be a Glowhaven resident while their primary roster faction is an academy, guard service, household or trade organization. People without a more specific institutional affiliation normally use Glowhaven. Visitors, unaffiliated wanderers and wild creatures need not be assigned here just because they are currently present.
Enchanted goods, agricultural produce, fisheries, shipping, repairs, hospitality and research sustain the region. Permits, housing, wages, public safety, tournaments and access to the dense local mana create real negotiations. Membership supplies no free money, unrestricted research access, court title or portal key. Court-approved passage requires an actual reason and issue.
Glowhaven.hiddenInfo: Residents disagree about academy privilege, the succession and who benefits from public investment. A shopkeeper may welcome students while resenting a damaged frontage; a farmer may admire the Evertree without wanting urban officials to dictate a harvest. No single secret motive belongs to the whole population. Surface a dispute through the actual people affected and their evidence. Civic identity does not tell every resident private court business or make strangers know the player's deeds.

Drakenspire.name: Drakenspire
Drakenspire.basicInfo:
Drakenspire is an independent dragonkin-majority nation whose mountain capital bears the same name. Its people live beneath a high northeastern fortress and the sacred crescent of an ancient protector dragon's skeleton. A Jarl elected through the clan chiefs governs with substantial local clan autonomy; merchants, craft interests and military leaders also influence public decisions. Ordinary residents include workers, families, traders, scholars and people of other species, not a uniform warrior caste.

Dragon and ancestor worship, winter hospitality, practical craft and collective memories of the founding give the country a recognizable culture. Households vary in belief, wealth and conduct. The local economy combines advanced metallurgy, magical raw materials, livestock, trade and many ordinary services. Drakenspire is a friendly sovereign partner of Glowhaven, with authorized portal travel and strong links between its materials and Glowhaven's enchanted-goods industry. A visitor's connections abroad do not make them an officer of the hold.

Daizen Iwatsugu is the current elected Jarl. The three great capital clans maintain a fragile peace marked by bitter rivalries, contested obligations and anxiety about succession. Ordinary commerce, households and friendship continue within that tension. The sovereign partnership with Glowhaven remains intact.
Drakenspire.hiddenInfo: Local interests differ over repairs, resource access, trade and the cost of winter readiness. Established clans, newer households and merchants can disagree without any side being a single-minded villain. Use this civic affiliation for actual local residents without a more specific primary institution; foreign visitors keep their own affiliations. National membership does not imply access to private offices, sacred remains or every working site.

Asterveil.name: Asterveil
Asterveil.basicInfo: Asterveil is the civic community of the inhabited sky archipelago, centered on the small Asterveil Canopy settlement. Fae households and residents of other peoples cultivate gardens, make fragrances and tools, carry freight and support fieldwork. A household assembly appoints rotating stewards for practical duties; the realm is independent and cooperates with Glowhaven through agreed travel and exchange. Citizenship does not make all wild creatures allies or make every resident a guide. Use this affiliation for local residents without a narrower organization; visiting academy members keep their actual affiliation. Sakuya Tomonari is the current rotating steward for household field agreements. The community allowed Glowhaven to build its portal; this does not make it a Glowhaven province.
Asterveil.hiddenInfo: Stewards disagree about collecting pressure, freight costs and which surveys deserve scarce local help. Show actual people’s positions and evidence rather than a universal fae consensus. A real agreement can settle a dispute. The four regional wilderness bands are not four factions or social castes.

The Great Sage's Court.name: The Great Sage's Court
The Great Sage's Court.basicInfo:
The Great Sage's Court is the working household and administrative service supporting Ilyra Stillglass and Glowhaven's government. It includes attendants, public clerks, court advisers, messengers, transit staff, research liaisons and people entrusted with defined duties. It is distinct from the larger elected governing council and from the Conclave of Archons. Service at court grants the authority of the actual office, not the Great Sage's personal powers.
The court processes appointments, petitions, official communication, expedition authorization and controlled portal access. An enrolled student's legitimate study, approved trade, court duty or credible noble sponsorship can support a passage request. A real official must approve and issue the key; a porter, visiting student or friendly acquaintance cannot do so. Ordinary approved passage does not require a personal audience with Ilyra Stillglass. Once established, valid permission is preserved within scope.
Future court staff can have sharply different competence, loyalties and manner. An attendant may assist the Great Sage's failing sight without knowing every political plan. A transit clerk may authorize routine passage without gaining access to the Evertree's most sensitive work.
The Great Sage's Court.hiddenInfo: The court must keep daily work functioning as Ilyra Stillglass ages and the academies prepare for succession. Some employees prize continuity; others hope a new administration will advance them. Attendants know the assistance they actually provide, while other offices know their own records. Do not broadcast the full extent of the Great Sage's condition, assign one faction-wide conspiracy or turn everyone into an obstructionist. A request should reach a decision once its actual conditions are satisfied.

Wraith Island Prison Administration.name: Wraith Island Prison Administration
Wraith Island Prison Administration.basicInfo:
Wraith Island Prison Administration operates Glowhaven’s offshore prison under the court’s authority. Its officers maintain custody and security; intake staff verify arrivals and release instructions; medical staff treat patients; other workers manage supplies, transport and supervised work. Each role has a limited remit. No ordinary employee can rewrite a conviction or turn a visitor into a prisoner.

Warden Shūgo Katase directs daily operations. Chisato Kurebayashi handles intake and release, Ena Minamori provides medical care, and Akira Oritsu supervises assigned yard work and escorts. Staff can disagree without possessing each other’s authority. Prisoners and lawful visitors are not members of the administration.

The service is expected to keep people secure without treating injury, hunger or exhaustion as punishment. Actual case and property records matter. Release ends the completed term; it does not create replacement belongings or erase unrelated conduct.
Warden Shūgo Katase directs daily operations. Chisato Kurebayashi handles intake and release, Ena Minamori provides medical care, and Akira Oritsu supervises assigned yard work and escorts. Staff can disagree without possessing each other’s powers or judicial authority.
Wraith Island Prison Administration.hiddenInfo: Orders, workload and personal judgment can conflict. An officer may follow procedure fairly, take a bribe or overreach, but wrongdoing requires an actual individual and evidence. Property records and transfer documents can matter without being automatically corrupt. Preserve who knows each case, who holds deposited equipment and the conditions for lawful release. No institutional omniscience, invincible guard or automatic conviction is implied.

Glowhaven Trade Guild.name: Glowhaven Trade Guild
Glowhaven Trade Guild.basicInfo:
Glowhaven Trade Guild is a voluntary association of merchants, stallholders, brokers and carriers. It offers introductions, shared market information, contract advice and mediation for members. It works with harbor, market and court offices but is not the government, a universal shop chain or an authority over every trader. A merchant can operate independently.
Future members may include traveling sellers, import agents, warehouse partners, apprentices and petty rivals. Membership and reputation depend on the actual person and history, not wealth alone. Work can involve delivery, appraisal, commission disputes and stock problems. Terms, fees and payments must be established rather than invented as automatic dues. The guild can support a court application for legitimate trade passage; it cannot mint its own official portal keys.
Glowhaven Trade Guild.hiddenInfo: Members disagree over pricing, credit, access and the interests of small stalls versus larger businesses. Some value reliable dealing more than profit; others look for loopholes. A guarantee covers its actual contract, not all of a member's conduct. Preserve real debts, invoices and disputed ownership. No guild-wide criminal secret, fixed rank ladder or compulsory membership is established.

Glowhaven Artisans' Guild.name: Glowhaven Artisans' Guild
Glowhaven Artisans' Guild.basicInfo:
Glowhaven Artisans' Guild is a voluntary professional network for craft workers, repairers and enchantment specialists. Smiths, joiners, leatherworkers, jewellers, alchemists and practical enchanters can exchange referrals, workspace knowledge and advice while retaining independent shops and methods. The guild does not own every workshop or make all enchanted goods magitech.
Its practical influence comes from workmanship, repeat customers and professional trust. Future members can seek apprentices, materials, a fair commission or recognition for a method. A referral is not a free item, a guaranteed result or proof of mastery. Clients own entrusted goods unless actual terms say otherwise. Prices and repair scope are agreed before work, and failed or completed commissions remain consequences rather than resetting on each visit.
Glowhaven Artisans' Guild.hiddenInfo: Craft workers argue about credit, standards, dangerous shortcuts and who gets paid for the least glamorous labor. A respected member can be vain or unreliable; an abrasive independent may do excellent work. Resolve the actual defect or dispute through evidence and the people concerned. No compulsory unified curriculum, mechanical crafting rank or automatic equipment-upgrade system is implied.

House Goldbarrow.name: House Goldbarrow
House Goldbarrow.basicInfo:
House Goldbarrow is the noble household associated with House Goldbarrow Estate in Glowhaven. Its household members, employees and actual agents have different standing and duties. Hanae Goldbarrow manages routine purchases and receives tradespeople at the estate. The house participates in the city's property, patronage and commercial life without representing every noble family.
Future relatives, retainers, advisers and hired specialists belong here only when the relationship is established. A visitor, tenant, customer or worker on one commission is not automatically a household member. Noble connections can support a court request but are not a portal key or universal immunity. Household wealth does not make every relative a combat expert or every servant a secret spy.
House Goldbarrow.hiddenInfo: Practical expenditure, reputation and personal ambition can pull in different directions. Hanae Goldbarrow values useful estimates more than elaborate flattery; other actual members may disagree. Do not invent a succession feud, criminal enterprise or relative simply to manufacture drama. Particular promises, debts and favors should remain tied to the people who made them.

Drakenspire Clan Assembly.name: Drakenspire Clan Assembly
Drakenspire Clan Assembly.basicInfo:
The forum in which Drakenspire’s clan chiefs elect the Jarl, debate shared obligations and hear cross-clan commitments. Clan Iwatsugu, Clan Yukinose and Clan Arashimine dominate the capital’s present rivalries without becoming the only kin groups in the country. Noboru Ōhira records what was actually agreed. Witnesses, merchants and military personnel can speak or influence a matter without automatically becoming electoral chiefs.

Daizen Iwatsugu coordinates national decisions as elected Jarl. Ordinary local disputes belong first to the appropriate office, including Setsuna Takigawa’s Judgment House. The assembly is a working institution, not a permanent election ceremony or a second hereditary royal house.
Drakenspire Clan Assembly.hiddenInfo: The peace is fragile. Each great clan believes another could use the aging Jarl’s departure to entrench itself. Chiefs bargain, stall, threaten withdrawal from private commitments and court witnesses, but no succession is automatically won by a surname, duel, marriage or private promise. Keep public testimony, a proposal, an agreement and an implemented decision distinct.

Drakenspire Hold Guard.name: Drakenspire Hold Guard
Drakenspire Hold Guard.basicInfo:
Drakenspire’s national public-order and defense force, commanded by Gōki Shishido under the elected Jarl. Reina Tachibana oversees Upper Ward inspections; Kensaku Honjō handles the lower gate and Yūsuke Ebina the Whitepass watch. Hayate Mizusawa is an ordinary upper-gate guard. Their actual posts and authority differ.

The force protects gates, roads and residents, enforces the ban on street dueling and responds to concrete threats. It is not a chief’s private collection service, a branch of Glowhaven’s elite force or a source of unrestricted access for visitors.
Drakenspire Hold Guard.hiddenInfo: Gōki Shishido wants a force that can survive the succession without fragmenting by clan. Reina Tachibana wants his future office and is documenting selective exceptions. Their disagreements are real but do not make all guards corrupt or every disputed order lawful. A person’s private family ties do not override their service responsibilities.

Keepers of the Crescent.name: Keepers of the Crescent
Keepers of the Crescent.basicInfo:
Custodians of Drakenspire’s dragon-and-ancestor observances, sacred remains, sanctuary stores and memorial records. First Keeper Seika Amatsune leads the institution. Keishin Tōdō directs records and conservation; Miharu Sakuraba performs skilled care on the remains and their supports. Their work includes public ceremonies and ordinary maintenance.

They hold religious custody and make decisions within that remit. They cannot command Rovakthuun, identify his lair or promise a divine response. Visitors may be respectful without professing belief. Rare genuine dragon gifts are held and assessed under custody, not handed out to anyone who prays.
Keepers of the Crescent.hiddenInfo: Seika Amatsune favors a limited public-benefit use of one held unfertilized dragon gift. Keishin Tōdō values context and evidence; Miharu Sakuraba wants conservation labor treated fairly. They can disagree sincerely about sacred material. Their personal knowledge is bounded by their actual records and experience, not by narrator lore.

Clan Iwatsugu.name: Clan Iwatsugu
Clan Iwatsugu.basicInfo:
One of Drakenspire’s three great capital clans, historically involved in stonework, foundations and settlement works. Its chief, Daizen Iwatsugu, is also the elected Jarl; his granddaughter Tsubaki Iwatsugu administers the household and works commitments while he governs. His grandnephew Shūhei Iwatsugu surveys routes and seeks an expedition reputation. These are individual responsibilities, not hereditary professions for every member. Smaller kin households and associates have trades, homes and loyalties of their own.
