Mizuhara Lakeside Upbringing.traitNarrativeEffects: Your early life followed ferries, fish markets and changing lake weather around Mizuhara. You learned to judge a crossing and listen to people whose livelihood depends on the water.

Koganedai Castle-Town Upbringing.name: Koganedai Castle-Town Upbringing
Koganedai Castle-Town Upbringing.description: You grew up around Koganedai’s busy workshops, market terraces and household offices. Comparing workmanship and hearing competing prices became ordinary habits. Start with +1 Trade.
Koganedai Castle-Town Upbringing.traitNarrativeEffects: You grew up around Koganedai’s busy workshops, market terraces and household offices. Comparing workmanship and hearing competing prices became ordinary habits.

Akitsuhara Farming Village.name: Akitsuhara Farming Village
Akitsuhara Farming Village.description: You grew up among shared irrigation, seasonal harvests and neighbors who noticed an unattended task. You learned to read the ground and work around weather. Start with +1 survival.
Akitsuhara Farming Village.traitNarrativeEffects: You grew up among shared irrigation, seasonal harvests and neighbors who noticed an unattended task. You learned to read the ground and work around weather.

Reed-Valley Childhood.name: Reed-Valley Childhood
Reed-Valley Childhood.description: You grew up among bamboo groves, mill paths and narrow river crossings. Quiet footing and attention to an obscured approach came from ordinary travel. Start with +1 Perception.
Reed-Valley Childhood.traitNarrativeEffects: You grew up among bamboo groves, mill paths and narrow river crossings. Quiet footing and attention to an obscured approach came from ordinary travel.

Northern Pass Household.name: Northern Pass Household
Northern Pass Household.description: Your household made a living along Akitsuhara’s colder passes. Planning fuel, shelter and a return route mattered more than the appearance of an easy journey. Start with +1 survival.
Northern Pass Household.traitNarrativeEffects: Your household made a living along Akitsuhara’s colder passes. Planning fuel, shelter and a return route mattered more than the appearance of an easy journey.

Household Service Upbringing.name: Household Service Upbringing
Household Service Upbringing.description: You grew up around the practical work behind a territorial household: deliveries, formal visitors, records and rooms that had to be ready. You learned the uses and limits of courtesy. Start with +1 Etiquette.
Household Service Upbringing.traitNarrativeEffects: You grew up around the practical work behind a territorial household: deliveries, formal visitors, records and rooms that had to be ready. You learned the uses and limits of courtesy.

Dojo Neighborhood Upbringing.name: Dojo Neighborhood Upbringing
Dojo Neighborhood Upbringing.description: The sound of practice was part of your childhood. Watching corrections, cleaning a floor and helping with equipment taught you to notice how people move and learn. Start with +1 Insight.
Dojo Neighborhood Upbringing.traitNarrativeEffects: The sound of practice was part of your childhood. Watching corrections, cleaning a floor and helping with equipment taught you to notice how people move and learn.

Shrine-Court Upbringing.name: Shrine-Court Upbringing
Shrine-Court Upbringing.description: You grew up near a working shrine and its stream of ordinary visitors. You learned how a ceremony, a private worry and a practical request can occupy the same courtyard. Start with +1 Etiquette.
Shrine-Court Upbringing.traitNarrativeEffects: You grew up near a working shrine and its stream of ordinary visitors. You learned how a ceremony, a private worry and a practical request can occupy the same courtyard.

Road-Theatre Upbringing.name: Road-Theatre Upbringing
Road-Theatre Upbringing.description: You grew up among traveling stages, costume bundles and audiences that changed at every stop. Timing, listening and making a small performance carry became familiar skills. Start with +1 performance.
Road-Theatre Upbringing.traitNarrativeEffects: You grew up among traveling stages, costume bundles and audiences that changed at every stop. Timing, listening and making a small performance carry became familiar skills.

Drakenspire Forge Neighborhood.name: Drakenspire Forge Neighborhood
Drakenspire Forge Neighborhood.description: You grew up among Drakenspire’s workshops and winter deliveries. You learned to compare a repair, a bargain and a piece of workmanship without mistaking ornament for quality. Start with +1 Trade.
Drakenspire Forge Neighborhood.traitNarrativeEffects: You grew up among Drakenspire’s workshops and winter deliveries. You learned to compare a repair, a bargain and a piece of workmanship without mistaking ornament for quality.

Drakenspire Caravan Upbringing.name: Drakenspire Caravan Upbringing
Drakenspire Caravan Upbringing.description: Your early life followed mountain supplies, snowbound delays and nights in shared lodges. You learned to prepare for the stretch between safe hearths. Start with +1 survival.
Drakenspire Caravan Upbringing.traitNarrativeEffects: Your early life followed mountain supplies, snowbound delays and nights in shared lodges. You learned to prepare for the stretch between safe hearths.

Asterveil Canopy Household.name: Asterveil Canopy Household
Asterveil Canopy Household.description: You grew up among Asterveil’s household assembly, landing paths and shared gardens. Recognizing a neighbor’s concern and finding a workable agreement were everyday skills. Start with +1 Insight.
Asterveil Canopy Household.traitNarrativeEffects: You grew up among Asterveil’s household assembly, landing paths and shared gardens. Recognizing a neighbor’s concern and finding a workable agreement were everyday skills.

Asterveil Field-Shelter Upbringing.name: Asterveil Field-Shelter Upbringing
Asterveil Field-Shelter Upbringing.description: You grew up around guides, conservatory work and careful journeys between sky-island shelters. You learned to notice a route’s changing conditions before committing to it. Start with +1 Perception.
Asterveil Field-Shelter Upbringing.traitNarrativeEffects: You grew up around guides, conservatory work and careful journeys between sky-island shelters. You learned to notice a route’s changing conditions before committing to it.

Veteran Infantry Soldier.name: Veteran Infantry Soldier
Veteran Infantry Soldier.description: You served through a campaign: long marches, cramped camps and the discipline of holding a line when enthusiasm had gone. You still judge a plan by what ordinary tired people can carry out. Start with +1 Force Combat.
Veteran Infantry Soldier.traitNarrativeEffects: You served through a campaign: long marches, cramped camps and the discipline of holding a line when enthusiasm had gone. You still judge a plan by what ordinary tired people can carry out.

Veteran Skirmisher.name: Veteran Skirmisher
Veteran Skirmisher.description: You learned to move under pressure, choose an approach and leave a bad position before pride made the decision. Old service shaped your timing more than your present occupation. Start with +1 Finesse Combat.
Veteran Skirmisher.traitNarrativeEffects: You learned to move under pressure, choose an approach and leave a bad position before pride made the decision. Old service shaped your timing more than your present occupation.

Former Watch Officer.name: Former Watch Officer
Former Watch Officer.description: You have broken up arguments, watched difficult doors and learned how quickly a crowded street can turn dangerous. Familiar procedure and a steady guard are part of your past. Start with +1 Guarded Combat.
Former Watch Officer.traitNarrativeEffects: You have broken up arguments, watched difficult doors and learned how quickly a crowded street can turn dangerous. Familiar procedure and a steady guard are part of your past.

Former Guild Adventurer.name: Former Guild Adventurer
Former Guild Adventurer.description: You have taken commissions, worked alongside unfamiliar partners and learned the difference between an attractive notice and a feasible journey. Something brought you to a fresh beginning. Start with +1 survival.
Former Guild Adventurer.traitNarrativeEffects: You have taken commissions, worked alongside unfamiliar partners and learned the difference between an attractive notice and a feasible journey. Something brought you to a fresh beginning.

Former Monster Hunter.name: Former Monster Hunter
Former Monster Hunter.description: You have followed signs, waited through poor weather and discovered why a confident description is less useful than a clear track. Preparation still shapes how you read a place. Start with +1 Perception.
Former Monster Hunter.traitNarrativeEffects: You have followed signs, waited through poor weather and discovered why a confident description is less useful than a clear track. Preparation still shapes how you read a place.

Expedition Survivor.name: Expedition Survivor
Expedition Survivor.description: A difficult expedition taught you to manage injury, limited supplies and frightened companions. You remember the small practical decisions that made returning possible. Start with +1 Medicine.
Expedition Survivor.traitNarrativeEffects: A difficult expedition taught you to manage injury, limited supplies and frightened companions. You remember the small practical decisions that made returning possible.

Former Mercenary.name: Former Mercenary
Former Mercenary.description: You once sold your fighting work, shared camp with people whose loyalties differed and learned to ask exactly what a patron meant by protection. Start with +1 Force Combat.
Former Mercenary.traitNarrativeEffects: You once sold your fighting work, shared camp with people whose loyalties differed and learned to ask exactly what a patron meant by protection.

Former Arena Fighter.name: Former Arena Fighter
Former Arena Fighter.description: You have fought before a crowd, recovered from public defeat and learned how to keep your movement controlled when an audience wants a spectacle. Start with +1 Finesse Combat.
Former Arena Fighter.traitNarrativeEffects: You have fought before a crowd, recovered from public defeat and learned how to keep your movement controlled when an audience wants a spectacle.

Former Field Medic.name: Former Field Medic
Former Field Medic.description: You have worked beside exhausted travelers or fighters, triaged an injury and cared for someone without promising a miracle. Those habits remain useful beyond the field. Start with +1 Medicine.
Former Field Medic.traitNarrativeEffects: You have worked beside exhausted travelers or fighters, triaged an injury and cared for someone without promising a miracle. Those habits remain useful beyond the field.

Former Bandit.name: Former Bandit
Former Bandit.description: You once lived by a road crew’s threats, stolen goods and unreliable loyalties. Whether you regret it, justify it or simply left, you know how a nervous lookout behaves. Start with +1 Stealth.
Former Bandit.traitNarrativeEffects: You once lived by a road crew’s threats, stolen goods and unreliable loyalties. Whether you regret it, justify it or simply left, you know how a nervous lookout behaves.

Smuggling Past.name: Smuggling Past
Smuggling Past.description: You have carried goods through unwanted attention, trusted the wrong handover and learned to recognize a price that conceals somebody else’s risk. Start with +1 Trade.
Smuggling Past.traitNarrativeEffects: You have carried goods through unwanted attention, trusted the wrong handover and learned to recognize a price that conceals somebody else’s risk.

Former Burglar.name: Former Burglar
Former Burglar.description: You have studied occupied buildings, quiet approaches and the habits of people who assume their belongings are safe. Your present use of that knowledge is yours to decide. Start with +1 Stealth.
Former Burglar.traitNarrativeEffects: You have studied occupied buildings, quiet approaches and the habits of people who assume their belongings are safe. Your present use of that knowledge is yours to decide.

Former Confidence Trickster.name: Former Confidence Trickster
Former Confidence Trickster.description: You have sold a convincing account, watched a mark hesitate and learned how a pleasing detail can distract from the real question. Start with +1 Deception.
Former Confidence Trickster.traitNarrativeEffects: You have sold a convincing account, watched a mark hesitate and learned how a pleasing detail can distract from the real question.

Time Served.name: Time Served
Time Served.description: You have lived through confinement, learned the informal rules of shared quarters and noticed how people negotiate a small amount of freedom. That experience is in your past. Start with +1 Insight.
Time Served.traitNarrativeEffects: You have lived through confinement, learned the informal rules of shared quarters and noticed how people negotiate a small amount of freedom. That experience is in your past.

Iwatsugu Clan Upbringing.name: Iwatsugu Clan Upbringing
Iwatsugu Clan Upbringing.description: You grew up as an ordinary member of Clan Iwatsugu in Drakenspire, around household obligations, stonework and arguments about which shared repair should come first. Your own branch and family life can be defined as part of your story. Start with +1 Trade.
Iwatsugu Clan Upbringing.traitNarrativeEffects: You grew up as an ordinary member of Clan Iwatsugu in Drakenspire, around household obligations, stonework and arguments about which shared repair should come first. Your own branch and family life can be defined as part of your story.

Yukinose Clan Upbringing.name: Yukinose Clan Upbringing
Yukinose Clan Upbringing.description: You grew up as an ordinary member of Clan Yukinose in Drakenspire, among winter provisions, carrier news and hospitality that could carry an obligation. Your place in that large household leaves room for your own ambitions. Start with +1 survival.
Yukinose Clan Upbringing.traitNarrativeEffects: You grew up as an ordinary member of Clan Yukinose in Drakenspire, among winter provisions, carrier news and hospitality that could carry an obligation. Your place in that large household leaves room for your own ambitions.

Arashimine Clan Upbringing.name: Arashimine Clan Upbringing
Arashimine Clan Upbringing.description: You grew up as an ordinary member of Clan Arashimine in Drakenspire, around equipment trials, service commitments and exacting practice. Household expectations are familiar, even if you chose a different direction. Start with +1 Guarded Combat.
Arashimine Clan Upbringing.traitNarrativeEffects: You grew up as an ordinary member of Clan Arashimine in Drakenspire, around equipment trials, service commitments and exacting practice. Household expectations are familiar, even if you chose a different direction.

Crescent Sanctuary Upbringing.name: Crescent Sanctuary Upbringing
Crescent Sanctuary Upbringing.description: You grew up around Drakenspire’s dragon observances, ancestral stories and the practical work of receiving pilgrims. You learned to recognize a solemn occasion and the ordinary person who needs help beside it. Start with +1 Etiquette.
Crescent Sanctuary Upbringing.traitNarrativeEffects: You grew up around Drakenspire’s dragon observances, ancestral stories and the practical work of receiving pilgrims. You learned to recognize a solemn occasion and the ordinary person who needs help beside it.

Mountain Herding Household.name: Mountain Herding Household
Mountain Herding Household.description: Your Drakenspire household raised goats or sheep along difficult slopes. You learned to read an animal’s unease, judge a shelter and bring a wandering charge home. Start with +1 Animal Handling.
Mountain Herding Household.traitNarrativeEffects: Your Drakenspire household raised goats or sheep along difficult slopes. You learned to read an animal’s unease, judge a shelter and bring a wandering charge home.

Winter Stores Community.name: Winter Stores Community
Winter Stores Community.description: You grew up around Drakenspire’s shared stores, distribution queues and neighbors making supplies last. Counting fairly and noticing a strained household became everyday habits. Start with +1 Insight.
Winter Stores Community.traitNarrativeEffects: You grew up around Drakenspire’s shared stores, distribution queues and neighbors making supplies last. Counting fairly and noticing a strained household became everyday habits.

Mountain Rescue Upbringing.name: Mountain Rescue Upbringing
Mountain Rescue Upbringing.description: People in your Drakenspire household helped bring lost or injured travelers back from the passes. You learned to watch conditions, prepare a line and take a small warning seriously. Start with +1 Perception.
Mountain Rescue Upbringing.traitNarrativeEffects: People in your Drakenspire household helped bring lost or injured travelers back from the passes. You learned to watch conditions, prepare a line and take a small warning seriously.

Self-Taught Spell Experimenter.name: Self-Taught Spell Experimenter
Self-Taught Spell Experimenter.description: Before formal instruction, you spent spare evenings taking simple spells apart, changing one detail and finding out why the result misbehaved. You learned to keep experiments small and notice which change mattered. Start with +1 Spellcraft.
Self-Taught Spell Experimenter.traitNarrativeEffects: You have experience with small personal spell experiments and the patience to test one change at a time. This is practical familiarity, not an academic qualification or a ready-made spell.

Outfit — Phoenix Wing uniform.name: Outfit — Phoenix Wing uniform
Outfit — Phoenix Wing uniform.description: Phoenix Wing Academy’s crimson red uniform with an embroidered a phoenix bird with spread wings crest; choose an individual cut and accessories.
Outfit — Phoenix Wing uniform.traitNarrativeEffects: In the final portrait brief, explicitly describe Phoenix Wing Academy clothing: substantial crimson red cloth panels and one embroidered pictorial a phoenix bird with spread wings crest on breast, collar or shoulder. Use a student cut, or an instructor’s coat/robes if the actual character is faculty. No lettering. Preserve the person and selected accessories. This is a cosmetic outfit, not membership, employment, inventory or a mechanical bonus.

Outfit — Hydra Head uniform.name: Outfit — Hydra Head uniform
Outfit — Hydra Head uniform.description: Hydra Head Academy’s violet purple uniform with an embroidered a many-headed hydra crest; choose an individual cut and accessories.
Outfit — Hydra Head uniform.traitNarrativeEffects: In the final portrait brief, explicitly describe Hydra Head Academy clothing: substantial violet purple cloth panels and one embroidered pictorial a many-headed hydra crest on breast, collar or shoulder. Use a student cut, or an instructor’s coat/robes if the actual character is faculty. No lettering. Preserve the person and selected accessories. This is a cosmetic outfit, not membership, employment, inventory or a mechanical bonus.

Outfit — Gryffin Tail uniform.name: Outfit — Gryffin Tail uniform
Outfit — Gryffin Tail uniform.description: Gryffin Tail Academy’s cyan blue uniform with an embroidered a winged gryffin crest; choose an individual cut and accessories.
Outfit — Gryffin Tail uniform.traitNarrativeEffects: In the final portrait brief, explicitly describe Gryffin Tail Academy clothing: substantial cyan blue cloth panels and one embroidered pictorial a winged gryffin crest on breast, collar or shoulder. Use a student cut, or an instructor’s coat/robes if the actual character is faculty. No lettering. Preserve the person and selected accessories. This is a cosmetic outfit, not membership, employment, inventory or a mechanical bonus.

Outfit — Dragon Hoard uniform.name: Outfit — Dragon Hoard uniform
Outfit — Dragon Hoard uniform.description: Dragon Hoard Academy’s yellow and gold uniform with an embroidered a dragon crest; choose an individual cut and accessories.
Outfit — Dragon Hoard uniform.traitNarrativeEffects: In the final portrait brief, explicitly describe Dragon Hoard Academy clothing: substantial yellow and gold cloth panels and one embroidered pictorial a dragon crest on breast, collar or shoulder. Use a student cut, or an instructor’s coat/robes if the actual character is faculty. No lettering. Preserve the person and selected accessories. This is a cosmetic outfit, not membership, employment, inventory or a mechanical bonus.

Angling Basics.name: Angling Basics
Angling Basics.description: Familiar with rigging a rod, feeling a bite and bringing a small fish safely to hand.
Angling Basics.traitNarrativeEffects: Familiar with rigging a rod, feeling a bite and bringing a small fish safely to hand.

Rare Fish on the Line.name: Rare Fish on the Line
Rare Fish on the Line.description: Something unusual is pulling at your fishing line. Keep its movements in mind: patience, a change of angle or a well-timed pull may bring it within reach. You can also let it go.
Rare Fish on the Line.traitNarrativeEffects: Something unusual is pulling at your fishing line. Keep its movements in mind: patience, a change of angle or a well-timed pull may bring it within reach. You can also let it go.

Fishing Starter Kit.name: Fishing Starter Kit
Fishing Starter Kit.description: An ash rod with reusable spinner, eight portions of bait and a waterproof field ledger for a quiet afternoon beside the water.
Fishing Starter Kit.traitNarrativeEffects: An ash rod with reusable spinner, eight portions of bait and a waterproof field ledger for a quiet afternoon beside the water.

Species & Ancestry.name: Species & Ancestry
Species & Ancestry.description: Choose one ancestry, with the listed attributes, skills and resource capacity. Individual anatomy and culture still matter. Profession, personality and magical affinity remain separate choices.

Beastfolk Form.name: Beastfolk Form
Beastfolk Form.description: Optional — for Beastfolk or a mixed-ancestry character with beastfolk heritage. Choose one mostly human form or skip and describe your own. Rare more animal-like bodies require explicit direction.

Fae Form.name: Fae Form
Fae Form.description: Optional — for Fae or a mixed-ancestry character with fae heritage. Choose one starting body plan or skip and describe a coherent individual blend. These are appearance examples, not rigid subraces.

Fae Stature.name: Fae Stature
Fae Stature.description: Optional — select a fae adult height or skip. Short fae keep adult faces and proportions. Height grants no power or age change.

Origin & Upbringing.name: Origin & Upbringing
Origin & Upbringing.description: Optionally choose one place or community that shaped your early life. Each background adds +1 to a useful skill; your present circumstances are yours to establish.

Past Experience.name: Past Experience
Past Experience.description: Optional: choose one part of your earlier working life, service or difficult history. It adds a small practiced skill while leaving your present direction open.

Primary Aptitude.name: Primary Aptitude
Primary Aptitude.description: Choose your strongest aptitude: +5, normally 15 from base 10. Force covers physical power, resilience, and guarded fighting; Finesse covers coordination, precision, and timing. Logic, Passion, Empathy, and Intuition support the listed magical disciplines. This is capability, not a personality or class. The choice also supplies common foundational skills at level 0.

Secondary Aptitude.name: Secondary Aptitude
Secondary Aptitude.description: Choose a different supporting aptitude: +3, normally 13. A spellblade can pair a physical and magical aptitude; a dedicated caster can pair two magical aptitudes. Other attributes remain 10. A matching primary is excluded. No attribute is required for the basic Health, Mana or Stamina pool.

Natural Magical Affinity.name: Natural Magical Affinity
Natural Magical Affinity.description: Optional — choose zero to three natural affinities, or leave this section empty for no innate affinity. Affinity eases learning; it grants no discipline or spell. Starting Magical Study is separate, and other disciplines can be learned through study or mentorship. Space and Time are unavailable at creation.

Starting Magical Study.name: Starting Magical Study
Starting Magical Study.description: Optional — choose up to two entries, or skip. Physical Foundations grants +1 Force and +1 Finesse without magic. Each magical study starts its discipline at skill level 3 and grants its two listed introductory techniques. Studies need not match affinities. Space and Time are unavailable at creation.

Practical Training.name: Practical Training
Practical Training.description: Choose one or two distinct practiced approaches. Force, Finesse, and Guarded Training each grant the matching combat skill at level 3; Scholarly Practice grants spellcraft 2 and investigation 1. Each option represents separate prior practice. Weapon and unarmed methods follow actual training and equipment, not one forced attribute for every sword. These choices grant no attribute points or automatic advanced abilities.

Profession & Useful Skills.name: Profession & Useful Skills
Profession & Useful Skills.description: Optional — choose one prior profession or practical background. Each grants +2 in its main skill and +1 in a supporting skill. These are starting experiences, not current employment, official licences, owned workplaces or free professional equipment.

Special Talent.name: Special Talent
Special Talent.description: Optional — choose up to two unusual gifts, blessings or exceptional aptitudes, or skip. Benefits are substantial but bounded; stronger gifts have the listed trade-offs. A granted discipline or technique is learned as stated without adding an affinity. No Space, Time, automatic authority or compulsory deity relationship is included.

Starting Equipment.name: Starting Equipment
Starting Equipment.description: Choose one basic casting, martial or practical kit, or Hand-Casting Practice for no extra item. It is independent of your training style. Ordinary tools, clothing and remembered techniques stay distinct; a kit grants only its listed items once.

Temperament.name: Temperament
Temperament.description: Optional — choose up to two tendencies or skip. Each grants its listed small attribute and skill benefit. Actual speech, feelings and decisions remain yours.

First Impression.name: First Impression
First Impression.description: Optional — skip this category if you prefer: how a stranger might initially read your visible presentation. Purely narrative. Actual circumstances and individual NPC judgment always matter.

Personal Motivation.name: Personal Motivation
Personal Motivation.description: Optional — skip this category if you prefer: what the character may be seeking. This creates motivation, not a mandatory quest, background tragedy, debt, relationship, status, or obligation.

Personal Complication.name: Personal Complication
Personal Complication.description: Optional — skip this category if you prefer: one realistic personal difficulty for stories and relationships. Narrative only: no mandatory penalty, trauma, or automatic player action.

Appearance Builder.name: Appearance Builder
Appearance Builder.description: Optional — choose up to one detail in each group, or skip any or all and write your own appearance. Hair, eyes, skin, build and outfit are visual choices. Portrait style, framing, camera and backdrop have their own optional sections below. Written appearance takes precedence. Styling does not grant equipment or membership.

subcategories.name: Hair Color — choose up to one
Hair Style — choose up to one
Eye Color — choose up to one
Skin Tone — choose up to one

Accessories & Outer Layers.name: Accessories & Outer Layers
Accessories & Outer Layers.description: Optional — add up to four compatible visual details over your selected outfit, or skip. Hats, outer layers, glasses and jewelry are appearance choices. They grant no equipment bonuses, possessions, official insignia or magical powers. Avoid incompatible duplicate hats or layers unless explicitly intended.

Portrait Style.name: Portrait Style
Portrait Style.description: Optional — skip for a detailed 2D fantasy-anime character illustration with expressive drawn features and clean facial shading. Alternative styles change the picture, not your abilities.

Portrait Framing.name: Portrait Framing
Portrait Framing.description: Optional — skip for a hip-up portrait showing the full waist, both hips and the top of the thighs. Choose Waist-up for a tighter crop. Explicit alternatives take priority.

Portrait Camera.name: Portrait Camera
Portrait Camera.description: Optional — choose a viewpoint or skip. Default uses a natural eye-level or three-quarter view. Eccentric Choices offers dramatic and unusual perspectives; keep the actual face and anatomy coherent.

Portrait Background.name: Portrait Background
Portrait Background.description: Optional — choose a picture backdrop or skip for a fitting setting from your opening. A background styles the portrait and does not move your character.

Archon.name: Archon
Archon.description: An Archon publicly represents one of Glowhaven City's academies and serves on the Conclave of Archons. Archons are exceptionally capable, but are not automatically hostile; each has an individual personality and agenda.

Headmaster.name: Headmaster
Headmaster.description: A headmaster runs an academy's school system and day-to-day operations. This institutional role does not determine personality or combat ability.

Teacher.name: Teacher
Teacher.description: A teacher works at one of Glowhaven City's academies and has an individual area of expertise. Instructors vary in temperament, experience, and combat capability.

Student.name: Student
Student.description: A student studies at one of Glowhaven City's academies. Students are individuals with different experience and abilities; being a student does not make someone helpless or define their personality.

Resident.name: Resident
Resident.description: A named resident, professional, officer, or visitor outside the academy role categories. Actual job, training, abilities, level, and temperament come from the individual's record; this type grants no shared powers or personality.

Great Sage.name: Great Sage
Great Sage.description: The elected ruler and steward of Glowhaven's Evertree weave. The incumbent's actual abilities, age, knowledge, and condition remain individual authored facts rather than universal type bonuses.

Wild Beast.name: Wild Beast
Wild Beast.description: An animal or local wild creature. Use actual size, behavior, abilities, and danger rather than human motives. A moss-backed boar can charge and retreat; it has no automatic spells, speech, or magical immunity.

Mana Beast.name: Mana Beast
Mana Beast.description: A soul-bearing magical creature. Actual abilities and behavior belong to the individual; the category grants no universal spell, speech, or immunity.

Academy Staff.name: Academy Staff
Academy Staff.description: Employees who make an academy function: attendants, kitchen workers, groundskeepers, technicians and caretakers. Give each an actual job and ordinary responsibilities. They know their workplace and its practical problems, not every private faculty decision. Some are trained mages or fighters; others depend on tools, procedures and colleagues. Helpful, resentful and self-interested individuals all belong to this type. Employment does not grant unrestricted records, court authority or a desire to accompany the player.

Court Official.name: Court Official
Court Official.description: Clerks, appointed officers and civil administrators working within a particular court remit. They can explain the process they actually handle, ask for relevant information and issue only what their office is authorized to issue. They have personal priorities and differing loyalties. An official might be kind, pompous, harried or corrupt without being omniscient. Their position supplies neither automatic combat mastery nor immunity from scrutiny. Use existing named office holders before inventing another one.

City Guard.name: City Guard
City Guard.description: Trained personnel responsible for public safety, patrols and ordinary law enforcement. They recognize immediate threats, call for support and use proportionate force when possible. A patrol can give directions, receive a complaint, separate combatants or make an evidence-based arrest; it cannot pronounce every sentence on the spot. Individual experience and temperament vary. They are capable adults with learned magic and practical training, not disposable obstacles scaled to flatter a new student.

Elite Operative.name: Elite Operative
Elite Operative.description: Experienced members of the Great Sage's exceptional service, selected for difficult protective, military, investigative or diplomatic work. Define the individual's assignment and methods: an envoy need not perform like an assault specialist. They act on actual orders and information, protect sensitive matters and can negotiate or withdraw. Their competence merits serious respect, but a service badge does not make them omniscient, universally loved or above all law.

Prison Officer.name: Prison Officer
Prison Officer.description: Custody, security and authorized transport personnel at Wraith Island Prison. Their actual post determines keys, access and responsibility. They maintain counts, searches, escorts and emergency procedures; an individual can be decent, brutal, diligent or negligent. Prison employment is distinct from being an inmate, visitor, contractor or sentenced worker. Combat ability, access and susceptibility to bribery belong to the individual. They do not confiscate or restore property merely because a narration mentions a search.

Merchant.name: Merchant
Merchant.description: People earning a living by buying and selling goods. Give a merchant a real stock, market, supplier relationship and reason for their prices. They may bargain, offer samples, seek repairs or refuse bad credit; they are neither universal quest dispensers nor automatic frauds. A quoted price is not a completed sale. Their knowledge follows their trade and contacts. Ownership, payment and delivery need actual agreement and supported state changes.

Artisan.name: Artisan
Artisan.description: Makers and repairers with a particular craft, workshop and trained method. Some enchant by hand; others use conventional tools or integrated magitech. Their competence follows experience, materials and the job, not a promise to repair everything instantly. Good scene pressures include a difficult commission, missing part, awkward customer or contested credit. They can discuss a fault before accepting work. Tools, samples and customers' property remain with their actual owners.

Healer.name: Healer
Healer.description: Practitioners of healing, medical care or both, with individual training, supplies and limits. They assess an actual condition rather than promising a perfect reset. Treatment can involve rest, mundane care and paid materials as well as magic. An experienced healer is not necessarily a frontline fighter. Healing does not automatically reverse old age, lasting damage or every unusual curse. Preserve the world's resource and medicine rules, informed choices and actual fees.

Researcher.name: Researcher
Researcher.description: Scholars and investigators pursuing a particular question through study, observation and experiment. A researcher can be generous, possessive, reckless, meticulous or mistaken. Their expertise is specific; one scientific field does not reveal all magic, secret history and institutions. Evidence can change their conclusions. Give their work practical materials, an observable test and something they have not solved. Most research remains ordinary work, not a guaranteed catastrophe or a shortcut to forbidden mastery.

Field Guide.name: Field Guide
Field Guide.description: Travelers, scouts and expedition workers who know particular routes, weather, creatures or communities. They can warn about signs of danger, negotiate passage, assess equipment and choose a safer pace. They do not know every hidden site or guarantee the safety of an unfamiliar route. Their fee covers an agreed service rather than permanent party membership. Distinguish an experienced local guide from an enthusiastic beginner and retain each person's actual capabilities.

Noble.name: Noble
Noble.description: People belonging to recognized houses or holding granted titles. Wealth, education, connections and obligations vary; noble status is not an elemental power or personality. They may be generous patrons, anxious heirs, pompous rivals or practical estate managers. Political influence has a scope and a cost. A title alone grants neither court-issued portal keys nor possession of someone else's property. Class prejudice is an individual attitude, not a statement of objective worth.

Performer.name: Performer
Performer.description: Musicians, dancers, actors, illusion entertainers and other working performers. Give them a real audience, craft and livelihood. Their onstage manner can differ from private behavior without concealing a conspiracy. Magical effects used in a show remain limited by actual skill and preparation; applause does not create combat power or intimacy. Scenes can involve rehearsal, a commission, a rivalry, a failed prop or simply an enjoyable evening.

Bandit.name: Bandit
Bandit.description: Robbers or extortionists operating through a particular opportunity and group. Some rely on intimidation and escape, others on preparation or violence. They can bargain, be deceived, lose nerve, surrender or flee when the risk changes. Give warning signs and a practical motive; do not make every road contain an ambush. This is a role rather than a species or damage profile. Captured or reformed individuals remain persistent people, not a renewable reward supply.

Fae.name: Fae
Fae.description: An exceptionally varied people, especially common in Asterveil. Most are short adults with mature proportions; some are human-sized and a few reach seven or eight feet. Most ears are pointed, some rounded. Individual animal features may include moth, butterfly, dragonfly or bird wings; satyr horns and hooves; antlers; feathered parts; or patches of barklike wooden scales. The common winged humanoid form is not universal. Choose a coherent individual body and state its actual height, mature adult face and proportions, ears, hair, eyes, wings and other features in basicInfo and visualDescription. Preserve those details thereafter. Wings do not prove unlimited flight, a passenger-carrying ability or size-changing. Lifespan and talents depend on the authored individual. No compulsory personality or shared damage modifiers apply.

Dragonkin.name: Dragonkin
Dragonkin.description:
Dragonkin are mostly humanoid people of roughly human height, with human faces, dragonlike horns, scales along the sides of their faces and vertical slit pupils. The backs of their hands and arms are scaly, while their palms retain a human appearance. They have thick dragon tails. Individual colors and the amount of visible scaling vary. Scale color is hereditary but carries no inherent magical affinity, rank, personality or moral significance.

Dragonkin can live up to about two hundred years. Drakenspire's populations and the desert populations of Nahlah Qamar's homeland belong to the same species, with regional differences in appearance, ancestry and culture. For visual direction, Drakenspire's populations have broadly European-inspired human features and the established desert populations broadly Middle Eastern-inspired human features; neither is a rigid template for every individual. Regional ancestry does not assign intelligence, temperament or abilities. Dragonkin are people, not lesser dragons or wyverns. Universal wings, breath weapons and elemental resistance are not supplied by this species definition.

Actual learned abilities determine breath, resistance or flight; this broad people category grants none by itself. Their personalities, careers and competence are individual. Do not use the NPC type as a loot-bearing monster template.

Beastfolk.name: Beastfolk
Beastfolk.description: People with animal-associated features whose appearance and physiology depend on the individual lineage. A ram beastfolk, rabbit beastkin and cat-featured person are not interchangeable. Do not infer temperament, intelligence, occupation or attraction from a trait such as horns or ears. Society, learned magic, personal training and relationships matter. This general type supplies no damage modifier or automatic natural weapon; use each actual record.

Domestic Animal.name: Domestic Animal
Domestic Animal.description: Ordinary cats, dogs and other household animals. Their needs include food, shelter, curiosity, comfort and familiar company. They communicate through behavior unless an actual spell changes that. They may be trained, frightened, stubborn or affectionate without understanding court politics. Ordinary animals do not deliberately cast magic, become collectible loot or join a traveling group merely because someone feeds them. Ownership and established bonds persist.

Livestock.name: Livestock
Livestock.description: Ordinary farm and working-yard animals: cattle, sheep, goats, pigs and similar stock. They shape rural work, fences, feeding, trade and daily noise. A distressed animal may need patience, handling or medical attention rather than combat. They have no deliberate spellcasting. Size can make accidental injury dangerous, but no automatic hostility or elemental resistance follows. Establish who owns the animal before any sale, removal or slaughter.

Pack Animal.name: Pack Animal
Pack Animal.description: Ordinary mounts and burden animals trained for hauling or travel. Terrain, loads, rest and handling affect what is practical. A nervous beast can balk at a portal, narrow ledge or unfamiliar smell; that is an interaction, not proof of possession. They do not understand route permits or cast their way out of danger. A hired animal remains subject to its actual loan terms and owner.

Wild Predator.name: Wild Predator
Wild Predator.description: Ordinary wolves, big cats and similar predators. Hunger, territory, cubs, injury and experience with people influence their choices. Most avoid a costly fight when they can. Tracks, calls, scent and disturbed prey can warn of their presence. They do not possess deliberate spellcasting or pursue a retreating party forever. Observation, distance, deterrence and a changed route can solve the encounter.

Wild Herbivore.name: Wild Herbivore
Wild Herbivore.description: Ordinary deer, hares and other nonpredatory wildlife. They may flee, freeze, hide or defend young. A cornered large animal can be dangerous without being malicious. Use them for ecology, observation, hunting where lawful or an ordinary pleasant sight. They have no automatic affinity or conversational knowledge. Finding wildlife is not necessarily an encounter that needs a quest or a fight.

Giant Spider.name: Giant Spider
Giant Spider.description: Large mana-bearing spiders whose hunting methods depend on species and surroundings. Web lines, abandoned prey and vibration responses can reveal a territory before contact. They may trap, ambush, guard eggs or withdraw; they do not all obey a matron or share a mind. Some use venom or trained-looking magical reflexes, but an individual needs those actual capabilities. Fire threatens exposed silk and body alike. Routes can be studied, cut or bypassed instead of charging into a nest.

Moltback Silkguard.name: Moltback Silkguard
Moltback Silkguard.description: A broad, hairless spider mana beast with layered rust-brown chitin, dull green eyes and pale webbing around its forelegs. It plants its weight over territory and anchors silk before lunging or pulling at an intruder's footing. Heavy plates resist cuts and punctures; fire threatens vulnerable joints and silk. Taut lines, shed plates and a braced posture telegraph its position. It cannot cover every approach at once. Study anchors, change elevation, disrupt its stance or find a bypass. This is a reusable creature type, not one named individual or an endlessly respawning guard. Set an actual encounter's level, tier, abilities and persistent outcome separately.

Slime.name: Slime
Slime.description: Mobile masses of mana-bearing gel that gather around food, moisture or particular residues. Size and composition determine their danger. Their soft bodies disperse blunt impact, while cold can stiffen the gel. A slime can engulf scraps, obstruct a drain or threaten an unwary animal without plotting against anyone. Notice trails and feeding before touching it. Specialized corrosive, intelligent or elemental variants require an actual individual record; this type does not dissolve every possession on contact.

Dire Wolf.name: Dire Wolf
Dire Wolf.description: Mana-adapted pack hunters, larger and more coordinated than ordinary wolves. They use cover, scent and group pressure rather than waiting in a line to be fought. Howling, tracks and a sudden absence of prey can warn travelers. Individuals protect territory and packmates; injury and an unfavorable position can make them disengage. They have no blanket resistance or automatic elemental spell repertoire. Negotiation needs a real way to communicate, not ordinary human speech assumed to work.

Stonehide Boar.name: Stonehide Boar
Stonehide Boar.description: A heavy forest or foothill mana beast with mineralized hide along its shoulders. It drives forward with alarming force but needs room to turn and recover after a committed charge. Plowed ground, broken saplings and scraped stone mark its route. Water-softened footing and redirected movement offer practical counters; the hide is particularly good at dispersing blunt impacts. It may be defending a feeding ground, not hunting people. A barricade or a quieter approach can be more sensible than a duel.

Great Bear.name: Great Bear
Great Bear.description: A large mana-bearing bear adapted to remote woodland or mountain territory. Its weight, reach and endurance make careless close combat dangerous. It can stand, bluff, swat or charge, with clearer intentions than a speaking villain. Tracks, torn bark and food caches offer warning. Cubs, hunger and injury shape its aggression. Individual magical techniques are authored separately; being a great bear does not grant every Nature spell or require a fight to the death.

Griffin.name: Griffin
Griffin.description: Powerful winged mana beasts with an eaglelike forebody and leonine hindquarters. They use height, dives and territorial displays; a grounded griffin still has dangerous reach. Wind conditions, wing room and a nest's position matter. They can be trained through a real history of care but are not automatically mounts. Aerie signs should precede a nest encounter. Avoid clipping wings or awarding flight merely because the creature's type is known.

Roc.name: Roc
Roc.description: Enormous mountain or sky-island birds whose size turns a landing, wingbeat or carried load into a serious local event. Their nesting ranges are large, not an excuse to spawn one above every bridge. Broken branches, vast shadows, calls and disturbed herds can announce them. They favor space and altitude; enclosed terrain restricts them. A roc follows animal needs rather than theatrical cruelty. Protecting food or young may be resolved by distance, diversion or a negotiated route through knowledgeable locals.

Sky Serpent.name: Sky Serpent
Sky Serpent.description: Long-bodied flying mana beasts seen among high currents and isolated islands. They coil through open air, using terrain and wind to approach or evade. A resting serpent can resemble a ribbon along a cliff until it moves. Their exact affinity and temperament vary; flight is not universal control of the weather. Young, wounded or territorial individuals behave differently. A careful crossing can avoid their hunting path, and a warning display need not become an attack.

Drake.name: Drake
Drake.description: Wingless or limited-flight draconic mana beasts, distinct from dragonkin people and fully developed dragons. Their scales resist light cuts, while bludgeoning force can reach through the armor. A drake's territory, diet and individual element determine an encounter; the category alone grants no breath weapon or fire immunity. Shed scales, claw marks and feeding remains give warning. They can be cunning without speaking or submitting to a claimant with a noble title.

Wyvern.name: Wyvern
Wyvern.description: Two-legged winged draconic predators, much smaller than true dragons, with territorial shrieks and a preference for height and a clear escape. Circling shadows, scored perches and displaced wildlife can warn of their presence. They dive, seize prey and defend occupied nesting ledges; narrow interiors restrict their wings. Venom and breath belong only to individuals explicitly possessing them. They are distinct from dragonkin people and sacred dragons, not automatically willing mounts, and their nests are not unowned treasure stores.

Dragon.name: Dragon
Dragon.description: Rare, formidable draconic beings whose age, intelligence, element and relationships must be established individually. Some may speak and negotiate; others behave as territorial beasts. Do not generate one casually to raise the stakes of an ordinary errand. A dragon's presence changes how settlements travel and prepare, with visible evidence before direct contact. This broad type gives no blanket elemental immunity, universal spell mastery, rebirth or permission to ignore resolved outcomes.

Phoenix.name: Phoenix
Phoenix.description: Rare fire-bearing winged mana beasts associated with sustained heat and brilliant plumage. They seek suitable nesting grounds and react to actual threats rather than functioning as academy mascots that anyone can summon. Fire cannot harm their burning bodies; water can break their concentration and chill the flame. Rebirth, healing tears and transferable immortality are not guaranteed properties of this category. Establish such exceptional powers in the particular individual, with real limits.

Hydra.name: Hydra
Hydra.description: Large many-headed aquatic or marshland mana beasts. Multiple heads can watch different approaches and coordinate bites, but they still share one body, space and capacity to maneuver. Their wake, tracks and feeding sites should warn of danger. Regeneration is not an infinite extra-life mechanic: any actual regrowth requires an explicit ability and its limitations. This type grants no resistance by default. Observation, terrain and leaving a nesting area can matter as much as damage.

Crystal Moth.name: Crystal Moth
Crystal Moth.description: Delicate mana-bearing moths with translucent mineral scales. They gather near particular currents and light sources, making their movement useful to attentive field researchers. Crowds can obscure vision or settle on exposed equipment, usually without hostile intent. Handling them roughly damages their wings; careful observation or a changed light source may redirect them. They do not provide effortless Divination, unlimited crystal materials or a new portal whenever they gather.

Thorn Creeper.name: Thorn Creeper
Thorn Creeper.description: A mobile mass of thorned roots and stems animated by its own accumulated mana. It probes toward vibration and accessible nutrients, rooting itself to pull or restrain prey. Dry fibers burn easily, while the springing structure disperses blunt blows. Fresh scratches, displaced roots and a patch of disturbed soil can telegraph it. Severing an anchor or moving outside its reach can break a hold. It is not automatically a person, a druid's familiar or a hive mind.

Mimic.name: Mimic
Mimic.description: A shape-assuming mana beast that imitates a particular kind of object to ambush prey. Its disguise has physical limits: seams, weight, residue or a suspicious position can betray it. Give an established mimic a consistent body and feeding method rather than turning every examined chest into one after the fact. Detection and careful handling can prevent a fight. Defeating it does not automatically create the valuable object it appeared to be.

Stone Golem.name: Stone Golem
Stone Golem.description: A deliberately animated stone body built for a task such as hauling, guarding or holding a dangerous structure. Its joints, core and instructions provide specific points to investigate. Stone resists cuts and punctures, while concentrated blunt force can break its body. It has no living circulation for poison. A simple golem follows an actual command system, not conversational persuasion; a sentient exception needs an individual record. Disabling a control or fulfilling an instruction can be more useful than smashing it.

Metal Automaton.name: Metal Automaton
Metal Automaton.description: An articulated metal construct with an identifiable power and control system. It may be an enchanted worker, a guard or a true magitech device; establish which rather than treating all machinery as the same. Its casing resists cuts and punctures, but lightning can disrupt exposed channels. Poison does not affect its nonliving body. Maintenance faults, control access and limited orders create practical interaction. A disabled machine is not repaired by flattery or automatically claimed as salvage.

Animated Armor.name: Animated Armor
Animated Armor.description: An empty suit moved by an actual enchantment. It can guard a threshold, perform rehearsed work or respond to a command, with movement limited by the suit's construction. Blunt force can deform joints; blades have difficulty finding flesh that is not present. Poison has no biological target. Decide how its order can be recognized, suspended or fulfilled. It does not acquire the remembered personality of every person who once wore the armor.

Rune Sentinel.name: Rune Sentinel
Rune Sentinel.description: An anchored constructed watcher tied to a defined ward and detection method. It reacts to what its sensors and instructions can actually perceive, not hidden character sheets or all criminal intent. Marks, lenses, a charged surface or a warning tone can reveal its coverage. It has no living body to poison. Bypassing a sensor, presenting valid authority or disabling the real power channel can change its response. It cannot pursue beyond its physical reach without an actual mobile form.

Clockwork Beast.name: Clockwork Beast
Clockwork Beast.description: An animal-shaped mechanism used for transport, workshop work, demonstration or security. Its design governs speed, load and attacks; resemblance to a beast supplies no natural instincts or inherited spells. Exposed workings are vulnerable to grit, damage and poorly controlled lightning. It has no living metabolism for poison. True integrated magitech is distinct from a simple enchanted toy. Skilled repair requires the real fault, suitable tools and materials, not a generic instant fix.

Skeleton.name: Skeleton
Skeleton.description: Reanimated bones held together by a particular necromantic force. They may follow a command, guard a site or retain fragments of a former person only when the individual record supports it. Blunt force breaks the frame effectively, and light disrupts its animating pattern. Piercing attacks find little soft tissue; poison has no living circulation to affect. Who animated it and whether it can be released are investigation questions, not knowledge every passerby possesses.

Restless Corpse.name: Restless Corpse
Restless Corpse.description: A dead body animated by an actual spell, binding or localized supernatural condition. Movement and awareness depend on that cause. Fire and light can damage the body and animating pattern; poison has no ordinary living metabolism to exploit. It is not automatically infectious or proof that a nearby living necromancer is guilty. Give a site credible signs and a way to investigate or avoid it. Returned remains are still somebody's remains, not routine trade loot.

Ghost.name: Ghost
Ghost.description: An incorporeal presence with a particular origin, awareness and attachment. Some can communicate; others repeat a limited pattern. Light can disrupt the manifestation, while ordinary physical blows pass through much of it. Poison cannot harm a body that is absent. These damage rules do not imply immunity to compassion, deception or evidence. Discover what it actually perceives and wants before assuming it must be destroyed. Knowledge and memories remain as limited as its history allows.

Wraith.name: Wraith
Wraith.description: A dangerous disembodied remnant sustained by a specific supernatural cause. Its chill, sound or effect on nearby life can warn of a manifestation. It may stalk, guard, hunger or pursue a binding; it is not automatically an intelligent schemer. Light threatens its form, ordinary physical blows are less effective, and poison has no biological target. Injuries it causes follow the actual attack and treatment rules rather than an invented unavoidable permanent curse. Wraith Island's name does not establish that these creatures patrol its prison.

Fire Elemental.name: Fire Elemental
Fire Elemental.description: Living flame gathered around a sustaining mana pattern. Heat shimmer, scorched surfaces and an appetite for fuel make its presence observable. It can flow around an obstacle but needs a real route; an extinguished manifestation does not automatically respawn. Its heat is dangerous to nearby people and possessions according to actual contact, not limitless ambient damage. Establish its origin, persistence, awareness and individual abilities when encountered. Its type supplies the listed damage profile, not a free spell list, a guaranteed reward or automatic hostility.

Water Elemental.name: Water Elemental
Water Elemental.description: A coherent moving volume of water held by a sustaining mana pattern. It uses flow, weight and its available surroundings. A basin, channel or dry interior changes its options. It does not have infinite water or automatic control of every liquid inside a person. Ripples moving against the current can signal its presence. Establish its origin, persistence, awareness and individual abilities when encountered. Its type supplies the listed damage profile, not a free spell list, a guaranteed reward or automatic hostility.

Earth Elemental.name: Earth Elemental
Earth Elemental.description: A mana-bound body of soil and mineral. It uses mass, footing and available ground, with limited reach through actual material. Water can loosen its cohesion; this is a damage vulnerability, not an instant automatic victory. Crumbling edges and shifting ground can announce its movement. Tunnels, buildings and bystanders remain real constraints. Establish its origin, persistence, awareness and individual abilities when encountered. Its type supplies the listed damage profile, not a free spell list, a guaranteed reward or automatic hostility.

Wind Elemental.name: Wind Elemental
Wind Elemental.description: A sustained circulating body of air. Dust, moving cloth and pressure changes can reveal it. It can buffet or obstruct but does not suffocate everyone nearby by existing. Confined geometry and rooted barriers affect its movement; earth magic is particularly effective at breaking its circulation. A harmless current is not automatically this creature. Establish its origin, persistence, awareness and individual abilities when encountered. Its type supplies the listed damage profile, not a free spell list, a guaranteed reward or automatic hostility.

Ice Elemental.name: Ice Elemental
Ice Elemental.description: An articulated manifestation of frost and ice around a mana pattern. Cracking surfaces, spreading rime and disturbed meltwater reveal its movement. It can brace, break or reshape within its actual abilities, without freezing a whole settlement on arrival. Heat threatens its coherence. Destroyed fragments do not each become a new enemy. Establish its origin, persistence, awareness and individual abilities when encountered. Its type supplies the listed damage profile, not a free spell list, a guaranteed reward or automatic hostility.

Lightning Elemental.name: Lightning Elemental
Lightning Elemental.description: A bounded electrical manifestation with a sustaining pattern. Charge noise, lifted hairs and light along conductive paths warn of it. It can exploit real conductors but does not teleport through any named metal object anywhere. Grounding and earth magic can disrupt it. A laboratory spark or routine storm is not proof that one exists. Establish its origin, persistence, awareness and individual abilities when encountered. Its type supplies the listed damage profile, not a free spell list, a guaranteed reward or automatic hostility.

Arachne.name: Arachne
Arachne.description: Sapient beings with a humanoid upper body and a large spiderlike lower body. Silk, climbing and natural reach depend on the individual's anatomy and trained abilities. They have their own names, motives and relationships; they are not all members of one brood or automatically hostile. A particular matron's territorial cruelty is her own character. Establish awareness, casting and combat capability in the real individual record. This type supplies no automatic resistance, spell mastery, social immunity or party membership.

Giant.name: Giant
Giant.description: Very large humanoid beings whose particular intelligence, speech, social behavior and abilities must be established individually. Mountain signs may include huge tracks, displaced boulders and shelters at a different scale. Size makes ordinary movement dangerous to smaller people without making every giant malicious or mindless. Show evidence and actual motives before direct contact. The category does not assign a fixed boss level, universal resistance, guaranteed treasure or automatic hostility. The isolated yeti Orrum is a separately authored individual using this broad body type. Reuse his NPC record when its rare encounter actually occurs; do not produce generic yeti packs or duplicate his identity.

Threadwing Grazer.name: Threadwing Grazer
Threadwing Grazer.description:
APPEARANCE: A rabbit-sized six-legged insect with a rounded moss-green body and four long translucent ribbon wings. Fine combs replace biting jaws; a small ring of amber eye spots sits around its blunt head. At rest the wings hang like loose silk, without a humanoid face.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Cloudbloom meadow colonies eat pollen and mineral fibers. Usually level 10–20 at appropriate sites; a cornered group can whip abrasive wing edges or raise a blinding pollen cloud. They migrate between bloom patches and are not universally hostile.
COUNTERPLAY: Observe the feeding rhythm, cover exposed eyes, interrupt the wing space or leave the colony room to move. Fire also destroys the crop a collector may be trying to protect.
FIELD VALUE: Naturally shed wing scales and properly gathered fibers support filter cloth and fragrance research.
GENERATION: Use the actual location band and establish this individual’s level, tier, disposition and bounded abilities. This type does not spawn itself or rescale an existing creature. Copy its diagnostic anatomy into the generated record and visual description; do not replace it with a generic humanoid or a familiar monster with the same color. Reuse a previously encountered individual. Recovered material requires actual acquisition; no guaranteed loot, instant crafting bonus, tame companion or universal consumable effect is granted.

Twigback Browser.name: Twigback Browser
Twigback Browser.description:
APPEARANCE: A deer-sized four-legged herbivore with a barrel chest, dark felt skin and branching flat paddles growing along its back instead of antlers on its head. Its head is broad and blunt with two sideways amber eyes. The back paddles carry living moss.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Browses Cloudbloom woodland and sleeps beneath branches. Slow and wary until crowded, when it shoves or charges. Its resting silhouette resembles a small fallen tree; this is camouflage rather than illusion magic.
COUNTERPLAY: Read hoof marks and breathing before collecting from a supposed log. Give young animals room; cover interrupts its straight charge.
FIELD VALUE: Discarded paddle tips and rubbed-off moss can be useful under an agreed collection limit.
GENERATION: Use the actual location band and establish this individual’s level, tier, disposition and bounded abilities. This type does not spawn itself or rescale an existing creature. Copy its diagnostic anatomy into the generated record and visual description; do not replace it with a generic humanoid or a familiar monster with the same color. Reuse a previously encountered individual. Recovered material requires actual acquisition; no guaranteed loot, instant crafting bonus, tame companion or universal consumable effect is granted.

Ribbonjaw Prowler.name: Ribbonjaw Prowler
Ribbonjaw Prowler.description:
APPEARANCE: A lean wolf-sized ambush animal with six short hooked legs, smooth bark-brown hide and two long flexible jaw membranes running down its neck. Its real mouth is small; the membranes unfold sideways into a ribbed capture basket. Four forward-facing black eyes catch tiny highlights.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Stalks Sunspill’s hanging bark lanes. It grips prey briefly, then retreats to cover; it does not swallow a person whole or teleport between shadows.
COUNTERPLAY: Watch both flanks, use open ground and strike the extended membrane during its committed rush. A severed membrane is a real injury, not a free endless whip attack.
FIELD VALUE: Recovered membrane can suit flexible bindings, but only actual suitable remains or shed tissue exist.
GENERATION: Use the actual location band and establish this individual’s level, tier, disposition and bounded abilities. This type does not spawn itself or rescale an existing creature. Copy its diagnostic anatomy into the generated record and visual description; do not replace it with a generic humanoid or a familiar monster with the same color. Reuse a previously encountered individual. Recovered material requires actual acquisition; no guaranteed loot, instant crafting bonus, tame companion or universal consumable effect is granted.

Petalglass Snail.name: Petalglass Snail
Petalglass Snail.description:
APPEARANCE: A knee-high snail with a broad pearly foot, four short feelers and a fan of overlapping transparent petal-shaped shell plates. Mineral colors show through the shell; it has no floral human head or separate limbs.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Grazes films from spring pools and Prismbloom margins. Mostly peaceful, but a hard blow can release razorlike shell fragments as it contracts. A living population contributes to filtration without making all nearby water safe.
COUNTERPLAY: Move it gently with an actual method, avoid crushing its fragile plates and collect cast-off shell rather than treating a grazer as a required kill.
FIELD VALUE: Loose shell fragments are optical and filter research materials, not restorative crystals.
GENERATION: Use the actual location band and establish this individual’s level, tier, disposition and bounded abilities. This type does not spawn itself or rescale an existing creature. Copy its diagnostic anatomy into the generated record and visual description; do not replace it with a generic humanoid or a familiar monster with the same color. Reuse a previously encountered individual. Recovered material requires actual acquisition; no guaranteed loot, instant crafting bonus, tame companion or universal consumable effect is granted.

Sailfin Skipper.name: Sailfin Skipper
Sailfin Skipper.description:
APPEARANCE: A cat-sized flattened animal with two gripping forelegs, a long rudder tail and a translucent fan stretched along each flank. Its narrow toothless beak scrapes salt; round dark eyes sit on short fixed stalks. It glides with body fins and has no feathered wings.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Rests under Tetherroot ledges and scrapes salts from rope fittings. Territorial rushes can cut cloth, damage sails or knock unsecured equipment aside.
COUNTERPLAY: Secure gear, avoid a leap after it into open air and obstruct the space it needs to spread its fins. A grounded specimen loses much of its maneuvering room.
FIELD VALUE: Discarded fin film can be studied for lightweight membranes.
GENERATION: Use the actual location band and establish this individual’s level, tier, disposition and bounded abilities. This type does not spawn itself or rescale an existing creature. Copy its diagnostic anatomy into the generated record and visual description; do not replace it with a generic humanoid or a familiar monster with the same color. Reuse a previously encountered individual. Recovered material requires actual acquisition; no guaranteed loot, instant crafting bonus, tame companion or universal consumable effect is granted.

Bellows Mite.name: Bellows Mite
Bellows Mite.description:
APPEARANCE: A fist-sized six-legged arthropod with an inflated translucent abdomen, three dark horizontal ribs and a short inward-folding nozzle. Rows of beadlike eyes run along the front rim. Colonies look like pulsing mineral nodules on a cave wall.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Clings around damp air vents. Exhaling individuals produce short pressure bursts; groups respond to blocked airflow and vibration. Their blasts are bounded local actions, not permanent weather control.
COUNTERPLAY: Cover the nozzle’s line, change the immediate airflow or clear a safe vent. Sealing the entire chamber can worsen pressure.
FIELD VALUE: Shed rib casings can inform valves and air filters.
GENERATION: Use the actual location band and establish this individual’s level, tier, disposition and bounded abilities. This type does not spawn itself or rescale an existing creature. Copy its diagnostic anatomy into the generated record and visual description; do not replace it with a generic humanoid or a familiar monster with the same color. Reuse a previously encountered individual. Recovered material requires actual acquisition; no guaranteed loot, instant crafting bonus, tame companion or universal consumable effect is granted.

Rimehorn Hare.name: Rimehorn Hare
Rimehorn Hare.description:
APPEARANCE: A large hare with dense slate-blue fur, powerful hindlegs and two short backward-curving translucent horns above its brows. Its breath frosts around the horns before a burst; it remains a four-legged animal with normal paws.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Inhabits the lower Rimeglass forest. It feeds on bark and roots, then uses abrupt icy leaps to escape or defend a burrow. Small appearance does not make it a harmless familiar.
COUNTERPLAY: Anticipate the landing direction, avoid surrounding its burrow and use cover. Its visible frosting warns of an imminent burst.
FIELD VALUE: Naturally shed horn layers can be sampled without trapping a whole colony.
GENERATION: Use the actual location band and establish this individual’s level, tier, disposition and bounded abilities. This type does not spawn itself or rescale an existing creature. Copy its diagnostic anatomy into the generated record and visual description; do not replace it with a generic humanoid or a familiar monster with the same color. Reuse a previously encountered individual. Recovered material requires actual acquisition; no guaranteed loot, instant crafting bonus, tame companion or universal consumable effect is granted.

Frostmantle Lynx.name: Frostmantle Lynx
Frostmantle Lynx.description:
APPEARANCE: A broad-pawed feline with pale gray fur, black ear tufts and loose translucent frost scales hanging over its shoulders like a broken mantle. Its eyes are copper and its long whiskers carry ice beads; it has no wings.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Stalks cold tarns and conifer margins. It breaks its outline against ice and snow, with short pounces and a territorial freezing spray. It does not become invisible or ignore tracks.
COUNTERPLAY: Use reflected movement, exposed breath, protected flanks and warm cover. Outside snowy terrain its mantle is easier to see.
FIELD VALUE: Moulted mantle scales support cold-weather material testing.
GENERATION: Use the actual location band and establish this individual’s level, tier, disposition and bounded abilities. This type does not spawn itself or rescale an existing creature. Copy its diagnostic anatomy into the generated record and visual description; do not replace it with a generic humanoid or a familiar monster with the same color. Reuse a previously encountered individual. Recovered material requires actual acquisition; no guaranteed loot, instant crafting bonus, tame companion or universal consumable effect is granted.

Knapcap Colony.name: Knapcap Colony
Knapcap Colony.description:
APPEARANCE: A low colony of jointed fungal bodies: dinner-plate caps ride on three pale tendonlike root legs, with porous undersides and no faces. Dark cords link nearby bodies while they feed. Colors vary from ochre to blue-gray.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Lives in wet fallen wood. Disturbed caps leap, vent spores or pull toward a sheltered root knot. A colony is not a society of tiny mushroom people or an automatic mind-reading network.
COUNTERPLAY: Ventilate, identify the cord routes and avoid standing over a disturbed cap. Breaking one visible fruiting body need not destroy the entire colony.
FIELD VALUE: A permitted contained culture can be useful for decomposition studies; wild spores are not automatically medicine.

Glacier Manta.name: Glacier Manta
Glacier Manta.description:
APPEARANCE: A wagon-wide aerial filter feeder with a broad diamond-shaped body, six short underside paddles, icy blue dorsal ridges and a long split tail. Pale comb plates line the underside around a central mouth. It has no fishlike gills on a humanoid torso.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Rides the lee of Rimeglass peaks and collects ice-laden mana dust. Defends a feeding lane with a sweep or compressed icy wake. It is a real animal, not a flying island.
COUNTERPLAY: Observe prevailing currents, use overhangs and leave the turn space. Heavy icing or damaged fins makes a turn slower.
FIELD VALUE: Shed comb fragments can be studied for filters and cold-environment craft.

Hushbell Carapace.name: Hushbell Carapace
Hushbell Carapace.description:
APPEARANCE: A waist-high arthropod walking on four narrow legs beneath an oval charcoal shell. Three hollow bell cups hang from its back on flexible stems. Its low head has two white eye bars; its cups face the ground when stalking.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Inhabits sheltered ruins and quiet stone passages. Its cups damp nearby sound while it approaches, then release a short stored pulse. Silence has a local range and duration, not a permanent ban on all casting.
COUNTERPLAY: Use sight, reflected light and floor vibrations. Obstructing a cup or changing the room’s resonance reduces its advantage.
FIELD VALUE: Recovered empty cups may suit acoustic research after safe handling.

Stormglass Kite.name: Stormglass Kite
Stormglass Kite.description:
APPEARANCE: A shield-sized angular organism with a translucent rhomboid central plate, four jointed blade fins and dangling hair-fine conductive tendrils. Its eyes form three small black beads along one leading edge; it has no bird head or feathers.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Flocks around charged mineral seams. It gathers electrical charge and discharges along a short tendril reach. Linked flock movement can threaten an exposed route, but every animal does not gain the entire flock’s output.
COUNTERPLAY: Break line and spacing, use rock cover and wait for a real discharge before collecting a shed plate. Metal equipment does not make its owner universally doomed.
FIELD VALUE: Spent plates can be used in bounded insulation and charge-storage experiments.

Mantlefin Drifter.name: Mantlefin Drifter
Mantlefin Drifter.description:
APPEARANCE: A small-boat-sized freshwater animal with a broad soft mantle, eight short flexible edge fins and a dark central underside keel. Its mouth opens below the keel; two pale eyes sit above it. It has neither human features nor a tentacled octopus head.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Feeds in Mirrorwater’s open lakes and rises slowly through reeds. Adults shove boats, defend calves and stir opaque silt rather than automatically hunt people. Young remain smaller individuals within the site’s level band.
COUNTERPLAY: Give turning room, mark shallow banks and watch the pale fin edges. Dry shelves interrupt pursuit.
FIELD VALUE: Naturally shed keel film can be studied for waterproof layers.

Glassreed Sifter.name: Glassreed Sifter
Glassreed Sifter.description:
APPEARANCE: A torso-sized marsh animal with six narrow jointed legs, a low green-gray body and a hinged cage of clipped glassy reeds around its back. Two brushlike feeding arms sweep water in front of a blunt head with paired gold eyes.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Builds feeding cages in shallow channels. The cage deflects slashes while brush arms catch small prey; threatened animals jab or churn reeds into confusing moving screens.
COUNTERPLAY: Read the moving joints, interrupt its feeding current and avoid pushing bare hands through the cage. A changed route can spare both colony and sample bed.
FIELD VALUE: Loose mature reed stems and abandoned cages provide usable research samples.

Lantern Leech Swarm.name: Lantern Leech Swarm
Lantern Leech Swarm.description:
APPEARANCE: A group of finger-length translucent ribbon organisms, each with a dark central gut and two glowing dots near a circular sucker. They swim or make short membrane-assisted hops between wet surfaces; they are not ghost lights.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Attracted to bright disturbance in Mirrorwater marshes. A swarm drains and irritates exposed tissue through real contact. It does not consume a numerical Mana pool from a distance or create an unconfigured disease automatically.
COUNTERPLAY: Shield exposed skin, control light and separate from wet vegetation. Appropriate treatment uses actual supported effects.
FIELD VALUE: Contained specimens support studies of lure chemistry, not a universal mana-draining item.

Spillback Crab.name: Spillback Crab
Spillback Crab.description:
APPEARANCE: A barrel-sized crustacean with six walking legs, two short grasping limbs and a pair of hinged stone-white backplates. A central siphon between the plates directs a water jet; amber eye stalks stay low beside the front rim.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Braces in Spillway pools. It aligns its backplates visibly before a narrow jet, then needs time to refill. A real opening exists between volleys; it does not fire an endless beam.
COUNTERPLAY: Break its alignment, move to broken dry rock or interrupt the local flow. Avoid sending a loose ally toward the spill edge.
FIELD VALUE: Intact discarded backplates can be inspected for pump housings.
