Mire Lantern.name: Mire Lantern
Mire Lantern.description:
APPEARANCE: A low four-legged amphibious predator with a broad dark body and a curved stalk above its shoulders ending in a pale luminous sac. Its true eyes are tiny and close to the waterline; its mouth opens across the flat front of its body.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Hunts insects and small animals among luminous marsh plants. It can mislead a traveler following its light, then snap from shallow water. Its lure is visible behavior, not compulsory magical obedience.
COUNTERPLAY: Compare light movement with fixed plants, keep a shore bearing and use an elevated line of sight.
FIELD VALUE: A safely obtained shed lure lining has optical value, without becoming a mind-control device.

Lensback Eel.name: Lensback Eel
Lensback Eel.description:
APPEARANCE: A long dark eel with four broad transparent discs running down each flank, a blunt circular mouth and two small silver eyes. It coils through old machinery; the flank discs bend light while the body remains physically present.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Lives in deep Mirrorwater hollows and the Drowned Orrery. It produces shifting reflections and strikes across a short water channel. A projected image is not a second creature or an attack from every reflection.
COUNTERPLAY: Cloud a sightline, vary the viewing angle and watch the actual wake. Reflection control does not stop physical barriers.
FIELD VALUE: A loose flank disc may be copied or recovered under the real commission terms.

Bramblehorn.name: Bramblehorn
Bramblehorn.description:
APPEARANCE: An ox-sized six-legged herbivore with a low armored brow, two forward thorn-shaped horns and dense violet-gray fur. A row of soft brush fans grows along its spine. It has broad cloven feet and two ordinary lateral eyes.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Grazes Mauvewind heath and defends herd spacing. Charges are strong but committed; juveniles and feeding animals are not inherently enemies. It is distinct from a sapient ram beastfolk person.
COUNTERPLAY: Respect warning displays, break a straight charge line and use gullies or solid cover. Do not stand between a parent and its young.
FIELD VALUE: Rubbed horn flakes and shed brush fibers can be collected without slaughtering the herd.

Glassmane Courser.name: Glassmane Courser
Glassmane Courser.description:
APPEARANCE: A tall narrow-bodied quadruped with long springy legs, a low reptilian head and a segmented translucent mane that rises from neck to rump. Its forward violet eyes and hooked foreclaws betray the predator beneath its grazing-animal silhouette.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Waits near pale heath ridges and hunts in small loose groups. The mane scatters its outline while still, then folds during a rush. It is not an enchanted horse or a mount awaiting ownership.
COUNTERPLAY: Identify eye placement and deliberate stillness, watch the flank and disrupt its run with terrain.
FIELD VALUE: Discarded mane segments can be studied for camouflage materials.

Chimeback Strider.name: Chimeback Strider
Chimeback Strider.description:
APPEARANCE: A tall tripod animal with three jointed legs around a rounded torso, one low head on a flexible neck and a broad hinged resonance plate above its back. Bands of pale mineral cross its violet hide. Its three eyes are clustered on the head, not painted on the plate.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Moves through Singing Stone passages. It raises its backplate before a directional resonant pulse and braces its legs to fire. Pulses have real targets and cover; ordinary stone everywhere does not become its weapon.
COUNTERPLAY: Break the lane, interfere with resonance or exploit the visible bracing interval. A Sound affinity is helpful knowledge, not automatic immunity.
FIELD VALUE: Naturally dropped plate shards support acoustic calibration research.

Prismfold Fan.name: Prismfold Fan
Prismfold Fan.description:
APPEARANCE: A low segmented animal with four short legs and three pairs of broad translucent membranes folding upward from its back. Pink and turquoise vein lines mark each membrane. Its tiny dark head and paired gold eyes remain below the luminous fan.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Basks by Prismbloom mineral pools. Refraction obscures its exact position while it snaps membranes outward or retreats. It cannot rewrite reality, turn into a person or create independent copies.
COUNTERPLAY: Use shadows, alternate angles, reflected water movement and shade. A real physical outline remains available.
FIELD VALUE: Cast-off membrane plates have optical research value; taking one does not grant Illusion mastery.

Veilhook Ray.name: Veilhook Ray
Veilhook Ray.description:
APPEARANCE: A lean aerial ray with a slate-violet diamond body, two short hornlike snouts and six retractile hooks along its belly. Its narrow tail ends in a broad rudder membrane. Paired amber eyes face forward; it has no humanoid upper body.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Rides chasm updrafts and catches cliff growth, small prey and loose equipment. A flock can create a dangerous crossing without being a coordinated sapient army. A snagged bag remains a physical object that can be recovered.
COUNTERPLAY: Secure loads, use overhangs and predict the current. Its hooks need contact and a committed pass.
FIELD VALUE: Dropped hook sheaths can be studied for climbing equipment.

Palimpsest Warden.name: Palimpsest Warden
Palimpsest Warden.description:
APPEARANCE: A person-height old construct made of nested pale ceramic plates marked with fine dark calibration lines. Four asymmetric arms fold around a lenslike central aperture above three short stone legs. There is no human face, robe or living torso beneath the plates.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Survives in old survey workrooms. Repeated flashes and movement near protected apparatus trigger bounded protective responses. It has no omniscient knowledge, universal speech or authority over living fae.
COUNTERPLAY: Learn its actual trigger pattern, occlude the aperture and interrupt a joint or power link. Permission records matter only if this real machine can read them.
FIELD VALUE: An intact calibration component may be salvaged under actual permission; breaking it destroys some research value.

Choirglass Colossus.name: Choirglass Colossus
Choirglass Colossus.description:
APPEARANCE: A large six-legged animal, roughly two wagons long, with pale layered mineral armor over a dark flexible body. Three sail-like resonance vanes rise from its spine, framing a blunt head with a horizontal band of small violet eyes. Its underside shows breathing seams; it is neither a crystal human nor a dragon.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: A rare mature individual occupies the Inverted Crown bowl at level 55–60. Its resonance can drive nearby wildlife outward, and its low stomps and directed pulses threaten prepared teams. Its abilities remain local and finite; it is a midgame apex animal, not a deity or an endgame boss.
COUNTERPLAY: Observe which vane charges, use the bowl’s solid cover, interrupt exposed seams and act between pulses. Damaged vanes change its tactics rather than immediately killing it. Retreat, a real diversion or habitat solution can be valid.
FIELD VALUE: Shed plates and actual resolved remains have research value. No guaranteed legendary equipment, unlimited energy source or repeated replacement boss.

Thunderbird.name: Thunderbird
Thunderbird.description:
APPEARANCE: A large dark-feathered bird with a hooked silver beak, gold eyes and pale conductive feather shafts that flicker before a discharge.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: A territorial hunter of charged northeastern crags. Its warning calls and occupied perches precede a dive or a bounded lightning attack. It is not a sacred dragon or a guaranteed storm deity.
COUNTERPLAY: Use grounded cover, disrupt the dive space and respect the interval after a discharge.
FIELD VALUE: Genuinely shed stable feathers can support electrical studies.

Cockatrice.name: Cockatrice
Cockatrice.description:
APPEARANCE: A knee-high two-legged bird-reptile with mottled feathers, a scaled tail and a red bony facial comb. Amber eyes brighten before its short-range mineralizing attack.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: A defensive animal at dry meadow edges. Its gaze or bite can cause a bounded hardening condition only through actual resolved abilities; a glance does not automatically permanently petrify an entire party.
COUNTERPLAY: Break eye contact and line of sight, use indirect observation and respond to the visible windup.
FIELD VALUE: Shed comb fragments can support safe hardening research, not instant cure-all potions.

Basilisk.name: Basilisk
Basilisk.description:
APPEARANCE: A heavy eight-legged scaled reptile with low mineral ridges, a wedge-shaped head and large reflective eyes.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: A patient predator of dry ruin passages or rocky heath. Its established mineralizing ability needs a real target, range and outcome. It cannot petrify everyone through walls or ignore its site’s level band.
COUNTERPLAY: Use cover, indirect viewing and movement that exploits its slow turn.
FIELD VALUE: Actual recovered scales may suit a materials study; they do not grant universal petrification immunity.

Harpy.name: Harpy
Harpy.description:
APPEARANCE: A sapient winged humanoid with feathered arms, raptor legs, a humanlike face and an individual’s distinct plumage and hair.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: Cliff communities may trade, defend perches or raid according to their actual group. Some use trained song or sound magic. Species alone is no proof of evil, seductive intent or permission to kill.
COUNTERPLAY: Establish motives, language and boundaries. In a fight, terrain, interrupted song and actual wing space matter.
FIELD VALUE: Trade and agreements can obtain lawful goods. A sapient body is not a loot table.

Chimera.name: Chimera
Chimera.description:
APPEARANCE: A large four-legged beast with a lionlike body, a separate goat head beside the main feline head and a scaled serpent tail ending in a small biting head.
ECOLOGY AND BEHAVIOR: A rare dangerous predator of remote highland or violet frontier territory. Each head’s actual senses and attacks matter, but it remains one bounded creature rather than three free full turns or a replacement for every expedition boss.
COUNTERPLAY: Exploit divided attention, turning space and actual attack recovery; use the site’s terrain.
FIELD VALUE: Recovered remains require a real resolution and appropriate handling; valuable material is not a guaranteed complete enchanted item.

Cinder Carapace Spider.name: Cinder Carapace Spider
Cinder Carapace Spider.description: A large spider mana beast with ember-brown sensory bristles, amber eyes and a dark slag-ridged shell. Limited natural Fire magic produces short heat bursts. It resists fire and is vulnerable to ice; no immunity, free healing or universal command of spiders is implied. Individual native health and casting outcomes remain authoritative.

Guild Staff.name: Guild Staff
Guild Staff.description: Adult staff of an actual guild: reception, records, assessment or material handling. Use the individual’s actual training and remit. The role grants no universal appraisal, lie detection, police authority or portal permission.

Adventurer.name: Adventurer
Adventurer.description: A registered freelance adventurer with an actual badge, background and chosen fighting or occupational method. Martial, magical and mixed approaches are all valid. Rank is a professional credential, not a species, personality, fixed build or automatic portal permit.

Young Stonehide Boar.name: Young Stonehide Boar
Young Stonehide Boar.description: A small, not fully grown Stonehide Boar with soft mineral patches rather than a mature armored shoulder. It stamps and makes a short, committed charge, then needs to turn. Its undeveloped hide has no inherited damage resistance. It is a beginner territorial obstacle, not a disguised adult champion.

Puddle Slime.name: Puddle Slime
Puddle Slime.description: A small translucent slime feeding on harmless drain and riverbank residue. Ripples and a damp trail reveal it. It makes one simple shove or splash and has neither strong corrosive venom nor a universal resistance to ordinary weapons. It can be lured away from its food.

Stray Forest Hound.name: Stray Forest Hound
Stray Forest Hound.description: A hungry, ordinary hound encountered near a maintained route. It barks, circles and may make a single clumsy bite before reassessing. It is not a Dire Wolf, pack leader or spellcasting predator. Food, distance and a firm barrier can change its behavior.

Underbrush Spider.name: Underbrush Spider
Underbrush Spider.description: A small forest mana spider with pale-brown legs and thin ankle-height trip silk. Its feeble venom is a short local irritation, not recurring lethal damage. A disturbed web and scattered husks warn of its hiding place. It has one simple lunge and can flee.

Snow Spirit.name: Snow Spirit
Snow Spirit.description: An intelligent winter manifestation with a humanoid adult face, cold-pale skin and hair or garments formed from a coherent local legend. Has individual knowledge and motives; neither every snow spirit nor every grievance is Ysolenne. Use bounded Ice workings and local terrain, not effortless death by looking at it. Ordinary instances follow actual location level bands; Ysolenne remains the unique named individual with her own fixed power and relationships.

Frostglass Leech.name: Frostglass Leech
Frostglass Leech.description: A flattened translucent ribbon animal the length of a forearm, with six black anchoring nubs along each side and a round glassy sucker at either end. Its frozen outer film crackles when disturbed. It nests in cold damp mineral seams and seeks warmth in pulses; dry ground and steady heat can deter it. It cannot freeze a whole party at a touch. Use a few actual individuals at the site's level band, preserving their unusual anatomy in generated portraits.

Cloudveil Nautilus.name: Cloudveil Nautilus
Cloudveil Nautilus.description: A floating sky mollusk with an opalescent spiral shell, a broad clear membrane sail and five short lavender fins beneath its body; paired dark eyes sit on flexible stalks, with no human face or humanoid torso. It grazes airborne mineral dust along sheltered Asterveil currents. Adults can conceal themselves in drifting mist but cannot teleport. Some mature current-sensing chambers produce a Stillwind Pearl, and an intact spent casing may preserve one. A living creature is not an automatic loot container; observation and actual safe collection matter.

Bracewing Cicada.name: Bracewing Cicada
Bracewing Cicada.description: A palm-sized emerald insect with four triangular translucent wings and hooked hind legs shaped like tiny clamps. Groups brace themselves across exposed vine cables and drink salt from woven fibers. Their resonant wingbeats can shake a light instrument or signal line; they are not a giant lethal swarm by default. Gentle vibration changes, a suitable lure or rerouting a cable can resolve interference. Keep these recognizable insects rather than generating fairy people.

Vaultjaw Marten.name: Vaultjaw Marten
Vaultjaw Marten.description: A long-bodied six-legged mammal with russet fur, small black eyes and two overlapping pale jaw plates that close like a hinged clasp around hard food. It nests in sheltered crates and steals resin, nuts and bright offcuts. A loose hinge-like clicking warns of a defensive snap. Juveniles are suitable weak low-level nuisances; mature wild individuals follow the real local band. It has no extradimensional stomach and cannot swallow an entire inventory or become an elite Mimic through a naming shortcut.

Needleback Prowler.name: Needleback Prowler
Needleback Prowler.description: A low, broad reptilian hunter with moss-green scales, four jointed legs and a flexible comb of hollow ivory needles along its spine. Its blunt wedge head bears four small amber eyes; its tail ends in two gripping pads used to cling to reeds and cage frames. It ambushes small prey in Asterveil wet channels and lashes its needle comb only within close range. Disturbed reeds, shed needles and a blocked retreat provide counterplay. It cannot fire endless projectiles, read minds or ignore cover.

Crucible Competitor.name: Crucible Competitor
Crucible Competitor.description: An adult competitor with an independent livelihood and actual chosen fighting method. Entry in an arena does not imply guild registration, a badge, noble birth or a single temperament. Regulated competition follows its announced nonlethal rules; the person retains ordinary loyalties, work and the ability to decline a match.

Gravewood Golem.name: Gravewood Golem
Gravewood Golem.description: A broad walking frame of pale timber, riblike branches and an empty stone face-mask. Moss threads its joints and amber lights burn in the grain. Most are mindless instruction-bound vessels, not conscious dead people. Nature and Soul workings are distinct ways to affect frame and binding. Guards the rooted walks in small groups; deliberate flanking and exposed joint bindings provide counterplay.

Rootbound Pallbearer.name: Rootbound Pallbearer
Rootbound Pallbearer.description: A four-legged bier of black roots carrying a hollow wooden torso and a little bell. It drags binding strands behind it and tries to hold an intruder for another guardian. Slow turns and the exposed rear bell are readable weaknesses. Its apparent coffin is not automatically occupied by a conscious soul.

Censer-Willow.name: Censer-Willow
Censer-Willow.description: A narrow willow-bodied guardian with hanging seed-pod censers and a crown of long white leaves. It releases visible drifting spiritual haze to obscure an approach, then strikes with flexible branches. Air movement and distance can clear a lane. The haze is not automatic possession, hallucination or unavoidable damage.

Hollowseed Swarm.name: Hollowseed Swarm
Hollowseed Swarm.description: A single coherent encounter of fist-sized seed husks with insectlike root legs and dim blue interiors. They skitter toward warm moving bodies and try to overwhelm one exposed position. Broad barriers, water channels and disrupting the central cluster can limit them. A swarm is not an unlimited number of independent attacks.

Ossuary Trellis.name: Ossuary Trellis
Ossuary Trellis.description: A wall-clinging lattice of roots and old animal bones, its folded limbs opening like a garden fan. It blocks narrow routes with real hooked growth and reacts to contact or vibration. Cutting its exposed anchors or following a different physical route can avoid a direct contest.

Grafted Sentinel.name: Grafted Sentinel
Grafted Sentinel.description: A tall armored tree-vessel with a polished memorial plate, a heavy root club and a visible amber binding knot behind one shoulder. These finite inner guards act with disciplined physical pressure rather than a limitless supply of spells. A real individual spirit may occupy a particular vessel only when established; otherwise it is an instruction-bound guardian.

Rootbound Regent.name: Rootbound Regent
Rootbound Regent.description: An individually named intelligent caretaker built from living timber, funerary bronze and conscious spiritual bindings. It can reason, bargain, lie and defend itself. Its Nature framework and Soul stewardship do not confer universal magic immunity, instant resurrection or the authority to command every dead creature.

Cellar Rat.name: Cellar Rat
Cellar Rat.description: A large ordinary brown rat with a blunt nose, torn ears and flour dust caught in its whiskers. It bites when cornered, then scurries behind cover; it has no venom, armor or magical disease. Usually a level 1 nuisance. Scratching, droppings and gnawed sacks reveal its route. Traps, a food lure or a clear escape can work as well as a blow.

Stray Dog.name: Stray Dog
Stray Dog.description: A lean, rough-coated domestic dog with muddy paws and an uneven leather collar. A hungry stray may defend stolen food, bark and make a short snap before retreating. Beginner individuals are level 1–2, not wolves or trained warhounds. Flattened ears and a stiff posture warn of a bite; food, space and patient handling may avoid one. No automatic rabies, bleeding effect or alpha pack.

Flour Beetle.name: Flour Beetle
Flour Beetle.description: A knee-high oval beetle with cream-brown wing cases, six stubby legs and flour clinging to its feelers. Its shell is thin. It drags dry food toward a dark gap, lifting its front legs before an awkward shove. Level 1–2 specimens are slow nuisances with no damage resistance. Turning a sack, blocking a gap or baiting a basket can contain one without destroying the grain.

Runaway Cleaning Broom.name: Runaway Cleaning Broom
Runaway Cleaning Broom.description: A household broom animated by a worn cleaning enchantment, with copper binding wire and an erratically glowing maker’s mark. It whacks whatever it mistakes for dirt and needs time to turn its long handle. Usually level 2. Pinning the bristles or safely interrupting its accessible binding can stop it. It has no hidden master, inexhaustible spell arsenal or resistance merely because it is a construct.

Orchard Crab.name: Orchard Crab
Orchard Crab.description: A broad freshwater crab about the size of a cooking pot, its mottled olive shell often carrying fallen blossom petals. It wedges itself into irrigation sluices and raises one conspicuous claw before pinching. Young specimens are level 2–3 and have no armored damage resistance. A baited pot, a lifted sluice or a cautious approach from behind offers alternatives to a fight.

Soot Moth.name: Soot Moth
Soot Moth.description: A hand-sized moth with charcoal wings, amber eye-spots and a fluffy white collar stained by lamp soot. It feeds on warm lamp residue and leaves dusty wing prints on glass. Level 2–3 nuisances flutter into faces or shed a brief obscuring puff; they cannot poison lungs, blind permanently or ignite a building. A shaded decoy lamp and a soft net can move them safely.

Timberjaw Gnawer.name: Timberjaw Gnawer
Timberjaw Gnawer.description: A stocky, rabbit-sized mana rodent with broad orange incisors, a squared muzzle and a tail fringed with wood fibers. It gnaws damp supports and stamps before lunging at a nearby boot. Common troublesome adults are level 5–8. Fresh paired tooth marks and a trail of damp shavings expose the nest; sound bracing, barriers and bait interrupt its approach. No instant beam collapse or buried swarm is inherent to the species.

Lantern Wasp.name: Lantern Wasp
Lantern Wasp.description: A fist-sized wasp with a translucent amber abdomen and folded wings patterned like paper ribs. Its nest resembles a little hanging lantern. A bright pulse and rising buzz precede a single close sting. Local nuisance adults are level 6–8. Their venom produces a painful welt rather than continuous lethal damage; covering the light or dampening an abandoned nest can make relocation possible.

Cinderback Lizard.name: Cinderback Lizard
Cinderback Lizard.description: A squat red-brown lizard with four splayed feet and a row of warm coal-colored scales across its shoulders. Often level 7–9 around forges, it warms its back visibly before expelling a short ember puff, then must cool. It cannot breathe a dragon’s stream of flame. A clear cool route, a shielded coal lure or shutting off its heat source changes its behavior.

Scrap Imp.name: Scrap Imp
Scrap Imp.description: A small nonhumanoid fiend with an angular brass-colored face, batlike ears, backward-bending legs and a forked tail used to carry washers. Often level 7–10, it steals useful offcuts and makes crude mechanical toys. It can speak and bargain, lie or become spiteful; these are individual choices. It throws loose scrap or makes a short clawing rush, without teleporting away an entire inventory.

Reed Ambusher.name: Reed Ambusher
Reed Ambusher.description: A flat olive amphibian with four finned limbs, a wide shovel jaw and a fringe of reed-like whiskers. It lies in shallow water and pushes a visible V-shaped ripple ahead of a short bankward leap. Usually level 8–11. It must return to water between committed lunges. High dry footing, a disturbed mud trail and bait are useful; concealment is camouflage rather than true invisibility.

Burrback Hedgebeast.name: Burrback Hedgebeast
Burrback Hedgebeast.description: A goat-sized grazer with short brown fur, a broad snout and tough seed-like burrs woven through its back. Local adults are usually level 8–11. It bowls through low fences, lowers its head before charging and leaves hooked burrs along its trail. Its prickles scratch at contact but do not launch endless binding roots. Fruit lures, open lanes and repaired fencing can redirect it.

Glass-Eye Basilisk.name: Glass-Eye Basilisk
Glass-Eye Basilisk.description: A six-legged gray reptile with green glassy brow plates and milky eyes that brighten before a fixed stare. Local adults are level 13–16. Its sustained gaze causes a brief creeping stiffness; looking away or breaking sight interrupts it. There is no instant permanent petrification. It moves poorly on loose rubble and cannot gaze through walls, shields or closed shutters.

Hollow Lantern.name: Hollow Lantern
Hollow Lantern.description: A salt-corroded rescue lantern floating inside a loose hoop of pale spirit-light, with a wavering human-sized shadow beneath it and no actual body. Usually level 13–16. It repeats a damaged signal and releases a bounded pulse of cold light when approached. Its direction and bell rhythm reveal the place to which it is bound. This is a local haunting, not an all-knowing dead soul or an automatic possession.

Ashcoil Salamander.name: Ashcoil Salamander
Ashcoil Salamander.description: A long charcoal-black salamander with six small feet, a coiling tail and orange seams between its broad scales. Furnace-fed adults are level 14–17. Its throat glows before a close heat jet, followed by a cooling pause. It hunts warm mineral deposits rather than metal objects in an inventory. Damp channels, furnace shutters and vent pressure offer counterplay; no unavoidable room-wide inferno.

Mireglass Stalker.name: Mireglass Stalker
Mireglass Stalker.description: A low wetland hunter with four narrow legs, a split paddle tail and translucent green plates over a dark amphibian body. Typically level 14–18. Reflections break up its outline, but mud prints, ripples and shifting reeds remain visible. It makes short lunges rather than teleporting and loses its camouflage on dry ground. It has neither perfect invisibility nor an unavoidable opening critical strike.

Canal Watcher.name: Canal Watcher
Canal Watcher.description: A waist-high municipal maintenance construct with a round ceramic torso, three iron feet, a water-level float and two jointed gate tools. Malfunctioning working models are around level 14–17. A clacking gauge precedes each heavy tool sweep. A cracked float or obstructed intake may explain its faulty safety order. It has reachable controls, limited movement and no blanket construct immunities.

Thunderfin Ray.name: Thunderfin Ray
Thunderfin Ray.description: A blue-gray mana ray that skims wet sand and shallow water on broad winglike fins, with three amber nodules along its spine and a narrow ribbon tail. Local adults are level 15–18. The nodules glow and its fins spread before a bounded electric discharge. Dry high ground and spacing matter; it cannot electrocute an entire coastline or discharge every action without recovery.

Yokai.name: Yokai
Yokai.description: A varied category of uncanny beings, awakened objects and enduring local spirits. Determine an individual’s actual body, intelligence, origins and disposition; the category grants no uniform hostility, spell list or immunity. Authored Koma, Suzu-no-Ura, Oroha and Hagire keep their individual identities and bodies rather than becoming interchangeable encounters.

Roadside Sparrow Imp.name: Roadside Sparrow Imp
Roadside Sparrow Imp.description: A fist-sized charcoal-and-cream birdlike imp with a flat wooden-looking beak, bright bead eyes and a ragged red throat pouch. It steals soft sandal cords and nests beneath benches. Usually a mischievous nuisance that can be lured, traded with or driven off, not an automatic lethal encounter.

Bamboo Fox.name: Bamboo Fox
Bamboo Fox.description: A lean russet mana fox with green-black ear tips, a long brush tail and narrow pale eyes. It uses bamboo cover and a small misleading rustle rather than human speech or broad illusion mastery. Territorial animals can retreat, hunt or defend young; they are not automatically helpful pets.

Moss-Tongue Kodama.name: Moss-Tongue Kodama
Moss-Tongue Kodama.description: A small bark-bodied forest spirit with a round knotted face, dark sap eyes, two root legs and a long mossy tongue. It tastes rain and rearranges little offerings. Usually curious or mischievous; an actual polluted or damaged shelter can provoke it. It is neither a child nor a compulsory combat target.

Antler-Moss Boar.name: Antler-Moss Boar
Antler-Moss Boar.description: A dark bristled boar with pale rootlike growths over its brow and short moss-covered antler branches. It turns soft soil and follows fallen fruit. A fence gap, seasonal food and clear escape routes matter more than an invented grudge against all humans.

Boundary Tengu.name: Boundary Tengu
Boundary Tengu.description: An adult bird-featured mountain yokai with a long beaked face, dark feathered wings, humanlike hands and red-brown travel layers. It guards a particular claimed crossing and can bargain, bluff or fight. Wings and local knowledge do not make it omniscient or sovereign over every mountain.

Cinder Umbrella.name: Cinder Umbrella
Cinder Umbrella.description: An awakened paper umbrella with one amber eye beneath a scorched rim, a wooden shaft leg and a ragged tongue of warm ash. It hops, spins and spits small hot flecks, usually around abandoned shelter or mishandled offerings. It can be dangerous without becoming an explosive city-destroying artifact.

Paper-Face Lurker.name: Paper-Face Lurker
Paper-Face Lurker.description: A tall loose arrangement of old paper masks around a thin dark frame. One face turns at a time while folded paper fingers test doors and rails. It uses blind angles and limited decoys; the moving frame is real and can be pinned or disrupted.

Scree Crab.name: Scree Crab
Scree Crab.description: A low slate-shelled crawler with six jointed legs, two broad foreclaws and orange seam eyes. It wedges among stones and scrapes mineral surfaces. Falling debris and occupied crevices telegraph it; it is not automatically a giant quarry boss.

Kiln Ashling.name: Kiln Ashling
Kiln Ashling.description: A small round ash creature with a red ember belly, thin soot arms and a wide pale mouth. It follows hot waste and cools into a sleepy lump when deprived of heat. Newly licensed jobs use small weak individuals, not a spontaneous inferno.

Crystal Centipede.name: Crystal Centipede
Crystal Centipede.description: A many-legged dark centipede with glassy amber mineral plates and long jointed antennae. It follows seepage and vibrations through mine cracks. Its armored back has gaps between segments; driving it toward a supported side passage can avoid fighting beneath an unstable brace.

Stone-Eating Centipede.name: Stone-Eating Centipede
Stone-Eating Centipede.description: A heavy gray segmented cave predator with grinding mouth plates and pale sensing whiskers. It rasps tracks through soft seams and can undermine loose rock. Deep occupied galleries are optional dangerous ground; an ordinary miner does not inherit its level or tier.

Storm-Kite Tengu.name: Storm-Kite Tengu
Storm-Kite Tengu.description: A gray-blue feathered adult tengu with long kite-like wings, dark eyes and a pale hooked beak. Conductive ornaments rattle along its flight feathers. It uses wind and limited electrical releases around exposed ridges; it must land, see and recover like a real opponent.

Whitefall Crane.name: Whitefall Crane
Whitefall Crane.description: A tall white mana crane with black wing tips, pale gold eyes and narrow green-blue streamers trailing from its crown feathers. It inhabits water edges and makes short startling sound calls. It is a living creature, not automatically Oroha or a tame spiritual guide.

Snow-Mantle Tengu.name: Snow-Mantle Tengu
Snow-Mantle Tengu.description: An adult white-and-charcoal feathered mountain yokai with heavy talons, a narrow beaked face and a cloak of insulating down. It claims sheltered ledges, seeks food and can negotiate passage. Cold terrain familiarity is not invulnerability to every Ice spell.

Ice-Reed Serpent.name: Ice-Reed Serpent
Ice-Reed Serpent.description: A long dark aquatic mana beast with translucent reedlike dorsal fins, silver eyes and a broad flattened jaw. Its fins scrape across thin ice before its body rises. It hunts vibration and movement in cold water rather than appearing instantly on a refuge floor.

Snowburrow Mukade.name: Snowburrow Mukade
Snowburrow Mukade.description: A broad white-plated centipede with red seam markings and two long black antennae. It travels below snow over loose ground, leaving a settling trough and a dry scraping noise. A raised moraine or prepared hard platform limits its approach.

Hollow War Armor.name: Hollow War Armor
Hollow War Armor.description: An empty lacquered armor frame tied around a residual Soul working. Its joints creak and its head follows an old guard line; it may repeat orders or resist entry. Determine whether it carries a conscious spirit rather than assuming every animated frame contains a person.

Paper-Face Moth.name: Paper-Face Moth
Paper-Face Moth.description: A thumb-to-palm-sized ivory moth with ink-like spots resembling a little face and delicate serrated wing edges. It feeds on damp paper fibers and gathers near fresh paste. Most are nuisance wildlife, with small finite groups and ordinary practical countermeasures.

Granary Rat.name: Granary Rat
Granary Rat.description: An ordinary small brown-gray rat with dark eyes and a pale belly. It steals accessible food, hides behind shelving and escapes when threatened. Beginner jobs use one exposed weak rat at a time and practical gaps, not an elite swarm or compulsory disease outbreak.

Whisper-Reed Oniwa.name: Whisper-Reed Oniwa
Whisper-Reed Oniwa.description: A reed-bodied spirit with long leaf fingers, a hollow stem throat and shifting pale eye marks. It repeats a few heard sounds to draw attention into wet ground. Touch, observation and a changed route can expose its trick; it cannot know private memories it never encountered.

Reed-Jaw Kappa.name: Reed-Jaw Kappa
Reed-Jaw Kappa.description: A squat river yokai with dark green pebbled skin, broad webbed feet, a dull shell and a flat reed-fringed head basin. Adults have varied temperaments and can bargain over a real crossing; a powerful grip and water familiarity make a hostile one dangerous. It is not automatically a childlike mascot.

Orchard Sootling.name: Orchard Sootling
Orchard Sootling.description: A little black-furred round creature with enormous pale eyebrows, tiny paws and a warm amber belly. It hides among fruit baskets and licks sweet spills. Usually mischievous, easily redirected and not a disguised high-level assassin.

Paddy Mudling.name: Paddy Mudling
Paddy Mudling.description: A small wet clay body with pebble eyes, broad paddle feet and a sprout on its head. It blocks a channel to hold a comfortable pool. Moving water, a more attractive puddle or a careful physical removal can solve a nuisance without battle.

Lantern Prowler.name: Lantern Prowler
Lantern Prowler.description: A lean long-legged predator with bark-brown fur, two pale lamps of eyes and a split tufted tail. Its flank markings break its outline among hanging lanterns. Rustles and briefly reflected eyes give warning; it is not a free unseen opening critical attack.

Root-Back Nue.name: Root-Back Nue
Root-Back Nue.description: A heavy forest beast with a primate-like face, feline forequarters, a long scaled tail and pale rootlike growths along its dark back. It waits on overhead roots and attacks from a committed pounce. Its strange body is not proof of limitless abilities or a secret human identity.

Mist-Lure Wisp.name: Mist-Lure Wisp
Mist-Lure Wisp.description: A floating knot of pale blue light around a tiny dark seed. It repeats short heard calls and drifts above unsafe ground. The voice can be tested by echoes and line of sight. It does not erase a character’s recorded memories, move inventory or teleport the party.

Marsh-Stilt Haunt.name: Marsh-Stilt Haunt
Marsh-Stilt Haunt.description: A narrow spirit body balanced on four extremely long black reed legs, with a pale hanging veil around two golden eyes. It crosses deep marsh pools and probes close movement with its front legs. Dry raised ground denies part of its reach.

Echo-Hide Stalker.name: Echo-Hide Stalker
Echo-Hide Stalker.description: A low six-legged predator with slate-blue skin, a smooth eyeless brow and pale listening membranes along its sides. It hunts repeated vibration and can mimic a short sound. It has no private knowledge of the person whose voice it resembles.

Empty Festival Husk.name: Empty Festival Husk
Empty Festival Husk.description: An animated festival effigy with a hollow reed torso, torn bright cloth and a painted wooden face. A residual working repeats a limited procession or invitation. It may accept a properly ended ritual or need physical disruption; it is not every lost ancestor at once.

Tanuki Wayfarer.name: Tanuki Wayfarer
Tanuki Wayfarer.description: An adult raccoon-dog yokai with expressive animal features, a thick tail and practical borrowed clothing. Individuals may use modest Illusion workings and enjoy bargaining or mischief. They cannot create permanent money from leaves or automatically turn into any named person.

Awakened Bell.name: Awakened Bell
Awakened Bell.description: An old bell given movement and personality through a particular history. Its metal body, cords and chime establish its anatomy rather than an added human torso. A ringing interruption and petty mischief are plausible; authority over all spirits is not.

Hush Crane.name: Hush Crane
Hush Crane.description: A rare intelligent crane spirit with actual wings, long legs and an individual attachment to a place or agreement. Identity, disposition and history belong to the actual being. Oroha is the authored crane at its crossing; do not generate replacements with its name or role.

Riftlimb Stalker.name: Riftlimb Stalker
Riftlimb Stalker.description: Reserved anatomical classification for the unique authored Hagire: a towering woman-shaped forest yokai with two long arms, two long legs, a ragged split mouth and joints that can unseat and reset. Do not spawn copies or use this as a renewable random encounter. Use Hagire’s actual record, whereabouts, hostility and resolved condition.

Tideglass Shrimp.name: Tideglass Shrimp
Tideglass Shrimp.description: Thumb-sized transparent shrimp whose blue organs flash in bright rock pools. They graze on algae and retreat into cracks; a panicked group can spoil delicate samples without becoming a lethal swarm.

Brinecap Slime.name: Brinecap Slime
Brinecap Slime.description: A small low dome of salty translucent jelly carrying a cap of trapped foam. It follows mineral runoff, clings to nets and stings bare skin; fresh water and a suitable container can redirect it.

Inkpot Cuttlefish.name: Inkpot Cuttlefish
Inkpot Cuttlefish.description: A clever, hand-sized marine animal with a dark mantle and two broad silver eyes. It imitates the texture beneath it and squirts ink when cornered. It is an animal, not a secret speaking scholar.

Hookbeak Gull.name: Hookbeak Gull
Hookbeak Gull.description: A heavy white-and-gray gull with a curved rust-colored bill. It steals fish and glossy objects from open baskets and defends a nearby nest. Feeding, covering cargo or leaving its ledge can avoid a fight.

Sailcloth Moth.name: Sailcloth Moth
Sailcloth Moth.description: A cream-colored coastal moth with wing markings resembling tiny knots. Its larvae eat damp canvas and grain sacks; an adult scatters irritating powder. Finding the source matters more than swatting one moth.

Kelpclaw Crab.name: Kelpclaw Crab
Kelpclaw Crab.description: A squat green crab whose flat foreclaws collect strips of living kelp. It braces in the surf and snaps at hands reaching into its refuge. A stick, bait and sensible footwear are useful.

Bellfin Shoal.name: Bellfin Shoal
Bellfin Shoal.description: Small blue fish with hollow translucent fins that ring together when startled. A school can confuse shouted boat signals, but the fish ordinarily flee. Light and sound lure them in different directions.

Shoalglass Ray.name: Shoalglass Ray
Shoalglass Ray.description: A broad pale ray with translucent wing edges and a stony central spine. It rests beneath clear sand and discharges a short magical jolt when stepped on. A visible sand outline gives careful waders warning.

Mooring Mimic.name: Mooring Mimic
Mooring Mimic.description: A small mimic resembling a damp coil of rope with an attached wooden float. Its sticky underside grabs careless hands; tugging hard tightens it. It cannot imitate a whole vessel or read a person’s thoughts.

Barnacle Brute.name: Barnacle Brute
Barnacle Brute.description: A barrel-sized crustacean with two mismatched pincers and a back armored in pale barnacles. It scavenges flooded holds and pins loose timber across entrances. Moving its food can draw it away from a narrow passage.

Undertow Eel.name: Undertow Eel
Undertow Eel.description: A long dark-green eel with pale jointed jaw plates and a thin violet line along its flanks. It makes short pulling currents around wreck crevices. The current weakens away from its refuge; it cannot drag someone across the sea.

Salt-Crest Wyvern.name: Salt-Crest Wyvern
Salt-Crest Wyvern.description: A lean two-legged, two-winged coastal predator with salt-white head spines and a hooked tail. It circles exposed nesting rocks and takes fish or unattended catches. It is a wyvern, not a sacred speaking dragon.

Reedlace Sprite.name: Reedlace Sprite
Reedlace Sprite.description: A finger-length wingless plant creature with translucent seed-pod limbs and a fringe of reed leaves. It knots loose fishing line around warm stakes to build a shelter. Its mischievous behavior has a practical animal-like pattern rather than malicious omniscience.

Tangletooth Otter.name: Tangletooth Otter
Tangletooth Otter.description: A sleek brown otter with a pale throat and small branching ivory teeth. It collects tools that rattle and hides them in a dry bank. It can bite when cornered but prefers a chase to a fight.

Burdock Lurker.name: Burdock Lurker
Burdock Lurker.description: A low, six-legged woodland browser hidden beneath a coat of hooked seed burrs. It drags sacks and low cloth into its nest while foraging. Its blunt face and slow defensive roll distinguish it from a vicious wolf.

Chalkback Ram.name: Chalkback Ram
Chalkback Ram.description: A sturdy grassland sheep with pale stony plates along its spine and broad curling horns. A territorial adult knocks against carts and gates during the rut. Its lowered head and stamping hoof signal a charge before contact.

Health.name: Health
Health.usageInstructions:
Health tracks current bodily harm. Combat results, item effects, and typed resource effects are authoritative: never apply their damage or healing a second time.
Outside already resolved combat, deduct Health only for a new concrete injury, damaging exposure, poison, disease, or an explicitly established health cost. For an otherwise unspecified new injury use roughly 5% of maximum Health for minor harm, 15% for serious harm, and 30% for severe harm; actual circumstances and supplied results take precedence. Never add harm for the same wound on subsequent turns merely because it still hurts.
Do not deduct for talking, ordinary exertion, being frightened, a dangerous atmosphere, remembering an injury, or being carried. Recurring harm needs an active cause actually continuing to injure the character.
Clean Bandages restore 8 Health and a Standard Healing Draught restores 25 Health when actually used, following their item definitions once. Other authored treatments follow their own stated effect. If a Healing Magic attempt has no more specific effect, successful basic restoration is about 10% of maximum Health, moderate 25%, powerful 40%, and extreme 60%, matching the mana scale; resolve resistance, failure, and actual limits before applying it.
The engine restores 1 Health per tick and a full pool on an actual rest (restRechargeMultiplier 1). Never add another tick's healing in prose. A conversation or a declaration of comfort is not a completed rest. Health recovery does not reverse aging, cure permanent injuries, or silently remove an established underlying condition.
Use the active death rules and supplied character state. Passive recharge and ordinary rest never revive a dead character. Explicit recovery or revival follows the active mode and actual effect; do not add a second restoration or bypass permadeath.
Zero usable Mana alone is not an injury, unconsciousness, death, or a reason to deduct Health. Ordinary casting never purchases a spell with vital mana. Restored Health or Mana does not automatically reverse a separately established soul shock; actual physical and medical conditions remain distinct.

Mana.name: Mana
Mana.usageInstructions:
Mana tracks usable internal casting mana, not every particle sustaining the soul. Only spend the acting caster's Mana, once for a committed working. Existing effects and actual item use take precedence. An explicit cost overrides the fallback: minor 1-3, basic 6, moderate 14, powerful 30, extreme 55 Mana. Scope, actual knowledge and control still matter. Do not charge for an idea, study, observing another spell, an ordinary physical strike, or an already paid effect's description.
Ordinary casting never spends the protected life-sustaining remainder and never pays an Mana deficit with Health. An unaffordable spell normally fizzles. At exactly zero usable Mana the caster remains conscious; a deliberately forced last spell may very rarely work only after an exceptionally difficult authoritative check. Repeated forcing causes migraines and can prevent further casting until recovery. Do not grant free repeated spells, automatic success, negative ordinary-casting Mana, unconsciousness from zero alone, or access to the vital reserve.
Actual hostile extraction below the usable threshold would cause unconscious soul shock; no witnessed humanoid practitioner or routine Void drain is established. Do not invent such an attack, automatic death, new resource, or disability merely because the pool is low. A genuine shock would persist independently of restored Mana and ordinary rest.
NORMAL RECOVERY: No Mana is restored per turn, combat exchange, conversation, walking, class attendance, or idle narration. A genuinely completed rest restores the usable pool through restRechargeMultiplier 1. An actual advance of the party's day counter also permits one full recovery to each character's actual current maximum; the daily recovery cue marks that event once. A time-of-day change, mentioning tomorrow, or planning to sleep is not a new day or completed rest. Apply supplied recovery only once. Potions, permitted external-reserve use and explicit recovery techniques retain their stated effects. Pool recovery does not cure soul shock or an independently established condition.
Capacity has a partly inherited starting point and grows through use. The existing base and level gains are game abstractions; no new universal biological formula or automatic additional gain per cast is defined. Ordinary food is not a mana potion. Regulated mana medicines can restore only the preparation's actual stated effect, once after real use; excess standard doses cause illness and poor return, not fatal overdose. A focus is not automatically a battery. External stored-mana assistance and mana potions are forbidden during active tournament duels, but emergency care after an official stop is allowed.

Quiet Meridian is the reviewed master Arcane recovery technique. After its actual uninterrupted recovery action, restore exactly 5 Mana to its caster once, capped by the real maximum. This explicit recovery action costs no Mana or Stamina and supplies no passive regeneration. It cannot be combined with an attack, another spell or demanding exertion in that exchange; active hostile interruption prevents the recovery. The authored ten-turn cooldown governs its reuse, including cosmetic restatements. Knowing the ability alone does not supply another passive regeneration or a full refill. Apply an already supplied recovery effect once, never once from the ability and again from this instruction.

Stamina.name: Stamina
Stamina.usageInstructions:
Stamina tracks demanding physical exertion and martial technique. Ordinary attacks, routine guard or defense, normal walking, conversation and unhurried travel are free. Spend only for a committed special maneuver or an actually sustained strenuous effort; naming a technique or describing intent is not expenditure.
Use an authored technique’s cost first. Fallback costs are light 4, standard 8, demanding 14, powerful 22 and extreme 35 Stamina for a real committed action. A spent attack normally stays spent on a miss. Apply a supplied effect once; do not add another charge for its narration or separately tax every flourish. Sustained exertion needs an actual continuing cause.
Pure spells spend Mana, not an automatic Stamina fee. A technique combining demanding bodily delivery and magic can explicitly spend both, with one primary accuracy resolution. Basic physical delivery with a small magical infusion need not become two demanding actions. Never pay an unaffordable Stamina cost with Health or Mana by default.
At zero, the person can still speak, move carefully, make ordinary attacks, defend routinely and seek safety; demanding special exertion must wait or change method. Zero alone is neither unconsciousness nor an injury, a lost turn or instant helplessness. Actual injury and circumstances can impose their own limits.
NORMAL RECOVERY: Stamina has no passive recovery per turn, conversation, class attendance, walking, or idle narration. A genuinely completed rest restores 80% of the current maximum through restRechargeMultiplier 0.8, capped at that maximum. An actual advance of the party's day counter also permits one full recovery to each character's actual current maximum, once for that transition. A new time-of-day label or a promise to rest does not qualify. Apply supplied recovery only once; explicit item or ability recovery keeps its stated effect. Healing Health does not automatically refill Stamina. Capacity starts at 100 and grows by 2 per character level.

Renown.name: Renown
Renown.usageInstructions:
Renown tracks the character's publicly established positive reputation, prestige, and recognition for accomplishments. It is not morality, personal friendship, political authority, character level, or proof that everyone admires them. The value ranges from 0 to 100.

INCREASE: Award approximately 1-2 for small publicly recognized accomplishments, 3-5 for significant local achievements, 6-10 for major city-wide accomplishments, and 10-15 for genuinely historic achievements. Appropriate examples include distinguished tournament victories, widely recognized research discoveries, successful public commissions, exceptional professional achievements, and publicly credited heroic deeds. Award only when the achievement and a credible means of public recognition are established. A private accomplishment does not automatically change Renown; recognition can occur later when its story actually spreads.

DECREASE: Reduce Renown only when an established public reputation is meaningfully damaged, such as through a credible exposed deception, widely acknowledged disgrace, or a demonstrated loss of public confidence. A private mistake, ordinary defeat, personal disagreement, or an unsupported rumor does not automatically reduce Renown. The size of a decrease should match the established impact.

STAGES: 0 Unknown; 1-19 Recognized; 20-39 Well-Known; 40-59 Distinguished; 60-79 Celebrated; 80-100 Legendary. These stages indicate general positive recognition, not universal knowledge or guaranteed approval.

GAMEPLAY: Established Renown can influence invitations, public expectations, professional opportunities, tournament attention, sponsorship offers, academic recognition, and credible social reactions. NPCs must have a plausible reason to know of the character. Renown is not an automatic persuasion bonus, guaranteed discount, legal immunity, or compulsory NPC admiration. High Renown can bring scrutiny, rivalry, and responsibilities as well as opportunities. No opportunity, position, quest, or obligation is automatically accepted on the player's behalf.

INDEPENDENCE: Renown and Infamy are separate. Both may increase from the same genuinely consequential event if public reactions justify it. Never subtract one merely because the other increased. Apply each event's supported change once; never repeatedly reward the same deed through retelling, conversation, or successive turns. If a trigger already changed the value, do not apply the change again. No passive recharge, rest recovery, or automatic gains from leveling, casting, fighting, wealth, or ordinary activity.

Infamy.name: Infamy
Infamy.usageInstructions:
Infamy tracks the character's publicly established negative reputation, notoriety, fear, and distrust arising from known or credibly believed actions. It is not an evil alignment, criminal record, morality score, or proof that accusations are true. The value ranges from 0 to 100.

INCREASE: Award approximately 1-2 for minor but noteworthy public misconduct, 3-5 for significant local scandals or notorious incidents, 6-10 for major city-wide controversies or widely feared deeds, and 10-15 for genuinely historic acts that become broadly notorious. Examples include exposed serious crimes, publicly witnessed cruelty, dangerous misconduct, credible scandals, notorious betrayals, and extraordinary acts that inspire widespread fear. The underlying action must occur or a consequential accusation must credibly spread. Private actions with no established information channel do not automatically increase Infamy. Being powerful, using unusual magic, winning a fair fight, refusing a request, or being disliked by one NPC is insufficient by itself.

DECREASE: Reduce Infamy when meaningful public developments actually weaken the notorious reputation, such as credible exoneration, disproven accusations, widely recognized restitution, sustained publicly demonstrated reform, or a substantial change in public understanding. Private apologies and one isolated kind deed do not instantly erase widespread notoriety. The change must reflect the actual audience and impact.

STAGES: 0 Unknown; 1-19 Whispered About; 20-39 Notorious; 40-59 Feared; 60-79 Dreaded; 80-100 Infamous Legend. These stages reflect the strength of negative reputation, not universal hostility or guaranteed knowledge of the character.

GAMEPLAY: Established Infamy may produce guarded reactions, rumors, investigations, social suspicion, rival challenges, intimidation opportunities, invitations from disreputable groups, or greater attention from authorities. These consequences require relevant knowledge, context, and plausible NPC motivations. High Infamy does not automatically cause arrest, hostility, fear, pursuit, combat, or refusal of all services. NPCs remain individuals, and some may admire actions others condemn. Crimes require actual evidence and jurisdiction for legal consequences. Never automatically impose punishment or force player decisions merely because a threshold is reached.

INDEPENDENCE: Infamy and Renown can coexist at high values. A controversial achievement can increase both when justified, but neither resource automatically offsets the other. Apply supported changes once per distinct reputation-changing development, not for every witness, retelling, or subsequent turn. If a trigger already changed the resource, do not apply it again. There is no passive recharge, ordinary rest recovery, automatic level scaling, or gradual decay without an established reputation-changing event.

Require an actual completed killing or destruction and clear malicious intent. A peaceful victim defending against the player's unprovoked attack is not a legitimate hostile enemy. Exclude accidents, self-defense, hostile-enemy combat, lawful duels, mere threats, plans, jokes, accusations, old incidents, remembered crimes, single-building damage, petty theft, ordinary assault, and torture alone. Do not reinterpret a failed or innocent action as evil.

narratorStyle:
Narrate a vivid fantasy-anime ensemble adventure in clear third-person present tense. Show an inviting world through distinctive clothes, expressive faces, food, weather, craft, streets and striking landscapes. Give an important arrival room to breathe; keep a quick exchange quick. Use a few precise sensory details and readable movement rather than decorative haze.
Comedy grows from conviction, clashing priorities, vanity, bad timing and consequences. Commit to a character's ridiculousness without erasing their competence or laundering cruelty, stupidity and selfishness into secret kindness. Serious danger, tenderness and loss deserve sincerity; quiet life can stay peaceful.
Let classroom life, work, shopping, journeys, rivalries and chosen romance develop through specific people. Distinct voices carry different cadence, warmth, profanity and reserve. Keep close to the player and those actually present; distant acquaintances need no cutaway. Attraction and friendship grow through actual exchanges, not universal admiration.
Action has clear positions, momentum, impact and tactics. A sword, fist, shield, clever tool, negotiation or retreat deserves as much attention as a spectacular spell. The setting welcomes warriors, craftspeople, travelers and noncasters as well as mages. Render authoritative outcomes; never invent extra hits, injuries, victories or powers for spectacle.
Resolve the chosen action and its immediate response, then leave a real opening to act. Vary endings without a compulsory cliffhanger, menu or mood summary. Never invent the player's dialogue, feelings, consent or next decision. Preserve continuity, finite resources and the authored cast's knowledge and flaws.

storySettings.worldBackground:
Glowhaven is a mostly human, self-governing city and its surrounding countryside, built around the Evertree. Legend credits the city's four founding archmages with planting it together. Its roots and canopy gather unusually dense currents of mana: something a practiced caster can almost feel against the skin. People come here to learn, make a living from magic, buy excellent enchanted work, or build a life among others who understand that fascination. The streets belong to porters, cooks, repairers and families as much as celebrated mages.

Magic is commonplace; mastery is earned. Ordinary residents often know a few useful cantrips, while serious practitioners study theory, technique and several disciplines. An affinity makes its school easier to learn, without closing off other schools. A spell requires actual knowledge and usable mana; expensive equipment and an impressive pedigree cannot supply either. Warriors, spellblades, unarmed fighters, craftspeople and noncasters have meaningful places here. Training, physical ability, preparation, tools and cooperation matter alongside spectacular spellwork.

Four rival academies offer broadly comparable magical education through a four-year adult program. Students follow required morning lessons and balance assigned afternoon preparation and practical work with breaks, relationships and outside commitments. Phoenix Wing, in red, connects its teaching to defense, public readiness and protective fieldwork. Cyan-clad Gryffin Tail maintains the strongest research infrastructure and the academies' formal magitech specialization. Dragon Hoard, in yellow and gold, turns strict inherited traditions toward exploration, relic assessment and bringing discoveries home responsibly. Violet Hydra Head connects scholarship to diplomacy, trade, logistics and community work. These are institutional responsibilities, not personality tests: every campus contains gifted fools, ordinary workers, ambitious rivals and people who contradict its reputation. Their disagreements concern methods, influence, resources and service as well as trophies.

Each academy's exceptionally capable Archon represents it on the Conclave of Archons; its headmaster runs the school. A larger governing council elects the Great Sage, who leads Glowhaven and tends the Evertree's magical weave. The court, influential houses, civic offices and academy leadership have overlapping interests rather than a single shared agenda. City guards handle everyday law enforcement; the Sage's elite service handles exceptional threats and important missions. Power brings influence, but developing a country still requires administrators, builders, money and public trust.

Glowhaven lives through farms, fisheries, harbor trade and the production of prized enchanted goods. A faulty household charm can matter as much to its owner as a lost relic does to a scholar. Markets, boutiques, taverns, workshops and rural settlements connect people across school and class. Noble titles, property, patronage and family connections create opportunity and friction. Festivals fill the calendar; the coliseum's tournaments make local rivalries a public spectacle.

Beyond this region, authorized Evertree passage connects to the snowy dragonkin-majority city of Drakenspire and the fae sky archipelago of Asterveil. Exploration reaches unfamiliar communities with their own work, customs and dangers. Use the established geography and its real routes; the world does not expand into a new country whenever someone walks beyond a gate.

The experience is a colorful fantasy ensemble adventure: lively school comedy, rivalries, chosen romance, ordinary pleasures and earnest action with room for epic stakes. Humor comes from specific people and incompatible convictions. Let kindness, vanity, cruelty, laziness and courage remain real. Peaceful days need no hidden catastrophe. The player may seek study, work, friendship, profit, exploration or power, gathering a few close companions from a much wider living cast. Existing people have lives beyond the player's attention, and the story takes their choices and consequences seriously.
storySettings.questGenerationGuidance:
OPPORTUNITIES AND AGREEMENT
Start with a person, concrete want and circumstance the player can act on. Reuse nearby authored people and acquaintances. A posting needs a client, terms and return contact. Offer two or three suitable possibilities when work is requested. Public news, overheard disagreements and visible problems can invite investigation without accepting or creating a journal entry. Ignore an unpursued lead rather than repeating it. Ordinary kindness and conversations need not become quests.

LOCAL CHARACTER
Academies: actual courses, teachers, years, experiments, contests, favors and rivalries. Their civic duties suggest work without dictating personality. The academic sequence keeps its own readiness and invitations.
Guild: finite contracts, hunts, escorts, recovery, repairs and professional disputes. Check the actual Bronze/Silver/Gold/Platinum badge. Pay the full posted fee; court keys and property permission remain separate.
Drakenspire: mountain routes, craft, clans, households, ancestors, pit contests and winter supplies. Terrain, promises and material needs create pressure; rare beings are not guaranteed appointments.
Asterveil: crossings, rescue, specimens, materials, research and competing expeditions. Distinguish Cloudbloom woodland, Rimeglass exposure, Mirrorwater channels and Amethyst acoustic terrain. Follow actual local bands and npcTypes; this remains midgame.
Everyday Glowhaven: food, music, neighbors, shopping, repairs and personal trouble. Simple work can end simply. Lawful prison work uses actual permission and never grants release just for finishing an errand.

PLAYABLE RESISTANCE
For substantial work, identify the obstacle, its location, how it blocks success and what resolves it. Use an actual rescue, contest, magical working, hazardous crossing, negotiation, fight or demonstrated result. Deliberately entering occupied dangerous ground produces the real encounter, not tracks forever. Tools, preparation, training and cooperation matter. Vary physical, magical, social and investigative approaches; animals are not negotiators by default.

QUESTS AND NATIVE ARCS
Most generated work is a finite standalone episode. Use configured arcs only for their actual premises, participants, secrets and expected conclusions; generated chapters belong to the runtime arc rather than an invented authored arcId. One meaningful development and its consequences justify another chapter. Preserve discoveries after a setback. Do not force every arc onto one player or split several simultaneous errands serving one goal into separate quests. Arc participants retain independent lives and motives. Respect credible alternative conclusions and do not restart a resolved arc merely to supply more content.

CHECKABLE ENDINGS
Give a generated quest a concrete final objective and a typed completionCondition repeating that final step's wording with the full relevant person, item and place names. Allow the stated alternatives and genuine imperfect results when appropriate. A proposal, quoted objective or unperformed promise does not qualify. Once achieved, let the scene show the deed plainly; no extra signatures, report loops or new mastermind are required. Failure can change cost, approach or relationships without erasing every clue.

CONTINUITY AND REWARDS
Compare active, planned, completed, declined and abandoned work by people, site and problem, not title alone. Preserve solved conditions; recurring work needs a fresh instance and terms. First thesis is once per playthrough, including transfers. Academic milestones, field tests, expeditions, the anomaly and Silken investigation retain separate conditions. No automatic calendar jump, acceptance, pass, recruitment or absent-participant credit.
State known risk, scope and payment before commitment. Respect refusal and withdrawal. Use one supported completion and reward owner; authored effects settle their fixed reward once. No duplicate prose payment or credit for unrelated work. Loans, salvage and customer property follow real agreements. Access, lessons and company can matter beside money; no generic reward grants affinity, mastery, court keys or affection.

INFORMED RISK
Routine work fits the least experienced human, excluding powerful NPC companions. Introductory Bronze work normally uses one level 1–3 weak hostile. Substantially harder work needs explicit player interest and concrete warning before acceptance. Offer a safer option instead of a surprise lethal mission. Existing scripted events, authored encounters and their conditions remain unchanged.

ASSESSMENT SAMPLES
Guild judgment examples, practice notices and classroom hypotheticals are not live contracts or new journal quests. Generate no job from an exam sample. First licensure remains its existing quest; real work needs a separate actual offer. For configured contracts keep the exact client, place and fee; accept only the single identified chosen offer.

mundane.rarityGuidance: Common everyday goods, broadly available in this world.

Follow the permitted per-pick ranges. Maintenance adds no bonus pick; non-equippable goods have no equipment bonuses.
artisan.rarityGuidance: Uncommon goods made by skilled craftspeople or specialists.

tips: Natural affinity makes a discipline easier to learn. Starting studies determine which magic and introductory spells you already know.
Creating or substantially redesigning a spell uses Spellcraft. Casting a learned spell uses its magical discipline.
Your First Spell can be a tiny practical invention. Start with one useful effect and a safe test.
You can study magic outside your affinities. A good teacher, practice and a useful book can all help.
Simple spell experiments can be brief. Difficult inventions may need research, materials and several attempts.
Force and Finesse support martial styles. You do not need to be a spellcaster to become an adventurer.
Demanding techniques use Stamina; spells use Mana. Ordinary movement and basic attacks remain useful.
A staff, wand or grimoire helps control learned magic. Owning one does not teach every spell.
Morning academy classes follow your issued timetable. Check it when you are unsure where to go.
Every academy teaches Magic Theory, but its other courses and professors differ.
The Crucible is an optional place to seek combat, not a compulsory school appointment.
Guild membership begins with its licensure exam. A badge determines which guild jobs you can accept.
A posted guild reward is the amount you earn for completing the agreed work.
Portal permission comes from the Great Sage’s Court. A guild badge is not a portal key.
The Evertree Base is Glowhaven’s portal hub. A return crossing brings you to its Portal Room.
A portal key remains an actual carried item. Check your inventory before planning a crossing.
Drakenspire is known for exceptional spellblade weapons, mountain resources and its sacred dragons.
Asterveil is wilderness with dangerous wildlife. Preparation, company and a retreat route matter.
Wraith Island lies offshore; its prison admits authorized visitors and workers as well as inmates.
A prisoner can ask to serve the remainder quietly and skip uneventful time.
Guards can demand surrender. A demand is not the same thing as a completed arrest.
Health, Mana, Stamina, Renown and Infamy describe different parts of your character’s current situation.
Public reputation and a particular person’s affection are different. Fame does not make every stranger a friend.
Meeting someone does not recruit them. Companions have their own work, loyalties and reasons to stay.
An NPC knows what they have actually learned. A private conversation is not a reason for them to reveal every secret.
A familiar bond connects people; it does not grant ownership or automatic obedience.
Beastfolk usually have mostly human features. Your selected ears, horns, tail or feathers make the individual.
Fae bodies vary widely. A very short fae can be a fully grown adult.
Portrait style, camera and backdrop choices are optional and do not change your map position or equipment.
Shopping starts with a quote. Browsing or asking a price does not purchase an item.
A useful piece of ordinary equipment can matter as much as a spectacular spell.
You can ask the narrator for a reminder of an agreed task, a timetable or your current options.
An overheard problem is an opportunity, not an accepted quest. Ask for the terms or leave it alone.
A room key or deed records your actual lodging or property agreement. A viewing does not buy the building.
Ordinary repairs restore function. Refinement needs an agreed improvement, suitable materials and real work.
If a genuinely finished quest stays active, type quest done: followed by its exact journal name. This optional repair works on your honor and applies its normal rewards.
A weapon-led charge still uses your actual physical combat method. Giving an ally an order is not your own attack.
Headmasters administer schools. Their office does not automatically make them stronger than their experienced faculty.

death.instructions:
Narrate defeat as a knockout rather than death in this non-permadeath world. Outside custody, the character can awaken treated in a plausible nearby settlement with the established party and belongings. If actually in lawful custody or Wraith Island Prison, awakening takes place under the same custody, usually the infirmary; a knockout never grants release or restores confiscated property into use. Preserve the actual property receipt, case, sentence, warrants, and review. A rescue or escape requires an actual established event rather than a free reset. Recovery should end the immediate defeat without erasing its consequences.
Do not invoke knockout or death merely because usable mana reaches zero. Ordinary spellcasting cannot consume the soul-sustaining remainder. A hypothetical extraction or soul-shock incident requires an actual separately established cause and authoritative outcomes; refilling Mana alone is no resurrection or release from medical care.
PERMADEATH EXCEPTION: In an actual solo run currently using Permadeath Mode, a genuinely lethal defeat receives a final epilogue instead of routine knockout recovery. Nonlethal training or capture is not automatically death. Normal modes retain their established recovery rules.
Regulated Crucible bouts preserve their actual nonlethal intent. A genuine tournament knockout is a sporting loss, not a newly invented lethal event. Capture the loss before describing treatment or recovery; healing never changes the result.

win.instructions: Narrate a satisfying victory ending that celebrates what the party accomplished and resolves the major stakes.

lose.instructions: Narrate a meaningful failure ending that makes the consequences clear while giving the adventure a sense of closure.

end.instructions: Narrate a neutral ending that gracefully closes the adventure and gives the story a final sense of completion.
