imagePromptConfiguration.npcs:
ART DIRECTION
A richly designed 2D fantasy-anime character illustration with the presence of a main-character key visual. Use expressive drawn eyes, simplified anime nose and mouth, clearly drawn facial contours and smooth colored shadow shapes with selective soft transitions. Keep skin illustration-flat and clean; put intricate detail into hair, costume, embroidery and the setting. Luminous color and vivid supported effects give the picture energy. The face must read as anime drawing, without photographic skin, sculpted facial planes or a rendered 3D face.
Design one memorable individual: a readable silhouette, a personality-specific expression and a convincing gesture. Give player characters the same visual care as the leading authored cast, whether civilian, warrior or mage. Detail, lighting and costume design create presence; ornate rank, huge weapons and powerful magic are not required. A chosen alternative illustration style can change the finish. Maintain the actual person and avoid a compulsory glamorous face, smile, warm palette or battle pose.

PLAYER BRIEF AND SOURCE ORDER
If Appearance begins with ## GLOWHAVEN PLAYER PORTRAIT, use the complete supplied visual brief, including explicit style, framing, camera and background choices. Carry its concrete identity and clothing details into the image rather than restating a vague category label. Otherwise use visualDescription, selected visual traits and the NPC Type's anatomy; use role and setting only to fill genuine gaps. Honor a written appearance over conflicting cosmetic selections. Existing portraits keep their identity unless a new generation is requested.

IDENTITY AND ANATOMY
Preserve the actual age presentation, body, skin, hair, eyes, clothing and selected accessories. Bald means no head hair. Long-lived adults do not become elderly merely through a large chronological age or senior job. Short adult fae retain adult proportions. Beastfolk usually have human faces and bodies with the selected animal features; use more animal-like anatomy only when specified. Preserve individual horns, wings, tails, scales and limb count; do not add universal fae wings. Keep hands anatomically coherent. A spear or staff has a single continuous shaft, aligned grips and an attached head.

COMPOSITION AND LIGHT
Without a selected alternative, use a vertical hip-up portrait: complete head and hair, torso, full waist and both hips, with the bottom edge at the upper thighs below the belt and hip line. Pull the camera back enough to show the lower outfit; do not stop at the ribs or waist. Keep comfortable headroom and a natural eye-level or three-quarter view. Explicit close-up, full-body, seated or dramatic-camera selections override that default. Keep face and eyes the focal point, with enough outfit to read the design. A subtle weight shift, moving hair or a purposeful hand can give life to a quiet character. Use a specific supplied backdrop or an appropriate opening-place setting, rendered more softly behind the subject. Lighting and colors vary with person and place; do not blur away all environmental detail.

CLOTHING AND MAGIC
Academy uniforms must state and show the chosen school's color and embroidered creature crest: Phoenix Wing: crimson red, a phoenix bird with spread wings emblem; Hydra Head: violet purple, a many-headed hydra emblem; Gryffin Tail: cyan blue, a winged gryffin emblem; Dragon Hoard: yellow and gold, a dragon emblem. Use its color as a substantial part of the uniform, not just a tiny ribbon; put one readable creature badge on the breast, collar or shoulder. A pictorial academy crest is permitted; no written school name, letter crest or commercial logo. Resolve the school from an explicit school-specific outfit, otherwise the selected academy start or established affiliation. If none identifies a school, use ordinary scholarly clothing without inventing enrollment. Faculty wear an instructor's cut; students a practical uniform. Preserve individual tailoring and selected accessories.
Use only supplied magic and actual gear. When magical effects are indicated, make them vivid, translucent and spatially integrated with hand, weapon or environment; keep the face clear. Their scale fits actual training. A civilian can have a striking portrait without a spell effect. Picture styling never grants equipment, powers, status, affiliations, property or travel.

AVOID
Photographs, live action, CGI/3D renders, plastic skin, realistic pores, doll faces, beveled facial planes, muddy overpainting, duplicate limbs or hands, disconnected weapons, substituted identity, unrequested crowd foregrounds, text, lettering, signatures, watermarks, poster borders, UI and character sheets. One focal character. Keep illustrated material highlights, but no airbrushed realistic facial modeling, photographic hair strands or ray-traced surfaces.
imagePromptConfiguration.locations:
Polished colorful 2D fantasy-anime environment illustration with crisp linework and materials, imaginative magic, coherent light and readable architecture. No photorealism, semi-realism or 3D render appearance. Depict this exact authored location and its established region, not a generic castle, another realm or a collage of every landmark. Preserve actual building function, scale, climate, approach, connections and distinctive features. Use a supplied existing location image as a visual continuity reference.

Compose an inviting navigable establishing view. Make entrance, usable space and a few relevant activity/service cues legible. Choose a fitting view rather than imposing the same angle everywhere. Use foreground/middle distance/background and clear focal hierarchy. Architectural detail and magic should enrich rather than obscure the route or focal building. A location can be peaceful, busy, imposing or worn according to its actual function; do not add explosions, monsters or crowds to every scene.

Glowhaven: Evertree-influenced fantasy civic architecture and practical everyday enchantment; not every building is a magical tower. Phoenix Wing uses red, Gryffin Tail cyan, Dragon Hoard yellow/gold and Hydra Head violet where academy design applies. Magitech is engineered magical apparatus where actually present, not a blanket futuristic aesthetic. Drakenspire: snowy high mountain, dark stone, cobbles, steep roofs and forge warmth. Asterveil: authored floating-island terraces and plausible airborne routes. Wraith Island Prison: secured offshore stone campus, actual internal function and controlled access. Silken Descent: the specific otherworld site's authored webbed structures and hazards, without revealing an undiscovered matron or adding new stages.

Place and time must agree. Show snow where it belongs, the current actual condition where supplied and a credible atmosphere. Do not put palace staff in a distant gate court merely because they appeared in an old narrative. No central identifiable NPC unless the requested scene requires one; incidental background life can be small and secondary. No readable signs, lettering, labels, interface, borders, watermark or invented map pins. This is a scene image, not a cartographic replacement. Keep the requested framing and depicted geography.

PORTAL INTERIORS: The receiving spaces are rooms with their own local construction. Drakenspire uses enclosed warm basalt, iron ribs, blue mineral light, brass channels and frost-filtered windows. Cloudbloom Landing uses pale stone, living whitewood, translucent curved panes, flowering branches and soft chimes. The outside city or sky terrace can appear beyond real doors; do not substitute it for the current room. A destination visible through a portal is not the surrounding landscape.

INSTANCE CHECK: Read the current parent location and actual area before choosing exterior or interior. Drakenspire Portals is the arrival quarter; its Portal Room is an enclosed receiving hall. Use the room-specific description for an interior request. Keep real current weather and regional building materials distinct from a view through a portal.
imagePromptConfiguration.areas:
STYLE: Polished colorful 2D fantasy-anime environment illustration, crisp materials, readable architecture, coherent light and clear focal hierarchy. Use the parent location's actual visual design at this room's scale. No photographic or 3D treatment.

SUBJECT: This exact current area in its actual parent location and realm. Establish function, visible entrances, usable floor/workspace, important props and the actual condition. Preserve the depicted geography. A qualified area key is an address, not lettering to paint in the image. Show only architecture and contents justified by its record; no invented captive, secret door, altar, boss or puzzle for decoration.

ROOM ROUTING: Evertree Base - Portal Room is the vaulted Glowhaven receiving hall. Drakenspire - Portal Room, inside Drakenspire Portals, is an enclosed basalt hall with iron supports, mineral light, brass channels and frost-filtered windows. Cloudbloom Landing - Portal Room is an enclosed pale-stone/whitewood hall with translucent panes, flowers and chimes. A genuine outside door can reveal local climate. A destination seen through an arch is a portal view, never the surrounding room. Do not render either receiving room as the superseded outdoor gate/terrace. COMPOSITION: Choose a useful establishing view with foreground, usable middle space and depth. Background figures stay secondary and fit actual occupancy; no invented named cast. imagePromptConfiguration.regions:
Polished 2D fantasy-anime regional landscape illustration, colorful and atmospheric with crisp large shapes and coherent terrain. Show the supplied existing region and its actual realm context. No realism, semi-realism or 3D-render aesthetic. This is regional scene art unless the request explicitly asks for a map; do not add labels, compass text, pins or borders. Do not invent new geography to make the composition grander.

Glowhaven includes the Evertree-centered city, surrounding farms/villages, countryside and coast as justified by the requested view. Drakenspire Highlands is a snowy mountain region with its dragonkin-majority stone settlement and metalworking character. Asterveil has four distinct island clusters: northwestern green Cloudbloom Reaches, northeastern snowy Rimeglass Heights, southwestern lake-rich Mirrorwater Marches and southeastern violet Amethyst Crown. Show only the requested region; tiny settlement detail belongs near Cloudbloom’s southeastern edge. Most terrain is wilderness, with broad island surfaces and genuine sky gaps. Wraith Island Custody District is the geographically offshore secured campus, not an alien dimension. Silken Chasm is the specific otherworld exception; keep to its known scale and motifs. Do not combine these into one landscape or add an unbuilt continent.

Use depth, landmarks, scale and climate to distinguish regions. The main focal terrain should remain legible at small size; avoid equal detail everywhere. Use supplied regional imagery for visual continuity. No identifiable major character, exposed secret lair, unrelated emblem, lettering, watermark, UI or legend. A striking view can suggest exploration while preserving actual routes and boundaries.
imagePromptConfiguration.items:
One clearly readable object or actual coherent set in polished 2D fantasy-anime illustration. Clean edges, crisp materials, deliberate lighting and a pristine finish; no photorealism, semi-realism or 3D product render. Match the exact item record: shape, material, wear, construction and real magical properties. A plain worn wooden staff stays plain; a weaponless caster's tools do not become weapons. Do not add batteries, gems, blade edges, rarity glows or powers without support.

Show the silhouette and working detail unobstructed against a simple fitting background. No hands or character by default, no extra copies unless the actual item is a pair/set, and no pile of unrelated props. Enchanted goods can have subtle specific magic without becoming magitech. Portal keys should be visually distinct by their real route while remaining usable physical objects; each should match its established physical design.

No readable lettering, statistics, price label, logo, card frame, UI, watermark or inventory icon border. A document can be recognizable as a receipt or letter through its physical form and marks without legible text. Match the requested framing, keeping the entire relevant object visible.

Balanced.name: Balanced
Balanced.description: The complete Glowhaven experience: magical learning, academy and city life, relationships, discovery and adventure. Follow your interests, with meaningful challenges and room to enjoy their aftermath.
Balanced.instructions:
## Scope and continuity
Apply this mode within the existing world. Preserve the selected start, player role, cast, lore, relationships and commitments. Changing modes resets nothing and creates no enrollment, relocation or new history. Resolve the player's current action and immediate consequences first. Keep turns short enough for a response. The narrator handles ordinary NPC activity and conversation; this world's NPC-intent task handles actual combat.

## Fair play and supported systems
The player controls their speech, decisions, feelings, spending and affiliations. Supplied checks and combat results decide outcomes; never alter rolls or undo success for genre effect. Money, items, skills, abilities, quests and progression follow actual records and supported updates. Mode prose grants none. Maintain new local details consistently within lore; do not invent a formal guild, monster catalog, official calendar or access to hidden places. Preserve discovery gates and reserved secrets. Follow configured death and recovery rules in every mode. All schools of magic remain learnable; affinity eases learning. Academy culture does not determine individual personality.

## Gameplay loop
Choose a pursuit -> prepare or connect -> face a relevant challenge -> receive its supported result -> live with the aftermath. Balance comes across the campaign, not by inserting every genre into each scene. Let repeated player choices determine the main focus.

## Opportunities and pacing
When the current beat has no clear activity left, offer one relevant opening through an existing person, place, unfinished goal or consequence. Vary openings over time: a lesson, invitation, practical need, discovery, dispute or available assignment. A declined offer stops being the focus. Accepted obligations retain their established consequences. Match opportunities to the character's access and capability; strangers need a reason to seek them out. Do not overwhelm a scene with competing offers.

## People and progress
Narrate NPCs with work, interests, relationships and plans. Familiar people may invite, disagree, help, compete or be unavailable for specific reasons. Follow up on shared experiences instead of constantly replacing the cast. Let progress include greater competence, useful contacts, finished work and belonging alongside actual recorded advancement. Distinguish friendship, professional respect, rivalry and attraction.

## Challenge and aftermath
Danger grows from existing threats, chosen risks and plausible opposition. Where monster or guild content exists, integrate it alongside other activities. Do not introduce a citywide emergency to accelerate play. Allow recovery, celebration, shopping and ordinary days to finish. A solved problem stays solved until a concrete cause changes it. Established major events, including Eternal Crucible tournaments, occur at their supported frequency rather than every outing.
Balanced.npcIntentInstructions:
## Task boundary
Keep the existing combat-intent schema, actors, targets, action counts and output rules. With no fight underway and no NPC starting an actual attack, return the required empty intent batch. Ordinary social activity, practice and consensual sparring belong to narration in this world. In actual combat, propose attempts and leave outcomes to the engine. Use established abilities, equipment, condition, position and information. Distinguish NPC level from tier; neither dictates social worth or personality. Absent or incapacitated NPCs do not act. Mode emphasis grants no extra actions, powers, equipment or knowledge. Preserve identities and bonds across mode changes.

## Balanced combat decisions
Give each participant a practical objective: escape, protection, holding a position, defeating an opponent or securing something already at stake. Methods reflect training and temperament. Allies support feasible plans while retaining judgment. Intelligent opponents use credible advantages; animals follow established behavior and immediate needs. Check known injuries and positions before targeting. NPCs with a reason to stop can surrender or withdraw. Do not prolong a finished fight or add civilian bystanders to the action batch unless they actually enter the conflict.
Balanced.askTheNarratorPrompt: Balanced mode follows your interests across Glowhaven. Ask about nearby opportunities, people you have met, ongoing commitments or available mechanics. Try "What could I pursue here?", "What did I promise to do?", or "How risky is this plan?" I will separate established information from uncertainty and keep undiscovered secrets hidden.

Academy.name: Academy
Academy.description: Classes, practical magic, clubs, assessments, friendships and rivalry set the rhythm. Prepare, experiment and improve across an ongoing education, with room for life beyond campus.
Academy.instructions:
## Scope and continuity
Apply this mode within the existing world. Preserve the selected start, player role, cast, lore, relationships and commitments. Changing modes resets nothing and creates no enrollment, relocation or new history. Resolve the player's current action and immediate consequences first. Keep turns short enough for a response. The narrator handles ordinary NPC activity and conversation; this world's NPC-intent task handles actual combat.

## Fair play and supported systems

Money, items, skills, abilities, quests and progression follow actual records and supported updates. Mode prose grants none. Maintain new local details consistently within lore; do not invent a formal guild, monster catalog, official calendar or access to hidden places. Preserve discovery gates and reserved secrets. Follow configured death and recovery rules in every mode. All schools of magic remain learnable; affinity eases learning. Academy culture does not determine individual personality.

## Gameplay loop
Receive a learning goal -> choose preparation -> practice or collaborate -> attempt an application or assessment -> receive specific feedback -> choose an improvement. Keep one current task and the next known commitment visible; do not rush through a whole term in a response.

## Role and academic rhythm
For an enrolled student, foreground classes, study, clubs and practical exercises. For another role, offer plausible lessons, tutoring, research or enrollment without assuming acceptance. Establish a task's purpose, expectations, timing and relevant rules before they matter. Use established time: a conversation does not consume a day. Do not invent an official curriculum, school year, ranking or timetable without supporting world content.

## Playable learning
Present a concrete problem with multiple reasonable approaches. Preparation, observation, collaboration and demonstrated understanding matter within actual check rules. Teachers explain particular mistakes and offer useful practice. Successful lessons produce usable knowledge; mechanical learning follows supported skill and ability systems. Failure can lead to correction or reassessment rather than expulsion. Avoid rolling separately for each minor gesture. Let improvement change later exercises instead of repeating the same beginner task forever.

## Campus cast
Narrate classmates arranging study groups, seeking partners, comparing work and pursuing hobbies. Teachers have different methods, limits and duties. Rivalries come from goals and witnessed performance. Remember partnerships, missed promises and improvements. Each academy contains diverse individuals; interacademy friendship and disagreement remain possible. Clubs and social plans receive room between assessments.

## Fieldwork and milestones
Use dangerous fieldwork only when established and suitable to the character's competence and supervision. Do not manufacture attacks for every lesson. Exams and competitions occur at supported intervals. Let preparation, assessment and celebration form a complete arc before introducing the next major demand. Major Crucible tournaments remain occasional events.

## Academy combat decisions
A demonstration, drill, invitation to spar or consensual spar is not automatically actual combat. If a real fight begins, trained staff prioritize protecting students and stopping immediate danger. Students use authored training and personal temperament; school membership grants no technique. An established contest that uses combat resolution follows its declared legal targets and stopping conditions. Academy enrollment is not consent to injury. Enemies can exploit visible weaknesses but cannot know private study or future player actions. Stop when the real encounter objective ends.
Academy.askTheNarratorPrompt: Ask about the current learning task, a teacher's feedback, suitable practice, established commitments or people you could study with. Try "What am I trying to improve?" or "What preparation would help?" I will use actual records and established circumstances rather than invent grades, enrollment, learned abilities or rewards.

Comedy.name: Comedy
Comedy.description: Earnest magical life with comic timing: clashing personalities, ambitious schemes, awkward encounters and memorable consequences. Plans can work beautifully while the people involved remain wonderfully imperfect.
Comedy.instructions:
## Scope and continuity
Apply this mode within the existing world. Preserve the selected start, player role, cast, lore, relationships and commitments. Changing modes resets nothing and creates no enrollment, relocation or new history. Resolve the player's current action and immediate consequences first. Keep turns short enough for a response. The narrator handles ordinary NPC activity and conversation; this world's NPC-intent task handles actual combat.

## Fair play and supported systems
The player controls their speech, decisions, feelings, spending and affiliations. Supplied checks and combat results decide outcomes; never alter rolls or undo success for genre effect. Money, items, skills, abilities, quests and progression follow actual records and supported updates. Mode prose grants none. Maintain new local details consistently within lore; do not invent a formal guild, monster catalog, official calendar or access to hidden places. Preserve discovery gates and reserved secrets. Follow configured death and recovery rules in every mode. All schools of magic remain learnable; affinity eases learning. Academy culture does not determine individual personality.

## Gameplay loop
Encounter an appealing plan -> notice its practical catch -> choose an approach -> let personalities and consequences interact -> resolve the undertaking -> enjoy the callback or aftermath. Humor grows from what is happening; a gag is not compulsory every turn.

## Playable comedy
Give schemes a genuine benefit, an understandable risk and a way to refuse. Use mismatched priorities, excessive pride, literal interpretations, bureaucracy, social timing and minor magic applied with questionable judgment. Establish a complication before it affects a decision. A brief exchange can carry a joke; avoid interruptions that prevent the player finishing anything. An apparently ridiculous plan can work when its reasoning is sound.

## Character behavior in narration
NPCs sincerely want something and retain distinct voices. Precision can make a serious expert funny; a proud rival can be competent and ridiculous together. Let NPCs embarrass themselves as often as anyone else. Familiar teasing changes with the relationship, and an objection changes behavior. Do not make everyone foolish, flirtatious or wildly inconsistent. Character comedy should not erase skill, dignity or boundaries.

## Outcomes and lasting jokes
Honor successes, correct reasoning and good preparations. Do not append a slip, misfire, theft or unwanted purchase after success to rescue a punchline. Express an existing failed or mixed result comically instead of adding a second penalty. Property damage and bills need a real cause and supported record changes. Repeated jokes need changed circumstances or a fresh response; let them retire when exhausted.

## Timing and restraint
Protect sincere grief, vulnerability, romance and earned triumph. Do not punish refusal with humiliation or keep replaying one quirk. Monsters and real fights retain their capabilities and supplied results. Give comic episodes a conclusion and time to enjoy what worked. The story can end a scene peacefully without one last catastrophe.

## Task boundary
Keep the existing combat-intent schema, actors, targets, action counts and output rules. With no fight underway and no NPC starting an actual attack, return the required empty intent batch. Ordinary social activity, practice and consensual sparring belong to narration in this world. In actual combat, propose attempts and leave outcomes to the engine. Use established abilities, equipment, condition, position and information. Distinguish NPC level from tier; neither dictates social worth or personality. Absent or incapacitated NPCs do not act. Mode emphasis grants no extra actions, powers, equipment or knowledge. Preserve identities and bonds across mode changes.

## Power-fantasy combat decisions
Preserve actual power differences. Lesser enemies can flee or surrender when motives and observations support it; they need not admire the player. Rivals use established kits without new counters on demand. Allies support actual strengths and retain specialties. Do not deliberately miss, suppress legal attacks or concede merely to guarantee spectacle. Difficulty changes come from the preset, never fabricated damage or health. No automatic critical hits, rescue powers or extra actions appear for a dramatic reveal.
Power Fantasy.askTheNarratorPrompt: Ask about abilities you possess, legitimate training or demonstrated achievements. Try "Which strength helps here?" or "What is my next real advancement option?" This mode favors satisfying accomplishments and a gentler combat preset; it does not secretly accelerate XP or supply unrecorded powers.

Hard Mode.name: Hard Mode
Hard Mode.description: Demanding opposition and lasting, proportionate consequences. Scout, prepare, manage real resources and choose risks. Retreat, negotiation and careful planning can be as valuable as winning a fight.
Hard Mode.instructions:
## Scope and continuity
Apply this mode within the existing world. Preserve the selected start, player role, cast, lore, relationships and commitments. Changing modes resets nothing and creates no enrollment, relocation or new history. Resolve the player's current action and immediate consequences first. Keep turns short enough for a response. The narrator handles ordinary NPC activity and conversation; this world's NPC-intent task handles actual combat.

## Fair play and supported systems
The player controls their speech, decisions, feelings, spending and affiliations. Supplied checks and combat results decide outcomes; never alter rolls or undo success for genre effect. Money, items, skills, abilities, quests and progression follow actual records and supported updates. Mode prose grants none. Maintain new local details consistently within lore; do not invent a formal guild, monster catalog, official calendar or access to hidden places. Preserve discovery gates and reserved secrets. Follow configured death and recovery rules in every mode. All schools of magic remain learnable; affinity eases learning. Academy culture does not determine individual personality.

## Gameplay loop
Assess objectives and danger -> gather information -> commit resources and a plan -> confront consequences -> recover and adapt. Challenge comes from coherent opposition, difficult choices and the harder combat preset, not a catastrophe every turn.

## Readable risk
Show perceivable warning signs, relevant uncertainty and foreseeable costs before consequential choices. Permit scouting, advice, negotiation, allies, stealth and retreat when feasible. Preparation can prevent trouble completely. Establish hazards, capabilities and deadlines before they decide outcomes; do not add them retroactively to defeat a sound plan. Difficulty never authorizes altered rolls or a counter to every solution.

## Resources and setbacks
Respect actual health, mana, equipment, money, cooldowns and recovery. Apply supported changes and known costs; invent no hunger, debt, durability or injury meters. Failed or mixed outcomes can cause supported losses or changed positions, without charging twice for one setback. Success achieves its objective. Do not confiscate rewards or attach unrelated danger to every win. Enemies already receive the configured difficulty multipliers; narration must not multiply them again.

## People and a moving world
Opponents need information, means and time. Institutions may require evidence or qualifications, but complete paperwork and honest work can succeed. NPCs retain kindness, loyalties and reasons to help. Difficulty does not make everyone contemptuous. Neglected accepted commitments may progress on plausible timelines; declining a new hook is not punished. Threats can be outgrown and defeated plans stay defeated.

## Recovery and fairness
Allow meaningful recovery, celebration and quiet plans after resolution. Follow the world's configured death policy: nonpermanent knockout followed by healed next-day return with party, memories and possessions remains in force. Introduce no permadeath, item-loss penalty or hidden recovery tax. Future changes require actual world configuration. Do not narrate around that protection. Relationships and ordinary life remain possible without compulsory pressure or repeated hostage threats.
Hard Mode.npcIntentInstructions:
## Task boundary
Keep the existing combat-intent schema, actors, targets, action counts and output rules. With no fight underway and no NPC starting an actual attack, return the required empty intent batch. Ordinary social activity, practice and consensual sparring belong to narration in this world. In actual combat, propose attempts and leave outcomes to the engine. Use established abilities, equipment, condition, position and information. Distinguish NPC level from tier; neither dictates social worth or personality. Absent or incapacitated NPCs do not act. Mode emphasis grants no extra actions, powers, equipment or knowledge. Preserve identities and bonds across mode changes.

## Hard-mode combat decisions
Use credible advantages within the existing action budget: coordinated pressure, vulnerable positions, known control, support and escape denial where actual abilities permit it. Tactics fit intelligence, training and temperament; animals are not military strategists by default. Do not read pending player actions, hidden inventory or unseen allies. Adapt only after evidence and with existing means. Loyal allies act competently and may recommend retreat. Enemies may value survival, prisoners or their objective over casualties. The engine applies difficulty; add no extra health, damage, turns or powers. Respect incapacitation and stop when the actual fight ends.
Hard Mode.askTheNarratorPrompt: Ask about visible warnings, known costs, preparations, alternatives or retreat. Try "What risks can I foresee?", "What supplies do I have?", or "What does recovery currently do?" Hard Mode uses demanding opposition and a hard combat preset while preserving Glowhaven's configured nonpermanent knockout rules.

💀 Permadeath Mode.name: 💀 Permadeath Mode
💀 Permadeath Mode.description: Optional solo challenge: one life, no ordinary knockout return. The same world and normal enemy scaling, with final consequences for a genuine lethal defeat. Recommended for experienced players.
💀 Permadeath Mode.instructions:
## One life, chosen openly
This is an optional solo challenge. Do not impose it on a normal or multiplayer game. Preserve the world, selected start and established difficulty; permanent death is not a reason to invent stronger enemies, bad luck or compulsory misery.

## Lethal outcomes
For an actual lethal defeat, no routine knockout recovery or spontaneous resurrection follows. End the run with a brief meaningful epilogue about the people, promises and places the character affected. An actual nonlethal spar, consensual practice, ordinary sleep or an explicit nonlethal capture is not a death. Zero Mana or Stamina is never itself death. Do not invent a lethal result contrary to Combat Results.

## Fair warning and agency
Let people assess visible danger, prepare, hire help, avoid an offer or retreat when physically possible. Keep existing surprise events and their real rules. Do not turn every setback into death or prescribe the player's courage, sacrifice or final words. Companions retain their motives and can aid a real withdrawal; no automatic abandonment or suicidal loyalty.

## Scope
While active in an actual solo run, these final-outcome instructions take precedence over ordinary knockout narration. Do not apply them to other players or another mode. An irreversible fictional outcome does not authorize changing a supplied mechanical result.
💀 Permadeath Mode.npcIntentInstructions: Use the actual abilities and action budget. Allies act usefully while the player fights, and an agreed retreat is coordinated rather than treated as cowardice. Enemies do not gain free moves or knowledge. Noncombatants and exhausted people have limits. No supplied miss becomes a hit for dramatic finality.
💀 Permadeath Mode.askTheNarratorPrompt: One life. Ask about visible danger, your actual condition and possible exits. I will not reveal hidden facts or change a resolved result. This challenge is intended for solo play.

authorSeeds.What They Want Today:
You show characters through a concrete present want that belongs to their actual role.
You focus on what they are doing to obtain it, even when the player never intervenes.
You include a small preference that makes the desire personal rather than a quest notice.
You create characters who can be satisfied, disappointed, distracted or willing to change their plan.
You reveal character through a choice the player could actually witness, without inventing a deadline or crisis.
authorSeeds.A Bond With Weight:
You show characters through how they treat one relationship already supported by their context.
You focus on the particular favor, irritation, shared activity or obligation that gives it texture.
You include disagreement without assuming hatred and affection without assuming romance.
You create characters with lives outside the player and room to refuse company.
You reveal character through a small exchange; do not invent a reciprocal bond with a named person.
authorSeeds.Pride in the Work:
You show characters through what they insist on doing well in their actual work or learned method.
You focus on a visible standard: a clean join, a clear explanation, a fair count or a controlled strike.
You include the pleasure or irritation of seeing that standard met or ignored.
You create characters whose expertise can coexist with laziness, vanity, bluntness or poor teaching.
You reveal character through practiced habits rather than granting extraordinary competence.
authorSeeds.Small Private Pleasures:
You show characters through an ordinary pleasure they make time for.
You focus on its tangible detail: the texture of bread, an absurd song, warm water or a familiar game.
You include a preference they might share, defend, spend money on or keep to themselves.
You create characters whose harmless enjoyment does not need a tragic explanation or secret power.
You reveal character through how they behave when someone interrupts or unexpectedly understands the pleasure.
authorSeeds.A Flaw That Costs:
You show characters through a real flaw that changes how they handle an ordinary situation.
You focus on the excuse they make, the opportunity they miss or the inconvenience somebody else bears.
You include selfishness, foolishness or cruelty honestly when it belongs to the character.
You create characters who are not automatically redeemed by competence, attractiveness or a sad past.
You reveal character through specific conduct rather than treating every unpleasant person as secretly kind.
authorSeeds.The Face of Authority:
You show characters through the way they use the actual responsibility or leverage they possess.
You focus on a particular decision, service or boundary rather than a vague aura of importance.
You include how their manner changes with colleagues, petitioners and people beyond their authority.
You create characters who may be fair, petty, patient or self-serving without becoming omniscient.
You reveal character through what they permit, explain or refuse; do not enlarge their office or invent a title.
authorSeeds.Someone Who Acts First:
You show characters through a small initiative they take for their own reason.
You focus on a useful action, awkward invitation, competitive gesture or attempt to avoid work.
You include room for the other person to accept, refuse or misunderstand.
You create characters who can start an interaction without waiting to dispense a quest.
You reveal character through their next practical move without deciding the player’s response.
authorSeeds.Comedy of Conviction:
You show characters through something they take more seriously than the surrounding people do.
You focus on timing, confident mistakes and the friction between their expectation and the actual situation.
You include a concrete habit or line of reasoning that can be funny without a narrator explaining the joke.
You create characters who retain their real competence and flaws when the joke is over.
You reveal character through the cost of their conviction; do not turn every voice into a quip or repeated catchphrase.
authorSeeds.An Ordinary Life:
You show characters through a life they find worthwhile without fame or exceptional destiny.
You focus on work, friendships, meals, rest and one practical thing that would improve the week.
You include a pleasure or annoyance that can matter without becoming a major plot.
You create characters who may be capable and powerful while still wanting an ordinary evening.
You reveal character through routine choices rather than a concealed bloodline, conspiracy or mandatory tragedy.
authorSeeds.A Comfortable Contradiction:
You show characters through one contrast that grows naturally from their actual identity.
You focus on the situations in which each side becomes visible: stern and easily flustered, brilliant and indolent, elegant and impatient.
You include a detail that makes both sides believable rather than announcing an archetype label.
You create characters who can contradict local expectations without representing an entire people or academy.
You reveal character through a change of context; do not add a second personality, false identity or secret villain by default.
authorSeeds.The Learned Hand:
You show characters through their individual use of a genuinely learned skill or physical method.
You focus on stance, preparation, tools, casting habit or the particular errors they notice.
You include one competent application appropriate to the established role and power.
You create characters whose affinity, teaching subject, profession and delivery method are separate facts.
You reveal character through technique and judgment, not a new affinity, ultimate ability or inflated level.
authorSeeds.Courtesy With Teeth:
You show characters through what polite language allows them to express or conceal.
You focus on the meaningful difference between a warm welcome, a formal refusal and a carefully delivered insult.
You include plain intent beneath the manner so the reader can understand what is wanted.
You create characters who can set limits without becoming an unhelpful riddle or endless gatekeeper.
You reveal character through whom they put at ease, keep at a distance or choose to challenge.
authorSeeds.Ambition Without Apology:
You show characters through a specific advantage they want: recognition, money, a better post or victory.
You focus on the method they actually use and the cost they are willing to impose.
You include a line they will cross, or one they refuse to cross, only when that suits the individual.
You create characters whose selfish goals need not conceal a noble cause.
You reveal character through their response to competition without inventing control over a faction or the player.
authorSeeds.Care in Particulars:
You show characters through attention to a particular person, creature, craft or responsibility.
You focus on a remembered preference, practical adjustment or small effort that actually helps.
You include limits: kindness can coexist with impatience, favoritism, fatigue or the need to be left alone.
You create characters whose care is not automatic attraction, obedience, party membership or universal self-sacrifice.
You reveal character through what they notice and choose to do, leaving others their own responses.
authorSeeds.A Different Worldview:
You show characters through a particular experience or body that makes an ordinary situation look different to them.
You focus on an actual custom, sense, lifespan, trained interest or physical need already supported by the context.
You include a concrete point of curiosity, amusement or misunderstanding without making the individual a spokesperson for their species.
You create creatures and people whose motives fit their real intelligence and anatomy.
You reveal character through practical perception; do not invent a homeland, species power or human romance for a nonhumanoid.
authorSeeds.Under Pressure:
You show characters through the difference between their settled manner and an actual difficulty.
You focus on what they protect, abandon, delegate, attack or ask for when the situation changes.
You include an imperfect but understandable response grounded in their real resources and experience.
You create characters who may panic, become precise, grow petty or cooperate without losing their established identity.
You reveal character through a bounded decision; do not invent a catastrophe, guaranteed victory or secret transformation.

encounterElements.Ordinary Life: A meal, shared table, working shift, purchase, hobby or comfortable silence can carry a scene. Use actual local people. Do not force a complication when the player chose peace.
encounterElements.Academy Life: Use the actual year, subject, teacher and current activity: a lesson, practice, club interest, assessment, rivalry or social invitation. Academy culture is not a personality requirement.
encounterElements.Comic Mismatch: Clashing priorities, overconfidence, evasive laziness, literal answers or badly timed enthusiasm can be funny through consequences. Do not explain the joke or make every serious person a comedian.
encounterElements.Friendship and Acquaintance: A manageable group doing something specific, a shared preference or small favor. Meeting is not recruitment, and kindness is not automatic attraction.
encounterElements.Chosen Romance: Use real interest, history, boundaries and the person's own style. Give an opportunity, not a compulsory confession or another romantic score.
encounterElements.Work and Commerce: A real buyer, service, quote, delivery, repair or commission with ownership, payment and scope. Browsing is not buying, and practice does not spontaneously pay wages.
encounterElements.Craft and Research: A practical question, actual materials and a bounded test. A failed experiment can teach a correction; it need not create an anomaly or a permanent ability.
encounterElements.Local Exploration: An observable detail, reachable side space or route choice within the current site. A scenery word never relocates the party to a distant similarly named place.
encounterElements.Creature Ecology: A specific local animal or creature behaves from its type, needs and habitat. Track a recurring individual. A type catalogue is not a spawn or loot schedule.
encounterElements.Combat and Escape: An actual motive, telegraphed danger, positions and counterplay. Allies aid their side; enemies can retreat or surrender. Use real power bands and supported action outcomes.
encounterElements.Sport and Friendly Practice: Scoring, technique, restraint and rivalry without assumed lethal intent. Losing can be embarrassing or instructive without killing the partner.
encounterElements.Public Duty and Law: An actual service, complaint, investigation, hearing or security situation under the appropriate authority. Evidence and proportional consequences matter; no omniscient guards.
encounterElements.Custom and Celebration: An established festival, performance, remembrance or local custom. Residents participate differently. Do not invent a world-wide holiday from an ordinary celebration.
encounterElements.Continuing Consequence: Develop a real earlier choice, commitment, loss or changed relationship. Preserve settled work and closed accounts; do not reset or repeatedly re-offer it.
encounterElements.Dungeon Groups: In a dungeon realm, draw on its actual finite roster and ecology: a two-to-four-enemy patrol, guarded choke point, nest with a flanker, or boss with distinct retainers. Use each real NPC’s health, tier and actions; an ingredient is not a spawn instruction. Preserve cleared routes and retreat. Do not apply dungeon combat density to an ordinary city or quiet scene.

characterArchetypes.Earnest Striver:

Drives: improve at something specific without being dismissed.
Traits: persistent, proud of small progress, sometimes overdoes it.
Morality: effort matters; may mistake exhaustion for virtue.
Relationships: admires a real mentor; can envy an easier success. Use actual canonical people only when the connection is supported.

locationArchetypes.Everyday Service:
Apply only if compatible with the actual parent location and current task. Preserve existing rooms, routes, images, coordinates and permissions.
A real counter, workshop, office or food business with a usable service, clear terms and responsible staff. Ordinary successful business can end normally. A shortage or dispute is optional, not a compulsory conspiracy.
locationArchetypes.Shared Study and Practice:
Apply only if compatible with the actual parent location and current task. Preserve existing rooms, routes, images, coordinates and permissions.
Readable working space, actual materials and room for a lesson or solo practice. Learners vary in ability and motivation. Expertise follows the actual teacher, not the school color or innate affinity.
locationArchetypes.Competitive Venue:
Apply only if compatible with the actual parent location and current task. Preserve existing rooms, routes, images, coordinates and permissions.
A defined contest, usable floor or field, spectators where appropriate, scoring and limits. Public access and backstage access differ. A friendly contest does not silently become lethal combat.
locationArchetypes.Quiet Social Place:
Apply only if compatible with the actual parent location and current task. Preserve existing rooms, routes, images, coordinates and permissions.
Seating, a characteristic sound or smell and space for privacy or ordinary conversation. Staff have work; visitors need not become a party. A peaceful visit need not reveal a mystery.
locationArchetypes.Working Institution:
Apply only if compatible with the actual parent location and current task. Preserve existing rooms, routes, images, coordinates and permissions.
Public approach, actual service area, records or workspaces and bounded authority. Private offices and quarters remain behind real access. Procedure can resolve a request instead of endlessly delaying it.
locationArchetypes.Home and Lodging:
Apply only if compatible with the actual parent location and current task. Preserve existing rooms, routes, images, coordinates and permissions.
A credible place to sleep, cook, store belongings and spend private time at its actual scale. Ownership, rent, guests and permission are specific. Never relocate someone's bedroom into a different business.
locationArchetypes.Public Gathering:
Apply only if compatible with the actual parent location and current task. Preserve existing rooms, routes, images, coordinates and permissions.
A square, market, performance or festival with multiple ordinary uses and manageable foreground cast. Let people have different priorities. No automatic riot, cult, thief or forced quest.
locationArchetypes.Craft and Industry:
Apply only if compatible with the actual parent location and current task. Preserve existing rooms, routes, images, coordinates and permissions.
Materials, workflow, tools, workers and an actual product or repair. Noise, heat and access follow the craft. Critical work stays within real competence and the existing equipment scale.
locationArchetypes.Sacred and Remembered Place:
Apply only if compatible with the actual parent location and current task. Preserve existing rooms, routes, images, coordinates and permissions.
Actual local belief, remembrance or history expressed in physical use. Ordinary sincere practice and disagreement can coexist. No invented god, curse, required miracle or hidden faction.
locationArchetypes.Outer Route and Field Site:
Atmosphere:
- A workable approach borders terrain that is not maintained for visitors.
- Sounds, spoor, weather and disturbed ground reveal what uses the place.
Tensions:
- Safe collection margins differ from occupied hunting or nesting ground.
- A survey, crossing or retrieval has an objective beyond killing everything.
Patterns:
- Use the actual habitat's npcTypes and local band; woodland may hold Wild Predator or Stonehide Boar, while sky woods use their established local species.
- Establish a finite present individual or group when the party actually reaches its occupied area, not endless warning signs.
Secrets:
- Cover, a feeding route or a dry ledge can provide a real bypass when the layout supports one. Cleared danger stays resolved.
locationArchetypes.Restricted or Dangerous Site:
Atmosphere:
- The real boundary is legible: a guarded threshold, webbed nest, broken mechanism or dangerous working floor.
Tensions:
- Entry may provoke its actual defender or expose an environmental hazard; a locked record room is not automatically a monster lair.
Patterns:
- Use site-specific occupants and motives: Arachne or Giant Spider at established web nests, Rune Sentinel at a supported guarded installation, actual officers at a prison.
- Keep an approach, occupied focal area and plausible retreat. Do not infer hostility merely from a generated NPC's level.
Secrets:
- A defender may be guarding offspring, a mechanism or a route rather than pursuing everyone forever. Existing authored bosses and finite dungeon packs take precedence; do not duplicate them.
locationArchetypes.Transit and Receiving Space:
Apply only if compatible with the actual parent location and current task. Preserve existing rooms, routes, images, coordinates and permissions.
A real approach, waiting/working space and the actual transport connection. Arrival stops at the supported endpoint. A portal is an authored facility, never a template-generated shortcut.
locationArchetypes.Hunted Ground:
Atmosphere:
- This space is used by predators: dragged prey, broken cover and interrupted animal calls matter.
Tensions:
- Looking from the margin is different from entering a feeding lane or defending a trapped traveler.
Patterns:
- A wolf group, a stalking Ribbonjaw Prowler or a territorial Stonehide Boar uses an appropriate actual habitat, not every woodland at once.
- Give the individual an approach, motive and real position; group enemies have separate identities and turns unless the type is a genuine swarm.
Secrets:
- An open sightline, noise, food diversion or another route may change the encounter. A defeated or diverted animal is not replaced immediately.
locationArchetypes.Guardians Without Masters:
Atmosphere:
- An abandoned installation still has a narrow function: protect a chamber, maintain a boundary or move material.
Tensions:
- Intruders can activate a real surviving mechanism without turning every ruin into a world-threatening plot.
Patterns:
- Use an actually supported Rune Sentinel, Metal Automaton, Clockwork Beast or existing custom guardian. Read its command, sensing limit and physical reach.
- A present guardian becomes a real encounter, not a decorative silhouette that never acts.
Secrets:
- A control point, interrupted power path or valid bypass can matter as much as damage. Do not restore destroyed defenses on the next visit.
locationArchetypes.The Ground Will Not Hold:
Atmosphere:
- Unstable snow, thin ice, flooded stone, rotten supports or exposed sky ledges create specific physical risk.
Tensions:
- Reaching the objective needs a suitable method; an environmental threat does not require a monster behind it.
Patterns:
- Show the actual hazard before commitment where perception permits, then resolve the chosen crossing, climb, brace or retreat.

Beyond Glowhaven: An Authorized Expediti.questDesignBrief:
This is a chosen educational assignment for actual student participants, not forced enrollment or a task accepted by proximity. Establish the academy, actual authorizing official or order, purpose, route/site, supervisor, participants, permissions, success criteria and safe turnaround. Use existing people and known locations. Phoenix Wing can assess a protective risk; Hydra Head can coordinate a community or supply need; Gryffin Tail can survey a phenomenon; Dragon Hoard can document or carefully assess a relic-bearing site. Do not invent a unique relic, compulsory fight, new named official, salvage code, or fixed administrative delegation. Scope can be low-risk, and lawful documentation can be a valid result. The Great Sage need not personally accompany anyone. No progress is credited for hypothetical outcomes, private travel, accepting another job, an absent participant's achievement, or a visitor merely being present. The persistent party ledger records the actual assignment scenes, not an individual graduation registry. Local Glowhaven countryside, Wraith Island and its prison never satisfy this distant-regional requirement. The current eligible maps are Drakenspire Mountains and Asterveil Sky Archipelago. Portal arrival itself is not fieldwork. Arrange the return and debrief without inventing an official or awarding credit for an absent student. The First Regional Field Examination and Silver Threads Below use separate records. Do not duplicate either as this generic assignment.

Academic storyline: this remains an independent authorized expedition that can be undertaken when genuinely assigned. At the expedition milestone, choose an accessible Drakenspire or Asterveil assignment, an actual appropriate professor/supervisor and two or three willing classmates if desired. Give the field stage a real reachable obstacle, creature, terrain or experiment, not only travel and a report. Use existing local work when its actual scope matches, preserving its separate payment. Court keys and local permission remain required. The level-twenty field test and its cancellation do not pass this expedition; the optional spider investigation and queen victory are not prerequisites. Earlier genuinely qualifying work can be recognized by the responsible supervisor without replay or duplicate pay. No automatic party recruitment or whole cohort is imposed.

Silver Threads Below.questDesignBrief: An optional first-arrival investigation, independent of academy enrollment, field tests and expedition credit. Follow four fixed chambers in order: Silken Portal Room, Threadfall Galleries, Sunken Broodworks, Widow’s Crucible. Earn the first lower passage by resolving the bridge or a viable alternative; earn the second by securing the broodworks and opening or safely bypassing the matron’s lattice. Relevant combat, skilled movement, tools, study or credible negotiation can work; no affinity or universal kill requirement is imposed. Use the finite type-based Giant Spider and Arachne encounter groups, their existing types, and the two named crucible retainers; preserve every actual identity and outcome. The sole boss is the authored hostile Vhalessra, fixed level 45. Her native defeat or genuine surrender awards Matron’s Anchor Sigil once through its existing trigger. Immediate retreat and cleared-route backtracking remain available. An actual received report to Mihoshi Kagamihara completes the case; the boss is not a field examination or the separate authorized expedition. Discovery at level 20 is not a recommendation to fight the queen alone. Telegraph the substantially stronger level-45 boss and her two retainers. Retreat, preparation, bringing a party and returning later remain legitimate; no instant mission failure for leaving.

A Measure of Polish.name: A Measure of Polish
A Measure of Polish.questStatement: Ryūka Marufuji questions how much of a reputation survives a proper demonstration.
A Measure of Polish.mainObjective: If you accept, agree a fair activity with Ryūka Marufuji, carry it out and answer her invitation on your own terms.
A Measure of Polish.questDesignBrief:
One optional rivalry encounter, not a forced duel. The bazaar introduction appears once after the actual Silken victory and held sigil. The item times the encounter; Ryūka Marufuji cannot read inventory or know its history unless it is revealed or credibly explained. Prior acquaintance, dislike, friendship and party membership all persist. She wants attention and a convincing display of her own preparation, and can be insulting or classist rather than secretly gracious in every outcome.
If accepted, agree a bounded activity: controlled wand or weapon practice, moving targets, examining an agreed nonhazardous item, or a practical contribution suited to a scholar, trader, artisan or noncaster. Owning or showing the trophy is not required after the introduction. Establish any necessary visitor permission and supervision; she cannot overrule faculty. Use Dragon Hoard Academy - Training Court for safe practice or Exhibition Hall for a display. No compulsory equalization, secret handicap or level scaling: her real level is 15 and a stronger player can win easily. A powerful player’s restraint must be voluntary. Fair loss, fair win, useful cooperation and an honest unsuccessful attempt can all conclude the session; choosing to leave is allowed.
Render actual attempts and results. Her reaction depends on how the player treats her, not a scripted victory. Banter can stay platonic, and humiliation can damage trust. When the chosen session and its immediate exchange finish, complete this small quest. No need for an apology, kiss, trophy handover or recruitment. An actual later personal invitation can open You Could Have Asked; completion alone does not make her romantically interested. A declined offer remains declined, not another mandatory pursuit.

session.text: Carry out the agreed session and conclude the exchange.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: Conclude the actual session with Ryūka Marufuji: retain its method, outcome and response. Award the typed 400 XP once. No fixed relationship increase, romance, spell, extra money or party membership. She can be pleased, annoyed or embarrassed according to events. Further invitations need real willingness.

You Could Have Asked.name: You Could Have Asked
You Could Have Asked.questStatement: Ryūka Marufuji has a carefully prepared spare invitation to a small student exhibition.
You Could Have Asked.mainObjective: Choose a role in the exhibition, resolve its unfair allocation of credit, and give an honest answer about future company.
You Could Have Asked.questDesignBrief:
An optional continuation after A Measure of Polish, offered only through Ryūka Marufuji’s actual invitation. No date, friendship or attraction is presumed. The player may accept as a rival, friend, professional collaborator, spectator or mutually interested adult. Declining ends the offer without compulsory pursuit. Arrange a small faculty-approved display in the existing Exhibition Hall; this is not an unscheduled citywide festival. Nonstudent visitors need ordinary legitimate access, not forced enrollment.
Her household contributes ordinary materials. She uses that contribution to claim the best placement and omit Mai Kajiwara’s genuinely agreed paid technical work from the credit. Establish the actual work/consent before the dispute; Mai Kajiwara is neither her servant nor a free repair resource. Avoid summoning the whole cast. Noriaki Takatsuki or Miyu Asahina can address a real dispute within their actual roles if contacted; they are not automatically complicit.
Prepare an agreed role, then expose the concrete unfair allocation through the actual program and contributors. The player can support a correction, negotiate, refuse involvement or knowingly benefit from favoritism. Each is playable; concealment does not secretly count as justice. Ryūka Marufuji must make her own response: repair, partial repair or refusal. Her original pride and sharpness persist. Complete the actual display, or a genuinely decided cancellation, with its real consequences. No endless replacement paperwork or mandatory public apology.
Afterward allow a private conversation or a clear refusal to have one. If trust and interest support it, she can admit wanting the player’s company and ask for another meeting. A rival’s rematch, friendship, mutual adult romance, complicity, distance or unresolved estrangement are all legitimate conclusions. The player’s clear answer closes the episode; do not require forgiveness or consolation. Remember witnessed harm and boundaries. Rewards are only the fixed completion XP and actual opportunities, never purchased affection or a free technique.

answer.text: Conclude the exhibition episode and answer any further invitation honestly.

onCompleteEffects.instruction: Close You Could Have Asked using the actual credit decision, exhibition outcome and final answer. Pay only the typed 650 XP once. Preserve repair, complicity, refusal, friendship or mutual interest as played. No forced confession, kiss, forgiveness, new spell, automatic recruitment or reset of Ryūka Marufuji’s personality. The same invitation and apology do not restart.

Let the applicant use their real trained weapon, body technique, magic or mixed method in a bounded safe exercise; no universal Intelligence test or compulsory spell. A real check and the supplied outcome determine practical success. A capable newcomer may demonstrate competence promptly; failing is a reason to practice, not humiliation or arbitrary detention. Komugi Hanabishi handles the docket and certification; an appropriate duty assessor may supervise practical work. Personal pass records and the actual issuance trigger control the badge. No starting badge, free weapon, portal key or automatic pass from level. Registration/assessment adds no invented charge. Applicants can postpone or leave.
The certification trigger exclusively awards the existing Document Guild Badge: Bronze. Do not also put a badge in generated quest rewards or create a renamed Relic for the same licence.

The judgment review uses a clearly labeled sample scenario, not a live request from the board. Its fictional client, terms and place do not become a quest, appointment or map destination. State the short example fully and recognize a natural answer that shows scope, ownership and sensible withdrawal; do not demand a repeated three-part recitation after understanding has been demonstrated. The practical is an onsite controlled exercise, not a commissioned repair, delivery or monster hunt. Only the existing licensure quest tracks the exam. Offer real contracts separately after actual licensing or an actual later request.

practical.text: Complete a controlled practical demonstration with your trained method.

certify.text: Have the completed results certified at reception.

Your First Spell.mainObjective: Create and safely demonstrate one simple original spell using Spellcraft.
Your First Spell.questDesignBrief:
An optional beginner experiment, available independently of school enrollment. Let the player choose a useful purpose and a discipline they actually know: a small light, a shaped breeze, a precise arcane nudge or another modest working. These are examples, not prescribed spells. A noncaster can postpone it or seek basic instruction; this goal does not teach a discipline or demand that a martial character become a mage.
Use an actual Spellcraft check to design or substantially adapt the blueprint. Then resolve a safe test with its actual discipline, effects and costs. A simple experiment can take one short scene; failed attempts invite a small revision, not a mandatory multi-session research project. Require a real successful design and a repeatable supported result, not just a name, promise, teacher demonstration or preexisting ability. Let the player name the spell, or offer a few vivid names after its function is known.
Use the normal learned-ability workflow to record the personal technique when eligible. A real cooldown may delay its card without undoing an already successful experiment. Do not grant free levels, an extra ability point or an unrelated spell. A teacher may be an existing academy professor or another genuinely qualified person; enrollment and paid instruction follow their actual circumstances. This experiment is not a second compulsory first-day class. If the same design also genuinely satisfies an accepted academy project, acknowledge the work rather than demanding a duplicate invention; preserve that project's own acceptance and requirements.
